News.title: Wild moment barmy beachgoer tries to out-swim massive tuna chasing him through shallow water off Spanish holiday shore
News.content:
THIS is the moment a bonkers beachgoer attempted to out-swim a giant tuna in a wild chase at a Brit holiday hotspot.

Crazy footage shows the massive fish with a large fin appearing in hot pursuit of the tourist at a Spanish holiday resort.



The man desperately attempted to reach the safety of shore line before the fish – which he thought was a shark – reached him.

Onlookers ran along the waters edge where the “chase” was unfolding to try and aid the swimmer.



When the man finally made it from danger, the large fish began flopping furiously in the shallows in front of baffled onlookers.

The monster sea creature turned out to be a giant 295kg tuna.

The jaw-dropping scenes occurred at Ancon Beach on Marbella’s so-called Golden Mile, near to a famous bar and restaurant called Victor’s Beach.

The sea turned red as the tuna bled from its gills following a previous scrape.



It is thought to have ended up in trouble after been injured by fishing gear or a jet-ski causing it to move around violently in the water.

Once it became clear it was harmless and in difficulties, hero beachgoers helped it return to deeper water using sun beds and deck chairs to push it back out.

The nationality of the unlucky swimmer was not immediately clear this morning.



Camilo Orosa, a Marbella-based local commenting on the scenes, said: “My God, if it were me, I would already have s**t my pants, or rather my swimming trunks.”

Another social media user added: “If I was that swimmer I would have died from a heart attack. It looks like a shark.”

He added, referencing the classic 1975 thriller by Steven Spielberg: “All that was missing was the music from Jaws.”

Jade Bloomberg, a British expat, said: “It was in so much distress, I went into the water to see if it was tangled in a net or if it had something inside but nothing.

“It was huge, so beautiful.”



Another social media user said: “That poor tuna must have had some kind of collision with a jet ski or something similar.

“Tuna being around is normal and they tend to stay close to the coast. Sometimes they get mistaken for dolphins.”

News.title: Moment women throw punches in shocking broad daylight brawl after row in McDonald’s spills onto street – as 3 arrested
News.content:
THIS is the moment three women brawl outside McDonald’s as a savage fight leaves stunned onlookers watching in disbelief.

The footage shows the trio grappling and wildly lashing out at each other as they tumble down a side road.



Shortly after the clip ends, a witness said one of those involved smashed a glass bottle which was used in the attack.

The chaos unfolded at around 6.10am on Sunday morning beside the fast food chain on Kingsland Road in Dalston, east London.



The fight had started inside the fast food restaurant before spilling outside, cops confirmed.

A group of clubbers grabbing food after their nights out were left stunned when the melee erupted.



A witness said one woman’s face appeared to have been badly cut and was gushing with blood after she was allegedly slashed.

They told The Sun: “There is always things kicking off down here, especially after nights out.



“God knows what started the argument but things got out of hand quick.

“They were all proper going for each other and one woman’s face was badly slashed up and she was bleeding quite badly.”

Cops scrambled to the scene alongside the Ambulance Service after reports of the fight.

Officers arrested three women, aged in their 30s, 40s and 50s, on suspicion of affray.

All three were taken to hospital for treatment as officers began investigating the brawl.



A cordon was put in place while officers carried out enquiries and spoke to witnesses.

The women in their 30s and 40s have since been discharged and remain in police custody.

The woman in her 50s suffered non-life-changing injuries and has not yet been discharged.

The Met said enquiries into the incident remain ongoing.

The Sun has approached McDonald’s for comment.

News.title: Teen girl, 17, ‘sexually assaulted’ by man at UK railway station as cops release CCTV
News.content:
STATION HORROR Teen girl, 17, ‘sexually assaulted’ by man at UK railway station as cops release CCTV

COPS have released images of a man they want to speak to after a 17-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted outside a train station.

The man approached the teen outside Coventry railway station at around 12.20am on Sunday July 12 and tried to kiss her, it is claimed.



After she told him no, the bloke sexually assaulted her, it is alleged.

One of the girl’s pals then challenged the man before he made a quick getaway from the area.



Detectives investigating the attack would like to speak to the man seen on CCTV images, as they think he might have information which could assist the probe.

Anyone who recognises him is urged to contact British Transport Police.



Text BTP on 61016, or call 0800 40 50 40, quoting reference 808 of 12 July.



Information can also be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: UK weather: All the UK areas expected to hit 35C this week as heatwave is set to return
News.content:
BRITS are bracing for their fifth heatwave of the year as temperatures are set to rise to 35C in a number of areas.

Amber heat health warnings are set to cover most of England throughout the week with more than 25million Brits underhosepipe ban restrictions.



Multiple locations across England are set to rise to 35C in the fifth heatwave of the year.

Parts of the West Midlands, East of England, the Thames Valley and the Home Counties are forecast to experience up to 35C at 4pm on Thursday, August 13.



Highs of up to 30C are expected across England and Wales on Tuesday, rising between 32C and 34C on Wednesday, and reaching 35C on Thursday.

Meanwhile parts of East Anglia and the South East of England are expected to be the warmest.



In response, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued an amber heat health warning for the entirety of England, excluding the North East.

The alert is set to stay in place between 9am on August 11 and 9pm on August 14, meaning the weather is likely to impact health and social care services.

This period of hot weather will become the fifth heatwave of the year, following record-breaking temperatures of 37.7C back in June.

It comes as England and the entirety of Wales remain in drought conditions, with another six currently facing “prolonged dry weather“.

News.title: ‘Not possible’ for Burnham to block early release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers despite fury, says Downing Street
News.content:
IT is “not possible” for Andy Burnham to block the release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers, Downing Street has said, despite growing anger around the early release scheme.

The government would reportedly face legal challenges if it tried to block the release of Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole halfway through their 13-year jail terms.



New PM Andy Burnham is reportedly opposed to the early release of the pair under Labour plans to let out up to 5,000 prisoners over ten months from October.

After stopping some 1,000 rapists and child sex offenders from being let loose onto the streets last week Mr Burnham said he had reached “the very limits of what is possible.”



A government source has since told The Times however that Mr Burnham is prepared “explore every option” to keep Bowers and Cole behind bars.

According to the publication, the government has already ruled out exempting the killers of emergency workers from early release.



The planned exemption is understood to have been described as a “complete non-starter.”

It was decided that the planned change to the scheme would be subject to a legal challenge.



And, because there is no specific offence of manslaughter of an emergency worker the case would be tough to win for the government.

Downing Street has since said that it is “not possible” to exempt “one or two offenders” convicted of manslaughter from early release.

Today, Mr Burnham’s official spokesman said manslaughter of an emergency worker was “not a standalone offence” and it was “not possible to simply exclude one or two offenders” within the wider category of manslaughter.

Asked whether ministers were accepting the situation as it stands, the spokesman said: “I think you’ve seen from the Prime Minister’s words that he’s far from accepting the situation and as he wrote last week he wants to go even further.

“He’s pushed hard on what more we could do and his focus now is on fixing the prison system long term to avoid a repeat of this prison crisis so that it never happens again.”



There are 950 prisoners serving sentences for manslaughter in the UK with hundreds of them set to be released under Labour’s scheme.

In another potential route to block the release of PC Harper’s killers, former detective superintendent at Thames Valley police, Stuart Blaik, suggested those more culpable under manslaughter laws be barred from the scheme.

Cases of manslaughter are categorised in three culpability ratings, A, B and C.



In response to the fury around the potential release of Bowers and Cole, Blaik suggested offenders in the two most severe categories of manslaughter be prevented from an early release.

But officials shot down this plan too, saying judges did not always include culpability ratings in their sentences – making it hard to determine who would be eligible for Labour’s early release scheme.

PC Harper’s family have expressed anger and disappointment at the decision not to exempt Cole and Bowers.

And, the boss of his former force said he was considering joining a potential legal challenge over the Government plans.

PC Harper’s furious widow Lissie Harper, 35, previously said it was “disgusting” that her late husband’s killers could get out early.



She said: “What abhorrent message does this send?

“How dare ministers say the killing of a police officer isn’t enough of a ‘sickening crime’ that deserves the stiffest of punishments.

“Andrew’s killers have shown no remorse. To release them early from their already pitiful sentences is an affront to justice.

“The Government and justice system have not just let me down, they have added insult to injury.

“This is an utter betrayal, one I will not be able to forgive or forget.”



Some 5,000 lags are expected to be released early under sentencing changes, down from 6,000 after the exemptions announced as part of an urgent review of the scheme designed to tackle jail overcrowding.

Under current plans, Cole and Bowers remain eligible to be freed in January, just halfway through their 13-year sentences.

In 2019 PC Harper, 28, was fatally dragged by a car driven by Henry Long, 18, as it towed a stolen quad bike.

Long, Bowers and Cole, then 17, were found guilty of manslaughter. The younger pair got 13 years’ jail, Long got 16 and will stay in prison.

Tiff Lynch, National Chair of the Police Federation of England and Wales, branded the pairs release as “deeply disappointing” and “impossible to justify”.



Freeing the two prisoners early “gravely risks undermining not only public safety but public confidence”, Lynch added.

The decision has also come under fire from Thames Valley Police Chief Constable Jason Hogg’s, who described the decision as “demoralising” for emergency service workers.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “The death of PC Andrew Harper was a horrific crime.

“Our thoughts are with his family and friends, and we share the anger from the police community that we are in this position.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We have been clear that we wanted to block more offenders from getting out sooner into their sentence but could not do so without risking prisons reaching capacity and collapsing.



“If that happened, police could not make arrests, courts could not remand offenders and there would be unchecked criminality on our streets.”

News.title: Brit ‘suitcase death’ victim’s final texts reveal mysterious late-night dash from flat: ‘What made her leave so late?’
News.content:
THE chilling final texts of a Brit aid worker reveal she was planning to make a late-night dash from her alleged killer’s flat, The Sun has learned.

Elisabeth Ross was found stuffed in a suitcase three days after she told Afghan migrant Sharif Ahmadzai and his wife that she was leaving the Athens flat owned by their charity.



Greek cops are now probing what made Elisabeth, 38, suddenly want to flee the apartment at nearly 10pm, a police source has said.

They told The Sun: “There could be motive here. Did he [Ahmadzai] perhaps lose it when he learned she was leaving?



“And what made her want to leave so late at night? They’re lines of inquiry that we are looking into.”

The last person Elisabeth texted was the son of a close friend who she had previously stayed with in Keratsini, southwest Athens.



She asked “whether it would be OK to return and spend a few days there again,” a police source said, “which was fine by him”.

The mum-of-three sent another WhatsApp message at 9.41pm, saying she would be on her way “within the next half hour”.



Three days later, a homeless man discovered her remains inside a suitcase dumped in a derelict building.

Police arrested Ahmadzai, 26, after his American wife, Alaina, provided crucial testimony and handed over evidence.

The part-time boxer is now holed up in a hellish Greek jail – the notorious Korydallos prison – packed to the rafters with terrorists, rapists and murderers.



He was formally charged with intentional homicide, robbery and possession of illegal weapons last Thursday.

Toxicology reports that will determine Elisabeth’s cause of death are expected to “take some time” due to a shortage of staff and lab space.

George Kalliakmanis, head of Greece‘s union of police officers, told The Sun: “They are not going to be released, as many think, this week.”

It comes after police sources revealed that Ahmadzai had undergone a sudden behaviour shift after the birth of his child.

Interviews with Alaina revealed that the suspect had “noticeably” changed in the months leading up to Elisabeth’s death.



She is said to be “revolted” by her husband and firmly believes that he killed her friend.

Kalliakmanis said: “Her testimony was very credible and very helpful.

“She’s in a state of confusion which is perfectly understandable after all she’s the mother of his child.”



Ahmadzai has denied killing Elisabeth, but admitted that he put her body in a suitcase and took it to the abandoned site.

The Afghan also confessed to withdrawing more than 10,000 euros with her credit cards.

Ahmadzai has insisted that she was dead when he found Elisabeth, known as Lisa, in the apartment’s bathroom.

He had keys to the flat because it was used as a regular meeting spot for Love Every Nation, the NGO that he set up with his wife.

Alaina grew suspicious of Ahmadzai in the fortnight between Lisa’s death and her identification.



The alleged killer attempted to gift her a new iPhone and €2,550 (around £2,200) in cash.

She refused the items and later handed them over to police.

On July 15, Alaina claimed in her testimony that she woke up and found her husband had left their home without any warning.

She said: “I checked his location on my cell phone. I saw that he was inside [Lisa’s rental] apartment on Rethymno Street.

“I was surprised because there was no particular reason for him to be there at that time.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ahmadzai told Alaina that he had been out at a bar, which she initially believed, but she later proved crucial in facilitating his arrest.

The alleged killer looks set to spend at least the next 18 months in Korydallos – which is said to be rife with disease – while he awaits trial.

News.title: Boy, 17, and two men, 21 and 23, killed in horror crash on rural road
News.content:
SMASH TRAGEDY Boy, 17, and two men, 21 and 23, killed in horror crash on rural road

A TEENAGE boy and two men have been killed in a horror crash on a rural road.

Cops scrambled to the scene in Rotheram, South Yorkshire at around 11.39pm on Saturday evening.

South Yorkshire Police said a grey Seat Cupra Leon was travelling towards Kilnhurst on Denaby Lane when it left the carriageway.

Emergency services raced to the scene of the crash but, despite their best efforts, a 17-year-old boy was pronounced dead at the scene.





Two men – aged 21 and 23 – were also tragically pronounced dead.

Their families have been informed and are being supported by officers, cops said.

Another 17-year-old boy was taken to hospital with minor injuries.

A spokesperson for South Yorkshire Police said: “An investigation is underway and we are now asking for anyone who witnessed the collision, or who may have dash cam footage that could assist with our enquiries, to come forward.

“If you can help, please report online or call 101, quoting incident number 1235 of 8 August 2026.”

News.title: Influencer Ash Trevino ‘had relationships with up to 75 hardened prisoners including murderers’ – as she admits fraud
News.content:
LIKES A BAD BOY Influencer Ash Trevino ‘had relationships with up to 75 hardened prisoners including murderers’ – as she admits fraud

AN INFLUENCER accused of having up to 75 relationships with murderers and criminals has been ordered to pay thousands amid fraud charges.

Ash Trevino, whose full name is Ashley Lopez-Trevino, 37, pleaded guilty to welfare fraud and the fraudulent securing of document execution on August 5.



Lopez-Trevino, from Texas, has previously been branded the “worst mum” on TikTok after ditching her receptionist role to rake in thousands of pounds by posting controversial content online.

She has repeatedly sparked controversy by discussing her preference for “inmate-hopping” – dating men who are in prison or have recently been released.



Lopez-Trevino has been relationships with up to 75 prisoners, court filings obtained exclusively by TMZ reveals.

Texas prosecutors alleged in the documents that Lopez-Trevino had relationships with approximately “50–75 inmates of the Texas Department of Criminal Justice”.



Some of the prisoners were behind bars for violent offences, including aggravated robbery and murder, prosecutors allege.

The alleged relationships were raised in documents connected to the fraud proceedings.



Lopez-Trevino did not plead guilty to any offence relating to those relationships.

As a result of entering her recent guilty plea, the mother of three was ordered to pay a whopping $16,799.95 in restitution to the state.

The social media star was also sentenced to complete two years of community supervision, 120 hours of community service, an anti-theft class, and financial counselling.



Prosecutors also criticised what they described as “panhandling” on TikTok.

They alleged Lopez-Trevino had requested financial contributions before disclosing health information concerning a dependant.

The filings also raised concerns over sexually explicit videos and livestreams allegedly posted by the influencer.

The plea comes after the influencer was initially arrested in Texas in December 2023 after police said she had active felony warrants.

She was booked into Ellis County Jail before being released on a $15,000 bond.



In livestream clips circulated following her release, the influencer said she had hired an attorney and planned to fight the charges.

But she was taken back into custody in March after prosecutors alleged she had breached her bail conditions.

They claimed she had consumed alcohol at a birthday party on one occasion and bought alcohol at a restaurant on another.

Her legal team denied at the time that she had violated the conditions of her release.

Under the resulting plea agreement, Lopez-Trevino must now complete two years of supervision and the other court-ordered requirements while repaying the money owed to the state.



Lopez-Trevino is famed for showcasing every part of her life – a decision which has caused outrage by many online.

She has previously admitted that her two teenage children were forced to leave school after they were ridiculed for their mother’s online antics.

Among her scandals have been failing to buy beds for her daughter despite splurging £1,500 on Louis Vuitton handbags, as well as marrying a prisoner, dumping him and then dating a 19-year-old.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

One of her biggest controversies was a live video on TikTok, where she admitted to being jealous of her daughter and late ex-husband’s relationship.

The mum revealed she had pulled her daughter’s hair as a child in a jealous rage.

News.title: Record 230 people cross Channel in one small boat
News.content:
There have been signs that smugglers are putting more and more people into each boat. In 2018, there was an average of seven people per boat - but last year, that had risen to 62.

On Tuesday, 173 migrants had to be rescued from a single boat, which caught fire.

However, the number of crossings overall is on course to be lower this year.

So far, the number of migrants who have made the crossing is down by 43%. The number of boats that have successfully crossed is down by 49%.

Last month, the Home Office recorded the lowest number of crossings in July since 2020.

Officials think this is partly because they have managed to disrupt the supply of small boats and engines to the people smugglers, with 1,100 seized since Labour came to power.

Officials claim that with the sophisticated surveillance and reconnaissance operation now operating over the Channel, "unintercepted" beach landings have ended.

All boats that make it across the halfway point in the Channel are met at sea by Border Force, which then brings the migrants safely ashore for processing.

There is still clear demand for the crossings as the number of people waiting in camps in northern France has not reduced. At the same time, weather conditions have not been significantly different this year.

Officials believe this shows their work to disrupt the smuggling gangs is beginning to show results. Despite this, concerns persist about the numbers still able to make it across the Channel.

News.title: 'Dust devil' spins through London park
News.content:
Footage captured in Greenwich park, south-east London, showed a small whirlwind, or dust devil, swirling around people on Sunday.

People were seen getting up from their picnics and screaming as the whirlwind moved through the park.

Dust devils are formed on warm, sunny days and are visible due to the dust or hay that they pick up and swirl around.

More on England weather.

News.title: Travelodge staff gave domestic abuser key to his victim's room
News.content:
Another woman, Jo from Leeds, contacted BBC News following coverage of the Maidenhead attack.

In July, she woke in her room to an unknown man standing at the end of her bed, and screamed for help.

"It was just horrible, it was horrendous. Terrifying. I was shaking so badly," she said.

Her friend who was staying in the room heard him say, "I'm sorry, they gave me this key," she said.

Jo considered staying elsewhere following the reports of the attack in 2022, but was reassured by Travelodge's chief executive Jo Boydell, who previously said: "The safety and security of customers in our hotels is extremely important and we want everyone to be safe, and feel safe, in our hotels."

Jo said: "What happened to us shouldn't have happened. And the assurances [Travelodge] gave are not accurate. The systems are failing."

In response, Travelodge said an investigation found "our updated room access security policies, which were in place at the time, were not correctly followed, which is not acceptable.

"We have retrained the hotel team on our current room security and check-in procedures."

Andy Smith, who has travelled the country with his band and stays in dozens of Travelodge hotels a year, said he had been given keys to other people's rooms recently.

"We went up to the room and there was a guy already asleep in there in a state of undress," he said.

It followed another incident about 18 months ago where another man had gained access to his room by telling reception staff he was checking in under a common name such as "Mr Smith", Andy Smith said.

"I think he just chanced it. Because my name's Smith, I think it's just the pure luck of it. I mean, why wouldn't anyone be asking for ID or anything, like a booking reference or an email address. It beggars belief."

Travelodge responded by saying "any case of an unauthorised person entering a guest's room is a significant cause for concern and we want to be clear that these incidents should not have happened".

News.title: Thames Water gave finance boss a £1m signing-on fee
News.content:
Thames Water paid its finance chief a Â£1m signing-on fee in July as the company struggles with a mountain of debt and faces temporary nationalisation.

Steve Buck joined the company in April 2025 but it is understood the seven-figure payment was not made until last month after the company had taken legal advice over its contractual obligations.

The existence of the payment, first reported by Sky News,, external was revealed in a letter from the Thames Water chairman to MPs on the Commons Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee.

In the letter,, external Sir Adrian Montague said he understood customers would see large payments to senior leaders as "unjust" but argued they were necessary to stop staff leaving.

The letter said: "The majority of the team were brought in recently to fix the problems the company faces and are not responsible for causing those problems.

"These talented and experienced individuals have opportunities for roles outside Thames Water and, in many cases, have been actively approached by other companies.

"These roles would be less in the public gaze, less difficult and more remunerative."

Sir Adrian described the payment to Buck as a "necessary incentive" and said the money had come from emergency funding provided by Thames Water's lenders.

He said the company is facing recruitment and retention difficulties and warned the problem would "persist" if it was nationalised or put into special administration.

Alistair Carmichael, Lib Dem MP and chair of the Environment Committee, said: "Money should be going into improving services, not remunerating already well-paid senior executives.

"The government were clear in the early days that they wanted this to stop. It is obvious that they have not succeeded in this. We need to hear now from them about what they intend to do about it."

The utility company owes roughly Â£20bn and has been working with creditors and government officials to find a way forward.

Failure to reach a deal could lead to Thames Water being forced into a "special administration regime", a form of temporary nationalisation intended to keep the business operating until a viable solution can be found.

This would see government-appointed officials temporarily running the company â including funding its operations and upgrading infrastructure as well as dealing with any outstanding debts following a restructuring of the business.

If the company was subsequently sold to a private buyer, the government would be able to recoup some taxpayer cash.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has previously said he would like to see "greater public control" of key water and energy utilities.

In the past year, Thames Water boss Chris Weston saw his pay increase 14% to Â£1.63m while other directors received bonuses totalling Â£4.1m.

Speaking on the BBC Big Boss interview late last month, Weston acknowledged there was anger about Thames Water pay, but argued that the company needed to be able attract "capable people to help turn this company around".

"If we're not prepared to pay market rates, then they won't come to us and they won't stay with us," he said.

News.title: Ex-Cambridge professor Jason Arday cancels live event after plagiarism row
News.content:
Jason Arday has cancelled an appearance in London next month, following his resignation as a Cambridge professor in the wake of allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements.

Arday's talk at the Royal Geographical Society's conference has been "cancelled at the request of the speaker", the organisation said.

He is also no longer listed on the websites of two other scheduled events in the coming months.

Arday - who became Cambridge's youngest ever black professor in 2023 - has admitted errors in his early work, but said he was not a "liar" and that the recent furore had led to "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack".

He had been due to take part in a "fireside chat" at the Royal Geographical Society's conference in London on 2 September.

Arday's appearance at Topping & Company book shop in Edinburgh on 18 September is no longer listed on the website and has reportedly also been cancelled. The shop declined to comment.

He was also announced as a guest for the Arizona Women's Board Authors' Luncheon on 24 October, but is no longer listed on the event's website.

He is still listed as a speaker for the Stroud Book Festival in Gloucestershire in November.

News.title: Fifa and Infantino accused of 'deception' in open letter from football confederations
News.content:
Fifa and its president Gianni Infantino have been accused of breaking trust "through deception" in an open letter issued by Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation.

The letter, signed by the presidents and general secretaries of the three regional governing bodies, said recent controversy over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was fundamentally about "the integrity of the game, and the integrity of those elected to lead it".

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including the World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

It was aborted after widespread criticism from several confederations, led by Uefa which has threatened a boycott of all Fifa competitions.

BBC Sport understands that there have been preliminary discussions between the three confederations over breakaway competitions - should Infantino remain in situ.

"When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned," the letter read.

It added: "Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding - or demanding - power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it."

While the statement did not name Infantino, sources have told BBC Sport that it should be seen as an opportunity for him to resign and leave his position with dignity.

It comes after Fifa issued a statement on Saturday evening which strongly criticised a "concerted and ongoing effort" to "undermine" the organisation and Infantino.

News.title: British couple held in Iran end hunger strike
News.content:
A British couple jailed in Iran after being accused of espionage have ended their hunger strikes after 93 and 84 days respectively.

Craig and Lindsay Foreman were arrested in January 2025 while passing through Iran on a motorcycle journey from Europe to Australia. They were both sentenced to 10 years in jail in February, but Craig Foreman's family said his punishment had been extended by two years after speaking to the media.

The couple from East Sussex, who both deny espionage, went on hunger strike in May when prison authorities prevented them from calling their families.

The family of the couple said they had been protesting against how they and other prisoners were being treated.

Five people outside the prison joined the pair on their hunger strike for the final five days as an act of solidarity, the family added.

The fast ran from Tuesday to Saturday with Lindsay Foreman's son Joe Bennett and four unnamed others taking part in the UK, as well as other prisoners inside Tehran's Evin jail, the family said.

"My mum and Craig have spent months on hunger strike, and even at the point of bringing it to an end they wanted to make it about something bigger than themselves," Bennett, from Folkestone in Kent, said.

"Those final five days became about people standing together around values that should be universal: Truth, justice, kindness, peace and unity."

By the end of the protest, Craig Foreman had been on hunger strike for 93 days, and Lindsay Foreman for 84 days, the family added.

Although they said they were unaware of the condition of the pair, who had consumed just milk and either honey or salt in water during their strikes.

Bennett said the couple also went on a seperate hunger striker back in November as a "cry out for help".

News.title: Asylum seeker who groomed and raped girl, 13, jailed
News.content:
An asylum seeker who raped a 13-year-old girl after pretending to be a teenager on Snapchat has been jailed.

Abdul Khan attacked the girl in a nature reserve in Clifton, Nottingham, on 14 May last year.

Khan arrived in the UK in a back of a lorry in 2015, Nottingham Crown Court heard, and faces automatic deportation to Afghanistan after he has served two thirds of his sentence.

He was jailed for nine and a half years on Monday after he was convicted of two counts of rape, one count of sexual activity with a child, sexual communication with a child, meeting a child following grooming and perverting the course of justice.

A four-day trial was told Khan, who is believed to be 28, arranged to meet his victim in woodland after telling her he was a 14-year-old boy.

When they met in person and it was clear he was not 14, he tried to appease her by claiming to be 16, the court heard.

After activity that jurors found had been consensual, Khan twice raped the girl.

News.title: Ban on 'subscription traps' brought forward by three months
News.content:
Subscriptions will be easier to cancel and companies will be compelled to make it clear when contracts auto-renew at a higher price, Andy Burnham has announced.

The prime minister is also planning to outlaw shops from falsely claiming products previously retailed at much higher prices to advertise supposed deals, which he said tricks shoppers into thinking they are getting better value on purchases.

Burnham will bring forward a package of changes announced under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer to end so-called subscription traps and a crackdown on "pretend prices".

Shadow chancellor Mel Stride branded the measures "reheated" and said the prime minister "has already run out of ideas".

The plans were announced under Sir Keir in April, but are being brought forward by Burnham's government in a bid to give families "room to breathe" amid the high cost of living.

On subscriptions, the government said the changes will mean businesses have "to provide clearer up-front information, regular reminders and a much easier exit to contracts" for customers.

Burnham, who is embarking on a tour of the UK while Parliament is in recess, has promised a series of "everyday fixes" to help people with the cost of living.

He said: "I'm determined to pull every single lever we can to provide people with some room to breathe on the cost of living."

The measures being brought forward are aimed at making it easier for consumers to cancel unwanted subscriptions and stopping people being rolled onto expensive contracts without their knowledge.

They were expected to come into force next spring, but Burnham's government has promised they will now be implemented by January 2027.

When they were announced in April, the government said the plans would save consumers Â£400m a year in total, or up to Â£170 per person.

At the time, the Department for Business and Trade said there are 10 million unwanted, active subscriptions across the UK.

It said that more than 3.5 million people are being "quietly rolled from free or discounted trials into fully costed contracts", while another 1.3 million are caught out by unexpected auto-renewals.

On top of the already planned changes, Burnham is also vowing to end shops' use of "pretend prices". This will stop retailers using "was" prices, made-up discounts or misleading recommended retail prices (RRPs) to highlight deals.

The government will launch a consultation this autumn to decide how the new measures should be implemented.

News.title: Radio Caroline breached Ofcom rules after mistakenly announcing King's death
News.content:
Radio Caroline has been found in breach of broadcasting rules after it mistakenly announced the death of King Charles III.

The station aired three pre-recorded announcements falsely stating the King had died during the Barry Marsh Show on 19 May.

The messages claimed the "news media" had "confirmed" the death, and were followed by the national anthem and 16 minutes of silence on DAB+, while AM listeners heard back-up music. A correction and apology was broadcast 30 minutes later.

The ruling by media watchdog Ofcom stated that once the staff member who accidentally played the files realised what they had done, they stopped playing them, "panicked and left the premises".

Ofcom said the incident breached Rule 5.1, which requires news to be reported with due accuracy, and Rule 5.2, which says significant mistakes must be corrected quickly.

It described the false announcement as a "very significant inaccuracy" on a matter of "very high public interest".

The mistake happened after a staff member carrying out maintenance accessed preârecorded obituary files intended for use in the event of the King's death.

Ofcom said the files were played "out of curiosity", cutting off the presenter's remote stream and putting the announcements on air.

News.title: Man, 18, dies after getting into difficulty in sea
News.content:
The three were known to each other and had travelled to the beach from London, according to police.

The coastguard also responded, along with Pett Level lifeboat and South East Coast Ambulance Service.

Stuart Ross Thomson said he was staying at property overlooking the beach with his family when the "harrowing" and "tearful" incident happened.

"It breaks my heart, to be fair. It's such a heartbreaking situation to watch," the former lifeguard said.

"You're seeing the family members distraught, crying, it's hard to watch. Unfortunately it's the reality of being close to the ocean."

He said there was another separate incident shortly before the man's death.

"You can't commend the [emergency] services more," he said.

"There were helicopters, boats, people doing crowd control. There was so much going on here, it was really top notch."

A police spokesperson confirmed inquiries in the area remained ongoing, and there was an increased emergency presence.

The force said there were no suspicious circumstances behind the death and it would be looked at by a coroner.

The man who died was initially reported to have been 24 years old, but was later said to have been 18.

News.title: Senior detective under investigation over use of AI
News.content:
A senior detective is being investigated over potential artificial intelligence (AI)-related gross misconduct.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it had started investigating the officer after they were referred to the watchdog by Derbyshire Police following an "internal review" of their use of AI.

The investigation into the force comes two months after a criminal investigation was launched into another officer accused of using AI systems to "create evidential material in a number of cases".

Derbyshire Police said on Monday it made a voluntary referral to the IOPC on 23 June "regarding an officer's use of artificial intelligence".

The force said the latest investigation was being independently led by the IOPC and it was unable to comment further.

The Financial Times (FT), external reported a person familiar with events said the case involved a detective chief inspector at the force alleged to have used AI to maintain "decision logs".

Senior investigators maintain such logs during investigations to record why they took each step, and they can be disclosed for defence lawyers to scrutinise during court cases, the FT said.

News.title: Kidnappers made man film naked ransom videos
News.content:
An ex-soldier who was part of a gang which kidnapped and beat a man before making him film naked ransom videos has been jailed for four years.

Mark Pearce, 53, and others took the victim to a caravan in a field owned by Pearce near Stockton for the hours-long ordeal in April 2024, Teesside Crown Court heard.

The kidnappers had disguised themselves as delivery drivers and bundled the man into a van outside his home, the court heard.

Pearce, from Stockton, had denied wrongdoing but was found guilty of conspiracy to kidnap along with Donald Hammond, 43 from London, who was jailed for six years at an earlier hearing.

The victim was confronted by three men in high-vis jackets outside his home and shoved into the back of a van on 13 April 2024, prosecutor Oliver Connor said.

The men were wearing their jackets to make them look like delivery drivers, the court heard.

The victim was taken to a caravan in a field where he was bound with tape and cable ties and blindfolded.

News.title: Water outage forces Chessington theme park to close
News.content:
Chessington World of Adventures has been forced to close for the day after what the resort described as a water outage in the local area.

The theme park and zoo in south-west London said tickets booked for Monday 10 August would be returned or could be resused.

It did not say what had caused the outage or when it expected to reopen.

The closure falls in the middle of the school summer holidays, one of the busiest periods for UK theme parks.

Chessington apologised for the inconvenience and thanked visitors for their understanding.

The park shut for a day in July 2018 after a burst water main left homes and businesses in the surrounding area without supply or on low pressure.

News.title: Rare £3.7m Ferrari seized in police crackdown
News.content:
A Ferrari valued at about Â£3.7m was among 90 vehicles seized by police during a weekend operation against antisocial driving in central London.

The Metropolitan Police said the vehicles, worth more than Â£8m in total, were taken in Kensington, Chelsea and Hyde Park between Friday and Sunday. Officers targeted uninsured, antisocial and dangerous driving.

The Ferrari Monza SP2 is one of 499 built by the Italian manufacturer and had been in the UK for a day when it was stopped, the force said.

The Met said the driver had been in the car for less than half an hour, held only a provisional licence and had no insurance.

News.title: Risk of patient safety 'bonfire' with Health Bill changes, Lib Dems say
News.content:
The Liberal Democrats have urged Andy Burnham to stop the "bonfire of patient safety" under Labour proposals to modernise the NHS in England.

Healthwatch England (HWE), an independent body which represents the views of patients at their local health and social care providers, is set to be scrapped under the government's Health Bill.

The Health Services Safety Investigations Body (HSSIB), which carries out patient safety investigations, is also being abolished.

The government says its changes will strip back bureaucracy and improve patient safety.

But the Lib Dems have warned the changes risk another Stafford Hospital scandal â where years of abuse and neglect led to hundreds of unnecessary patient deaths.

A Healthcare Commission report found the scandal â one of the biggest in NHS history â involved at least 400 more deaths than expected between 2005 and 2008.

Under the bill, introduced in May by the Starmer government, Healthwatch's responsibilities will be transferred to integrated care boards (ICBs) and local authorities, meaning they would have to respond to feedback about their own services, rather than being challenged by an independent body.

Last November Andy Burhnam, when still mayor of Greater Manchester, co-signed a letter, external to Wes Streeting, then health secretary, opposing the changes to Healthwatch. He said the organisation played a vital role in ensuring patient voices were heard, adding "their independence is central to this".

Separately, HSSIB's functions will be transferred to the government-run Care Quality Commission (CQC), which the Lib Dems argue raises concerns there is no guarantee that staff who raise safety concerns are given anonymity.

Former Conservative Health Secretary Sir Jeremy Hunt has also raised concerns, telling the BBC: "We have made countless representations to the government and cannot understand why they won't budge.

"Scrapping HHSIB won't save money, nor do the CQC really want it," he added.

The Conservative MP Sir Bernard Jenkin, former chair of the Commons Public Administation Committee said: "HSSIB is, as yet, very small and has not had time or money to build up its capacity to have a big impact. Labour supported this when it was implemented, so they have no mandate to do this. Abolishing it now is a major setback for safety in the NHS."

Other measures in the bill include the abolition of NHS England in a bid to centralise the running of health and social care services under the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC).

The government says this will reduce bureaucracy and allow more resources to be delivered to frontline healthcare services.

Chessington World of Adventures has been forced to close for the day, sparking outrage for customers who said they were unable to claim refunds.

Thrillseekers and parents hoping to take their children for a day out during the school summer holidays were left disappointed after a water outage in the KT9 area of Surrey left the amusement park unable to operate.

Chessington has advised people not to travel to the theme park if they had tickets booked for Monday.

A statement from the park on its website read: “Due to a water outage in the local area affecting our operations, Chessington is closed today. All tickets booked for today will be automatically revalidated under our Return Promise and can be used on a future date. We apologise for the inconvenience and thank you for your understanding.”

Customers were told they would be able to return for free on “selected dates” within nine months under the Return Promise that is only issued during inclement weather that lasts over an hour, extreme weather like heatwaves, power cuts and loss of water. Returning requires customers to pre-book a reservation ticket.

open image in gallery Chessington World of Adventures is popular among parents with young children (Chessington World of Adventures Resort/PA) ( Chessington World of Adventures Resort )

Journalist Jessica Elgot shared a photo from the site of the shut down park and said on social media that there were “zero comms till you arrive, no refund available and only a guarantee of a return on ‘limited dates’.”

One customer on social media, who said he was queued outside the park shortly after 10am, said it was an “utter shambles” as the theme park provided “no information whatsoever on why they won’t let us into the park - but rides going past with people on them.”

Thames Water reported a burst water main on Leatherhead Road which appeared to be behind the water outage, according to a statement issued on the water company’s website.

“We are working to carry out the repair on the damaged pipe to get water flowing through your taps as soon as possible,” the statement read, promising an update by 2pm.

The water outage comes as Thames Water and South East Water customers are currently under a hosepipe ban as half of England remains under a drought. The National Drought Group will meet on Monday to decide whether more parts of England are experiencing drought conditions.

A spokesperson from Chessington World of Adventures said: "We are currently experiencing operational disruption due to a burst water main that is affecting the local area. As a result, the attraction is closed today while our teams work closely with Thames Water and local partners to restore normal operations as quickly and safely as possible.

“We appreciate the patience and understanding of our guests and can confirm that anyone impacted will be automatically revalidated under our Return Promise. The safety of our guests and employees remains our highest priority."

Half of England and parts of Wales are now subject to a hosepipe ban as most of the country is in drought.

Half of England and Wales have already been plunged into drought but more regions could be declared on Monday afternoon when officials - including regulators, government officials, water companies and agricultural bodies - meet at the National Drought Group.

East Anglia, Hertfordshire, London, Thames Valley, Hampshire, the Isle of Wight, Devon, Cornwall, the West Midlands and Wessex (Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire, and south Gloucestershire) are already officially in drought.

Nine water companies have announced a hosepipe ban this summer. Although temporary, there is no official date in place for when these bans will end.

open image in gallery A temporary ban is in place across half of England and Wales ( Getty )

South West Water was the latest water company to impose water restrictions due to prolonged dry weather that saw the UK record the driest July on record.

The utility firm said that due to below average rainfall and a high demand on supplies, customers in Devon, Cornwall, the Isles of Scilly, parts of Dorset and Somerset should not use hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars or filling up paddling pools.

Where are the hosepipe bans?

Nine water companies across England and Wales have imposed hosepipe bans following persistent hot and dry weather.

Affinity Water, Anglian Water, Cambridge Water, Essex & Suffolk Water, South East Water, Southern West Water, Southern Water, Thames Water and Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water are affected by hosepipe bans.

When will the hosepipe bans end?

There is no specific date set for the hosepipe bans to end but water companies have explained that it will be lifted once water sources have recovered back to normal levels.

Southern Water has said it needs enough water in reservoirs, rivers and underground aquifers to meet demand before it can lift the ban.

Anglian Water has also said it needs to ensure “public water supply and the environment are protected” before restrictions are eased.

However, areas will need more than just a few days of rain to bring water back up to normal levels.

“A few days of rainfall won't reverse the effects of many months of hot, dry weather,” Anglian Water explains on its website.

“Our rivers, groundwater and reservoirs need sustained rainfall over a much longer period to recover.

“Any rain is welcome and will help. The sooner water resources recover, the sooner restrictions can be removed,” it added.

open image in gallery People walk on a path between the sun scorched grass, turned yellow-brown by a lack of rain, in Greenwich Park ( AFP/Getty )

But the South East will continue to see little in the way of desperately needed rain, the Met Office has warned.

Met Office science manager Dr Amy Doherty described July as a “truly remarkable month” in the UK’s climate record.

“The combination of record-breaking dryness, exceptional warmth and unprecedented sunshine has delivered one of the most notable summer months in our historical records,” she said.

A Thames Water spokesperson explained the firm is monitoring water levels across the region and will lift restrictions “as soon as conditions allow”.

Why are there hosepipe bans in place?

Back-to-back heatwaves and severely low rainfall has led to official drought conditions being declared and water companies now need to restrict water use.

Almost half of England and the whole of Wales is in drought. Last month, 19 counties across England recorded effectively no rainfall – 1mm or less, Met Office figures show.

England as a whole had just a 10th of the average rainfall for the month, while Wales saw just 9 per cent of the average, with both countries seeing less than half of the rainfall in the previous record dry July in 1911.

open image in gallery in July, 19 counties across England recorded effectively no rainfall, according to the Met Office ( Getty )

June 2026 was the hottest June on record for England, the Met Office has said, with the highest temperature of 38C set in Lingwood, Norfolk, on 26 June. The previous record of 35.6C was set in Southampton in June 1976.

Helen Wakeham, chairwoman of the National Drought Group and director of water at the Environment Agency, said: “Dry weather depletes our water, while the hot conditions mean we use more of it.

“This is a difficult combination, and we are seeing the effects on our farmers, our wildlife, and the amount available for public and business use.

“All sectors are taking action, and we are grateful to the public for following the restrictions, where in place, to make sure there is enough water for everyone this summer.

“We want everyone to stay safe and hydrated during the hot weather but every drop we can save is a drop more for nature and agriculture.”

Gianni Infantino’s position as Fifa president is verging on untenable as member associations begin to withdraw their support for his re-election following his disastrously botched bid to privatise the World Cup.

Infantino planned to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors under the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), but this was met with intense backlash from football federations, with Uefa threatening to boycott Fifa tournaments if the plans were passed.

The response forced a climbdown from the Swiss-Italian but that is far from the end of the story. Many footballing bodies say they have “lost confidence” in Infantino as president, with the Asian Football Confederation calling for an “urgent review of [Fifa’s] governance”.

And now Infantino has summoned senior Fifa officials to a crisis meeting with a number of his allies dwindling after Fifa’s secretary general Mattias Grafstrom’s criticism, while the president of the Jordan FA publicly accused Infantino of “blackmail”.

Before he eventually scrapped the plans, senior figures inside Fifa turned on the president. Infantino’s long-term adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, chose to quit in protest over the initial proposals, while Fifa’s chief operating officer said that Infantino “deceived” staff over his plans.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham reiterated his belief that Infantino is “not the right man for the job” before things escalated further with the official withdrawal of support from the likes of the Welsh and Swedish FAs, with England set to follow suit.

With it not expected that Infantino will bow to resignation calls despite the immense pressure, federations are now looking to oust the maligned president from power, with certain dates in the coming months set to prove pivotal in shaping the football world governing body’s future. Here are the key dates that could decide Infantino’s future as Fifa president:

5 August: Gianni Infantino holds a crisis meeting with senior Fifa officials in Morocco in a bid to salvage his presidency and releases a letter apologising for ‘mistakes’ over World Cup sell-off plan but reiterates support from Fifa.

14 August: Fifa to come to a decision over an independent agency’s exploration of a 64-team World Cup.

A brief appearing to show the acceleration of Fifa’s World Cup expansion plans dropped at the height of the sell-off controversy, which revealed an “independent” assessment of the potential format which would implemented from the 2030 edition.

The timeline on the documents said Fifa would receive agency proposals by 7 August, with a Fifa decision on 14 August. Delivery of analysis by the agency is then scheduled for 11 September - eight days before member associations were meant to be voting over the FFE, before plans were scrapped.

While the timing of this decision appeared linked to the privatisation scheme - an expanded tournament would be hugely beneficial on a commercial front, after all - a 64-team format could nevertheless win Infantino support from smaller nations looking for a greater chance of qualification to football’s top table.

open image in gallery The World Cup could be set for further expansion after the first 48-team tournament in 2026 ( Getty )

23 September: Deadline for Extraordinary Congress agenda, which takes place two months later. This is where a vote of no confidence could take place, if the necessary procedural steps are completed by this date to include it on the agenda.

Uefa is reviewing the possibility for its national associations to trigger a vote of no confidence in Infantino, which would only require 43 associations to take action.

However, it is unlikely such a move would be made unless there was a strong belief, if not certainty, that a majority among Fifa’s 211 members existed to unseat Infantino at that Congress.

This means the movement to garner enough opposition to Infantino faces a race against time.

open image in gallery Gianni Infantino may face a vote of no confidence ( PA )

18 November: Deadline for Fifa presidential candidates.

Those looking to challenge Infantino for president would need to submit their proposals by this time to stand in the election held in March 2027. So far no other candidate has declared to take Infantino on.

There are calls for Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin and Qatar Sports Investment chairman Nasser Al-Khelaifi to stand, though it does not appear either are keen to run for office.

Meanwhile, it appears Concacaf president Victor Montagliani, a current Fifa vice-president, would be prepared to expedite his aspirations to run for football’s top position, though no official statement of intent has been made.

open image in gallery Concacaf president Montagliani has been rumoured as a potential challenger to Infantino ( Getty )

23 November: Extraordinary Congress scheduled to take place.

If included in the agenda by September’s deadline, this is would be the vehicle for a vote of no confidence.

Infantino would lose power if a simple majority of the votes cast supported the motion. There are 211 member associations who all have a single vote.

open image in gallery A vote of no confidence could take place at the Extraordinary Conference, if it's included on the agenda ( Reuters )

18 March 2027: Fifa presidential election takes place at the 77th Fifa Congress, held in Rabat, Morocco.

If Infantino avoids being ousted by a vote of no confidence, his presidency will be put on the line when he seeks re-election next March.

That is contingent on somebody standing against him. In 2023, the incumbent Infantino was the only candidate in the presidential race.

Fast food venues saw footfall rebound in June because of demand for chicken shops but pubs suffered weaker customer numbers despite the boost from the World Cup, according to new figures.

Hospitality industry footfall data from Meaningful Vision showed that fast food operators managed to avoid the downturn affecting large parts of the sector this year, as consumer spending comes under further pressure.

It showed that fast food footfall increased by 0.3% in June compared with the same month a year earlier, representing the first increase so far this year.

Foot traffic for fast food was nevertheless 0.9% lower for the first six months of 2026, compared with a year earlier.

Chicken shops have driven the growth, with a 10.5% increase for the half year, while burger restaurants reported a period of decline.

The research also highlighted continued pressure on the pub sector so far this year, amid a backdrop of higher labour costs and weak consumer sentiment.

The Meaningful Vision data – which tracks customer visits, pricing, promotions, and store openings at 60,000 outlets – showed that footfall fell by 4.8% at pubs in June.

It represented a slowdown in decline amid a boost from the World Cup, with customer visits down 7% year on year over the second quarter.

Maria Vanifatova, chief executive of Meaningful Vision, said: “The start of the World Cup provided a sentiment boost and filled pubs for live screenings, but the uplift was not strong enough to reverse the broader downward trend for the sector.

“More widely, the UK food service industry is still struggling, as consumers reduce how often they eat and drink out, while food and labour costs continue to rise, putting significant pressure on profits.

“But June did bring around a relative improvement across all sub-sectors, pushing fast food back into positive territory.”

News.title: Asylum seeker who posed as teen on Snapchat to groom and rape 13-year-old girl is jailed
News.content:

An asylum seeker who pretended to be a teenager on social media to groom and rape a 13-year-old girl has been sentenced to nine and a half years in prison.

Nottingham Crown Court heard that Abdul Khan, believed to be 28, arrived in the UK hidden in a lorry in 2015, and will be subject to automatic deportation to Afghanistan after serving two thirds of his term.

Khan, currently of HMP Nottingham, was already serving a 23-month sentence for engaging in sexual communication with another child in the Derbyshire area.

Members of the jury convicted him last week on two counts of rape, alongside charges of sexual activity with a child, sexual communication with a child, meeting a child following grooming, and perverting the course of justice.

During a four-day trial, the court heard Khan interacted with the victim via Snapchat while pretending to be a 14-year-old boy, before arranging to meet her at a nature reserve in Clifton, Nottingham.

open image in gallery Khan was sentenced at Nottingham Crown Court ( PA )

Following initial sexual activity that jurors decided was consensual, Khan raped the victim twice in May last year.

The victim attended court on Monday as prosecutor Dawn Pritchard presented a victim personal statement to Judge Mark Watson, stating that the teenager "feels numb when she thinks back to how she felt at the time".

Summarising the statement, Miss Pritchard said: "She felt scared of the world after it happened and felt overwhelmed.

"When she has flashbacks she sees his face and what happened. She feels like she can’t trust anyone."

Defence barrister Andrew Wesley told the court he could offer no personal mitigation on Khan’s behalf, as the defendant continues to contest the identity and age under which he was prosecuted.

Sentences were passed as Judge Watson addressed Khan, telling him: "You deliberately concealed your true identity.

"She (the 13-year-old) thought she was communicating with a child of her own age. It was a lie you have persisted with throughout these proceedings."

The court was told that when the victim met Khan in person, it became apparent he was older than 14, at which point he attempted to appease her by claiming he was 16.

The judge described the defendant’s claims regarding his age and identity as "nonsensical" and destined to fail, adding: "The police were called by her father, he learning from her that she had been raped.

"She has on any view been profoundly affected, as her parents must also have been. Your sentence will mean automatic deportation."

Khan, who covered his face with his hands as he departed the dock, was also ordered to register as a sex offender indefinitely.

Police say a former Thai MP shot and killed a senior local official on Monday before calling a YouTuber to confess to the shooting during a livestream.

Chalong Reawraeng, a former veteran politician, is accused of shooting Thongchai Yenprasert, president of the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organisation, outside a government building at 11am on Monday morning.

Thongchai died at hospital while receiving treatment for gunshot wounds to the face and neck. His driver, who was also shot in the arm, is in stable condition after undergoing surgery.

The incident in Nonthaburi came just days after a major school shooting in the same province, in which a 14-year-old boy killed his grandparents and six others before shooting himself.

Mr Chalong served as an MP for three terms, most recently under the Pheu Thai party. Moments after Monday’s attack, he called YouTuber Anchalee Paireerak and confessed to what he had done, according to police and a recording of the conversation.

open image in gallery Chalong Reawraeng dialled into a YouTube livestream to confess to shooting Thongchai Yenprasert ( TPBS )

He was arrested shortly after, and presented before the media at the police station. There, he again admitted to the shooting, claiming he was “angry” at Thongchai and calling him a “good friend”.

"I wanted to apologise to the people of Nonthaburi," he said. "I had no intention. We were friends and I thought we could talk it out, but he wouldn't talk to me."

He said he had come to talk to Thongchai as he wanted to retrieve money he had lent him. He said he followed Thongchai to his car before drawing a gun.

"He [Thongchai] then pushed me, saying 'I don't want to talk, I don't want to talk.'"

open image in gallery Thongchai Yenprasert, 71, died at a hospital after shot in face and neck on Monday ( Social media )

He said he did not intend to shoot Thongchai, but the driver also drew a gun and pointed at him, prompting him to open fire.

"When I pulled the gun out, I didn't intend to shoot him. But then [Thongchai's driver] pulled his gun out and pointed it at me, so I fired."

Regional police commander Wattana Yeejeen said the suspect had admitted to the shooting and that the motive was personal.

open image in gallery Forensic police officers inspect the site of a shooting after former lawmaker Chalong Riewrang allegedly shot Thongchai Yenprasert, president of the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organisation ( Reuters )

Mr Chalong’s conversation with YouTuber and political commentator Anchalee played out dramatically on her YouTube channel, though his side of the conversation largely could not be heard.

“Please wait… It’s Brother Chalong Reawraeng,” Anchalee said as she answered a call on her mobile phone. Chalong cannot be heard during the first part of the conversation.

“Brother Chalong Reawraeng, wait up - I’ll call you back, I’m on air,” Anchalee said. “What’s the big story? What? What did you say? Why did you shoot him? And where are you? You shot him just now? And did he die? Did he die? You shot him in the head?

“Now where are you going? You need to wait there for the cops. Don’t go anywhere.”

Anchalee’s team eventually put Mr Chalong on loudspeaker, and he can be heard saying that Thongchai owed him money for a favour.

“Just calm down, sit down and we can talk,” Anchalee said.

open image in gallery Moment Anchalee Paireerak received Chalong’s call confessing crime ( Naewena Online )

Later, Mr Chalong was heard saying: “The cops are here.”

“You’re with the cops now. Put your gun down and don’t shoot anyone else, okay?” Anchalee replied.

“Yes, I gave it to them,” Mr Chalong said.

Thongchai was appointed chief of the provincial body in 2004. He was a former police officer who joined the forces in 1984 and served as the deputy superintendent. He also served as a superintendent of several district police stations in Nonthaburi, a district on the outskirts of Bangkok.

Nonthaburi was still reeling on Monday after a 14-year-old student killed at least eight people in a shooting at Debsirin Nonthaburi School and his home on Friday, before taking his own life.

open image in gallery Forensics police officers gather evidence at the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organization (PAO) office in Nonthaburi province, north of Bangkok ( AFP/Getty )

A 12-year-old schoolgirl and five school staff were killed at the school, while the boy also killed his two grandparents at his family home earlier in the morning, officials said.

The incidents have set off a debate over gun control laws in Thailand, which has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in Asia, second only to Pakistan and far surpassing its Southeast Asian neighbours.

Following Friday’s shooting, Thai premier Anutin Charnvirakul ordered tougher enforcement against people carrying guns in public and said police would set up checkpoints as part of a crackdown, which would include tightening controls on the possession, ‌carrying and use of firearms.

"No one has the right to carry a firearm, especially in ​a public place," Mr Anutin told reporters, adding that claiming a weapon was for self-defence was no ‌justification.

Under government rules, people in Thailand are required to obtain separate licences for owning and carrying firearms, and there are tough punishments in place for violators.

Nonetheless, the country also has one of the highest rates for mass shootings in Asia, with recent incidents including ​schools, a major Bangkok mall and a 2022 killing spree in the country's northeast that killed 36 people, including 22 children

News.title: Radio station falsely announced King’s death then broadcast 16 minutes of silence as panicked presenter ran away
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging.
