Radio Caroline has been found to have breached Ofcom rules when it accidentally announced that the King had died.

The Essex broadcaster apologised in May after the messages were played on The Barry Marsh Show, one of which said “we have suspended our normal programmes until further notice as a mark of respect following the passing of His Majesty King Charles III”.

The messages were followed by the national anthem and around 16 minutes of silence before the presenter apologised for the error.

He said: “I’ve just been informed that we’ve played in error some information a little earlier. I didn’t hear this myself, but it is incorrect, it’s a technical issue, and of course we apologise.”

An Ofcom ruling said that once the presenter realised what he had done, he stopped the files and “panicked and left the premises”.

The media regulator said it had received two complaints about the broadcast, and said it had breached rules 5.1, requiring that news is reported accurately and impartially, and 5.2, requiring that mistakes in news are acknowledged and corrected on air quickly.

open image in gallery The Essex radio show apologised in May after the messages were played on The Barry Marsh Show, one of which said 'we have suspended our normal programmes until further notice as a mark of respect following the passing of His Majesty King Charles III' ( Reuters )

An Ofcom statement read: “We considered this to have been a very significant inaccuracy about an issue of particular public importance.

“As outlined above, Radio Caroline did not broadcast an apology and clarification until approximately 30 minutes after the inaccurate announcements were first broadcast.

“We noted that the Licensee was monitoring the output around the time of the incident and that an engineer was already aware of the issue, but that it took some time to understand what had occurred and reinstate the scheduled programme, with that being exacerbated by the circumstances of the presenter streaming the programme remotely.”

The station said the files that contained the messages were accompanied by “a set of strict instructions to presenters and managers” to follow before playing them, but that a member of staff played them out of curiosity.

Radio Caroline said that they “took the matter very seriously”, and that they had acted “as soon as possible”.

open image in gallery Radio Caroline said that they ‘took the matter very seriously’, and that they had acted ‘as soon as possible’ ( AFP/Getty )

The station said the staff member who played the files had been “reprimanded” and had “apologised”, and that in order to prevent a recurrence of this issue, Radio Caroline had removed the relevant files from the desktop on the studio computer.

It also said that its presenters and support staff had been reminded of the relevant procedures.

News.title: Richard Madeley scares Kate Garraway with ‘disturbing’ Hannibal Lecter mask
News.content:
Richard Madeley left his Good Morning Britain co-host Kate Garraway “disturbed” after he tried on a Hannibal Lecter mask.

On Monday (10 August), John Partridge joined the presenters on the ITV sofa to discuss his role playing the cannibalistic serial killer in a new play adaptation of the 1990s hit film The Silence of the Lambs.

Trying on Partridge’s custom-made mask, a deadpan Madeley stared down into the camera, whilst Garraway told him: “It’s so disturbing.”

“I’m really enjoying this,” Madeley remarked as Partridge took back the mask, with Garraway laughing as she said her co-host was back to “being all adorable and cuddly”.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: ‘Made my eye involuntarily twitch’ – Man Utd fans immediately triggered by Ruben Amorim’s comments after Chelsea loss
Sports.content:
RUBEN AMORIM has left Manchester United fans traumatised – after conceding his AC Milan side will “suffer” following a pre-season hammering against Chelsea.

A Joao Pedro brace and wonder goal from Moises Caicedo resulted in the Italian giants being consigned to a 3-0 thumping.



The worrying defeat came just weeks after Amorim, 41, bagged the AC Milan job and was tasked with spearheading a Serie A title charge.

But the former United boss immediately triggered Red Devils fans during his post-match interview.



Amorim, who was brutally sacked by Old Trafford chiefs in January, said: “We knew we would suffer a little, but we want to put our players through this kind of challenge.

“They know how to defend as a team, play one-on-one and press high. Against teams like Chelsea, we would never press in this way.

“But we are here to prepare ourselves to win the first official match of the season and give the players confidence.

“We also had a lot of young players in the squad. We are following the right path to put the team in a position to win the first official match of the season.”

Amorim warned United supporters to expect to “suffer” just days after being handed the Old Trafford reins.

And he repeated the message several times before the Red Devils wielded the axe.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

United fans raced onto social media to admit Amorim’s comments had led to bad memories.

One said: “Made my eye involuntarily twitch.”

Another added: “Instantaneous United fans PTSD.”

A third chimed in: “Here we go again.”



A fourth noted: “He said the thing!”

And a fifth claimed: “He has an unhealthy obsession with suffering.”

Sports.title: Man Utd icon, 41, reveals he needs hip replacement weeks after retiring from football
Sports.content:
FORMER Manchester United star Ashley Young needs a hip replacement, just weeks after announcing his retirement from football.

The 41-year-old called time on his 23-year career this summer after a short spell at Ipswich Town, in which the Tractor Boys climbed back up to the Premier League.



Speaking on the High Performance Podcast, Young explained the problems he was having with his hip.

He said: “I went down on my hip in November and had an injection. I have always said to myself: ‘If my body is saying you need injections, there is a problem, you need to think about retiring’.



“Basically I need a hip replacement, in November I was told I would need it in about 10 years time.

“I got to January and was due to have another injection which would have got me through to the end of the season, as I was saying to the specialist ‘I know it is painful, but I want to make sure I do everything I can possibly do to help the team’.



“About a week before I am about to have the injection, I go down on it in training and I am like ‘this is worse, I know it is a lot worse’.”

Young then revealed that a specialist told him his hip had become “much worse”, giving him a two-year window to get it replaced.

He concluded that it came as a result of overuse following his 756-game senior career which spanned from 2003-2026.

The 41-year-old was physically unable to train for three months but was still determined to end his career on a high.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He said: “From January to the end of the season, I literally had two or three months where I couldn’t train it was that painful. I saw the specialist again and said ‘I’m not going out like this’. He said he didn’t want to give me another injection as it would weaken the area.

“I asked him ‘are you telling me I can’t play football again, you can say it if you want, trust me if I get an opportunity to be back on the pitch, I’ll be back on the pitch’.

“The last two months of the season I was training every day and he was like ‘it is not possible, you shouldn’t be training’.”

The ex-England man’s grit and determination saw him train all the way through the crucial end of season run-in, despite not actually getting on the pitch.

He added: “It would have been incredible to come onto the pitch for the last game of the season but for me to train like I did that week and for us to be promoted on the last day of the season, it was fitting.”



Ipswich finished second in the Championship, securing a return to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

It was the final feat of Young’s successful career, which included winning the Premier League, Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup at Man United.

Young also won a Serie A title in 2021 during his spell at Inter Milan.

Sports.title: Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos ‘closing in on stake in Liverpool and deal could be announced THIS WEEK’
Sports.content:
TECH BILLIONAIRE Jeff Bezos is reportedly closing in on a deal to buy a minority stake in Liverpool.

The Amazon founder is part of a consortium that is in talks with Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG).



And according to Sky News, a deal could be announced as early as this week.

The investor group is headed up by Amit Bhatia, who was previously a long-term shareholder at Queens Park Rangers.



Bhatia’s father-in-law is Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, with a net worth put at around £23bn.

Eduardo Saverin – who co-founded Facebook alongside Mark Zuckerberg – is also said to be involved in the syndicate.



Saverin was memorably played by Andrew Garfield in the hit movie The Social Network based on the early days of Facebook.

The deal would see Liverpool given additional financial power from some of the wealthiest men on the planet.

Bezos has an estimated net worth of £213BILLION, making him the third-richest person on the planet.

And Saverin is said to be worth around £25bn and is the wealthiest person in Brazil.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

BEZOS COULD TAKE LIVERPOOL TO NEXT LEVEL By Ken Lawrence LIVERPOOL’S links with Amazon tycoon Jeff Bezos could deliver the club to the next level. The Reds finished fifth last season – a mammoth 25 points behind Premier League winners Arsenal. So the news that Bezos, after joining forces with Amit Bhatia’s consortium, is nearing a deal to buy a minority stake in the Anfield side means they could become box-office once again. American Bezos, 62, is estimated by Forbes magazine to boast a fortune of around £200billion, making him the world’s fourth-richest man. And if he comes on board, Liverpool could be wrapping up more of the game’s big prizes. Read the full story

The investment – previously reported to be £1.35bn for around 30 per cent of the club – would value Liverpool at £4.4bn, making it is one of the richest deals in sports.

Liverpool’s FSG ownership is headed up by John W Henry and their leadership has overseen two Premier League title wins and the Champions League.

Henry and FSG bought Liverpool for a modest £300m after the club ran into financial trouble under Tom Hicks and George Gillett.

Links between Liverpool and Bezos first emerged last month.



FSG confirmed the approach in a statement to the Financial Times, saying: “An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.”

The extra investment could be vital amid Liverpool’s talks with PSG to sign £130m-rated star Bradley Barcola.

Liverpool embarked on a record-breaking spree of more than £440m last summer, but still finished fifth and 25 points behind Prem winners Arsenal.

The news comes at a time when interest from investors in top level football appears to be at an all-time high.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fifa president Gianni Infantino recently plotted to create a subsidiary that would have allowed investors to buy chunks of the World Cup.



But the footballing world rebelled against the controversial proposals and threatened a boycott of future tournaments before the plans were scrapped.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s pre-season woes are a sign of what’s to come if Declan Rice and Co aren’t back sooner rather than later
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’S pre-season struggles are a warning sign for what might happen if their World Cup stars are not back sharpish.

And the Gunners will be desperate to get new £75m signing Bruno Guimaraes ready for action as soon as possible to make things right.



The reigning champions have leaked six goals in two consecutive pre-season defeats as Mikel Arteta battles to manage his bare-bones squad.

Sunday afternoon’s 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium marked the first time since April 2023 that Arsenal conceded three or more goals in consecutive games.



It followed their 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday and will have alarm bells ringing for Arteta with the Community Shield just SIX days away.

Arsenal kick off their campaign proper with a trip to Cardiff this Sunday, taking on Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City in the annual curtain raiser.



City have dispatched teams like Atletico Madrid in pre-season and are already playing with top returning players like Antoine Semenyo and Omar Marmoush.

But Arteta finds himself without a host of top stars, which has made his champions look like a shadow of their usual selves in pre-season.

England quartet Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke and Ebere Eze, and world champions Mikel Merino, David Raya and Martin Zubimendi will only begin their pre-season preparations today.

Martin Odegaard played just 30 minutes against Dortmund after returning to training last week, and he will need more minutes in the tank before he can be trusted to play a full game.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Meanwhile Jurrien Timber and William Saliba both remain out with groin and back injuries, respectively, and are not expected to return for the start of the season.

The absence of those players has been felt throughout Arsenal’s pre-season.

Yesterday’s defeat to Dortmund showed Arsenal’s defensive frailties when Saliba and Timber are unavailable.

Cristhian Mosquera fell asleep, allowing Samuele Inacio to ghost in behind him and score the opener for Dortmund.



And Arsenal finished the game with 18-year-old prospect Theo Julienne at right-back after Ben White was substituted – showing their lack of depth in that position without Timber.

Arteta revealed after the game that both Timber and Saliba are still some way from returning to the fold.

The Arsenal boss said: “Jurrien is progressing really well. He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now. But he’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.

“And William is in rest mode at the moment for two weeks. He had to do almost nothing, don’t aggravate the injury. It’s going to take some time to heal. We know that.”

In midfield, Myles Lewis-Skelly has been operating out-of-position as a lone No6.



Given his inexperience in that area, attacking players have run riot around him without an experienced head to help him through the game.

That was evidenced when Konstantino Karetsas stormed through Arsenal’s midfield as if it didn’t exist before firing a curling effort in for Dortmund’s second goal.

Guimaraes, who was paraded out on the pitch before kick-off, can be the man to help solve that problem when Arsenal take on City on Sunday – but only if he is ready in time.



Arteta will be desperately scrambling to integrate the Brazilian into training and get him up to scratch during their final pre-season friendly against Como on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham was watching from the stands too, at the Emirates to support his brother Jobe who started in midfield for Dortmund.

And what Arteta would give to have a superstar like him available to command the middle of the park in the absence of Rice and Zubimendi.

The Arsenal duo haven’t kicked a ball since the World Cup, and their return seems unlikely before Sunday’s Community Shield.

However, Arteta said that some of his World Cup returnees could be put on a fast track back to action if they were used sparingly during the summer tournament.



He added: “We have very different groups within the same time that they are coming back.

“Some of them, they’ve done more. Others, they’ve done less. Some of them, they almost didn’t participate in the World Cup in terms of minutes. So they are all very different stages.”

There are still some positives in the performance of new addition Christos Tzolis, who continued his pre-season form by getting an assist and winning a penalty.



But it feels paramount that Arteta gets some of his stars back as soon as possible, with Arsenal facing a monstrous start to the season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Gunners take on Man City, Coventry, Aston Villa and Chelsea in a tricky start to their title defence.

If they have to face those challenges without their best players back in action, they could hit a stumbling block or two – leaving them playing catch-up in the title race.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland becomes a tourist attraction as boat full of cheering people sails past his yacht while he’s on holiday
Sports.content:
ERLING HAALAND was stunned after a boat full of adoring fans gatecrashed his holiday.

The Manchester City striker, 26, has been relaxing following a World Cup to remember.



Haaland bagged seven goals before Norway’s dream run was ended by England in the quarter-finals.

And the lethal finisher jetted out to Sicily to soak up the sun ahead of the new Premier League season.



But Haaland appears to have become a tourist attraction after a boat full of cheering people pulled up alongside his luxury yacht to get a glimpse of him in the flesh.

The fans also raced to get photos of Haaland, whose number of Instagram followers skyrocketed during the World Cup, before sailing away.

Footage of the incident has gone viral since being uploaded onto YouTube and social media.

In the video, the City favourite said: “They do tourist boats. Go and drive past where Haaland stays.



“Come have a look at where Erling Haaland stays. I’ve never seen anything like it.”

The former Borussia Dortmund man boarded the yacht after heading to team-mate Gianluigi Donnarumma’s wedding last month – where he hilariously led a Viking Row.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And Haaland turned into a jealous boyfriend when partner Isabel Johansen was seen chatting to Italian actor Michele Morrone.

But the marksman’s time away from the pitch is coming to an end because he is due to return to City ahead of the Community Shield showdown with Arsenal on Sunday.



It is the first time Haaland will be available since Enzo Maresca replaced Pep Guardiola in the Etihad Stadium dugout.

City have locked horns with European heavyweights Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid during preparations for the new season.

The Sky Blues also notched a comfortable win over the K League All-Stars during their Asia tour.



Haaland and Co will get their Premier League title push underway with a clash against Bournemouth on August 23.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino accused of ‘breaking trust through deception’ as Uefa and other football bosses pen furious letter
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO has been accused of “breaking trust through deception” in a damning letter from football bosses.

Uefa and their Asian and North American counterparts, the AFC and Concacaf, teamed up to pen the furious statement taking aim at the Fifa president and want him to resign.



The confederations are also understood to have begun preliminary talks about organising rival tournaments for their players in the wake of Infantino’s radical plans.

Infantino has come under heavy fire since his controversial plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.



He made an embarrassing U-turn and ditched his money-grabbing scheme in a desperate attempt to cling on to his power and position.

Uefa and the other confederations were willing to boycott the World Cup and publicly withdrew their support for Infantino.

And now they have co-signed the letter which directly hits out at his leadership.

The lengthy post – entitled an “open letter to the football family” – was signed by the Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, AFC chief Sheikh Salman Bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa and Concacaf boss Victor Montagliani plus their organisations’ general secretaries.

It says: “This is about something more fundamental: the integrity of the game, and the integrity of those elected to lead it.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.

“Fifa’s recent letter to its Vice-Presidents and 211 Member Associations acknowledges that mistakes were made in the process.

“It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment.



“A proposal advanced on a compressed timeline, without meaningful consultation, and pushed toward a deadline before Member Associations could properly review its terms is not the product of an oversight — it is the product of a design intended to limit scrutiny.

“It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong.

“There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the Fifa World Cup was a profound failure of judgment — not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions Fifa exists to serve.”

The letter also called for an independent commission to conduct the review into Fifa’s recent conduct – not an internal Fifa committee.

It went on to point out that only one election official was part of the Fifa crisis meeting in Morocco last week – with no Fifa Council members or member associations invited to contribute.



The letter continued: “This recent meeting, where a select number of members of the Fifa Management Committee—not the full Committee—were summoned abroad, rather than leadership going to Zurich to address the heart of Fifa, its staff, only reinforces these concerns and

represents a continuation of the very pattern of conduct that brought us to this moment.

“It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him.

“There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness.

“These are not the qualities football deserves in its leadership.

“That is why we have taken this stance: not lightly and not alone, but together, and out of duty to the game we serve.



“Football’s strength has always been its unity. We call for that unity to be honoured now, for leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.”

SunSport understands Concacaf, Uefa and the AFC are pressurising Infantino to resign with immediate effect and not run for re-election for a fourth term in March.

LaLiga chief Javier Tebas, meanwhile, insists the Infantino era is “over” and he is “destroying the very essence of football”.

Tebas fumed in an interview with Le Monde: “For me, Gianni Infantino’s time has long since passed.

“Gianni Infantino is not someone who contributes to the growth of football.



“On the contrary, his projects are destroying the very essence of the sport: the national leagues.

“Football is not limited to the elite. For me, the Infantino era is over.

“What remains to be seen is when that will take effect and how the succession will unfold.

“I hope it is not just a matter of swapping out some people for others, but of a genuine overhaul.”

Fifa released their own strong statement last weekend and claimed there was a “concerted and ongoing effort” to undermine Infantino.



The governing body said: “The Fifa President was democratically elected by Fifa’s Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate.

“It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president.

“Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s Member Associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes.

“Fifa welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress.”

But as well as the scandalous attempt to privatise the World Cup, it has also been revealed in bombshell documents that Infantino was actually plotting to partner with the rebel breakaway European Super League – and it could even have been called the Fifa Super League.



Also, The Telegraph reported on Friday that Uefa paid off a six-figure sum to an alleged mistress of married Infantino while he was general secretary.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And SunSport revealed his latest blow that even his hometown club Zug 94 in Switzerland are refusing to back his beleaguered leadership.

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley ‘wants to buy London Stadium at bargain price’ if she lands stake in West Ham
Sports.content:
AMANDA STAVELEY wants to buy the London Stadium if she becomes a major West Ham shareholder.

The British business executive is reportedly keen on exploring a bargain deal for the Hammers’ home if her bid for David Gold’s family’s 25 per cent stake is successful.



Staveley, 53, is locked in a boardroom battle with current co-owner Daniel Kretinsky, who is also trying to land the shares.

But if she comes out on top, her ambitions may not stop at buying into the Championship club.



According to The Times, Staveley wants to look at buying the London Stadium from the Greater London Authority.

And London mayor Sir Sadiq Khan has opened the door to talks if a sale could save taxpayers money.



A spokesman for Khan said: “The Mayor would welcome any discussions regarding the London Stadium that would deliver greater value for money for Londoners.”

The stadium – built for the 2012 Olympics – is thought to be worth as little as £50MILLION because of the huge cost of running it.

West Ham‘s favourable tenancy agreement after moving into the stadium in 2016 has long been criticised, with the deal regularly labelled the “deal of the century”.

The Hammers were paying around £4.4m a season to use the ground while they were in the Premier League, but that fee has now been cut following relegation.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Meanwhile, the latest accounts are expected to show the stadium is costing taxpayers around £19m to operate.

Any sale would still come with strings attached, with London’s bid to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships meaning any MAJOR redevelopment would likely have to wait until after the event.

Staveley – who pulled the strings in the Saudi takeover of Newcastle – hinted at those wider ambitions in an interview with Bloomberg last week, saying: “Whatever club we take, there’ll be a big property play as well.

“We won’t just do a football-led.



“I just want a challenge, and that’s what excites me.

“That’s where you get value uplift – when you take something from seedling and allow it to grow.”

But before she can start thinking about the stadium, Staveley first has to win the battle for a stake in West Ham.

Staveley’s improved bid for the Gold family’s 25 per cent shareholding has been accepted.

BUT Kretinsky – who owns 27 per cent already – has first refusal on the shares and is trying to get a deal over the line himself.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy could make sensational return to English football as West Ham ‘keep eye on transfer situation’
Sports.content:
WEST HAM are reportedly considering a shock move for Jamie Vardy in their desperate push for more firepower.

The Hammers are targeting an immediate return to the Premier League after being relegated to the Championship last season.



And they made a winning start to their competitive campaign after seeing off Portsmouth in the first round of the Carabao Cup on Saturday.

But West Ham boss Nuno Espirito Santo is still in the market for a striker in the final weeks of the transfer window.



Sky Sports report the Hammers are keeping an eye on Vardy’s situation after his exit from Italian side Cremonese.

The one-time Premier League champion, 39, is a free agent following his decision to quit.



Vardy failed to avoid the drop from Serie A despite notching seven goals in 29 appearances last term.

And West Ham are showing interest in offering him a route back into English football.

Taty Castellanos, who bagged a brace in the win over Portsmouth, is the East Londoners’ first-choice frontman.

Pablo is still searching for his first goal since joining West Ham in a £21.8million move from Gil Vicente in January.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Niclas Fullkrug has been brutally left without a squad number following his return from a loan spell at AC Milan.

Vardy made himself a Premier League legend during his 13-year spell with Leicester.

He spearheaded the Foxes to their shock title win in the 2015/16 season and scored 145 goals in 342 top flight appearances.

Sports.title: Stella issues rivals warning over McLaren 'momentum' in title battles
Sports.content:
McLaren boss Andrea Stella has issued a warning to his team's rivals for the remainder of the 2026 season as he expressed confidence in the Woking squad's ability to maintain momentum once it has been gained.

The reigning constructors' champions claimed a long-awaited first victory of the season in the final race before the summer break as reigning drivers' champion Lando Norris dominated in Hungary.

The result brought Norris back to within 91 points of championship leader Kimi Antonelli, while McLaren closed the gap on the Italian's Mercedes team to 159 points. To retain his title, Norris would also need to leapfrog Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Charles Leclerc, while Ferrari are only 72 points back from Mercedes in the team standings.

While both margins are considerable, Norris' performance following a significant upgrade package in Budapest has provided Stella with belief that McLaren can continue to perform strongly over the remaining 12 rounds of the season, starting with the Dutch Grand Prix from August 21-23.

Asked whether his team can get back into the fight for world titles, Stella said: "That's a difficult question, but there's a very clear answer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Norris' victory last time out in Hungary, David Croft debates whether McLaren are now capable of winning further races or not

"If we can continue the season as we did in Budapest, we can still achieve a great deal. To do so, we must keep pushing with the development of the MCL40 and ensure we outpace our rivals - who certainly aren't standing still - in this race within the race, which is the competition over updates.

"The result will depend on how effective the solutions we bring to the track prove to be. In the first part of the season, we struggled more than we expected in this regard too, but I believe that in recent years, once we've gained some momentum, we've been able to maintain it."

McLaren were in a contrasting position this time last year, having reached the summer break with a 299-point lead in the constructors' standings, and Oscar Piastri leading team-mate Norris in what appeared to be a two-horse race for the drivers' title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

However, Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who trailed Piastri by 104 points with nine rounds remaining, staged a remarkable fightback to ultimately finish the season just two points behind Norris and 11 ahead of Piastri.

Stella added: "There are still 12 races left on the calendar, so there are plenty of opportunities given that 546 points are up for grabs.

"Of course, the gap in both championships is significant, but we remember last year's lesson well: after all, I always tell the team that if we've set up a new display cabinet to house the new, recent trophies at the McLaren Technology Centre, then we have a duty to do our utmost to keep filling it..."

Hungary upgrade represented 'change of direction'

McLaren had played down the upgrade package they brought to Hungary ahead of the event, but the results spoke for themselves as Norris took pole before showing searing pace to win the race.

The Brit ultimately beat Verstappen by 15 seconds but had he not been held up by Piastri for the first half of the race having been overtaken by his team-mate on the opening lap, the margin could have been far greater.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris snatches pole off Lewis Hamilton as Max Verstappen and George Russell struggle in Q3 at Hungaroring

Reflecting on the process that led to the latest upgrades, Stella said: "There wasn't a single event that changed course; rather, it was a growing awareness of the scale of the challenge we're facing and the adjustments we needed to make.

"Paradoxically, the enforced break in April probably allowed us to focus entirely on analysing the MCL40's performance and to fully understand that we needed to redirect or strengthen its development in certain areas of the car.

"It is clear that the Budapest weekend, which brought the first half of the season to a close, was the highlight: not only because of the result, but above all because the aerodynamic package we introduced at the Hungaroring is the result of this change of direction in development and has enabled us to make significant progress in terms of competitiveness."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris reacts to his first win of 2026 saying he always believed he could win and calling it one of his best personal performances

Stella also praised the work his team have done alongside engine supplier Mercedes to optimise the performance of their power unit.

"Over the past few months we've had the opportunity to deepen our understanding of the new power unit supplied by Mercedes HPP and to work with our technical partners to work out how best to utilise it," he added.

"It's been a long process, with its ups and downs, but one that's starting to bear fruit. That said, I expect that optimising the power unit will remain a complex issue throughout the 2026 season."

Sports.title: Amazon founder Bezos nears deal to buy stake in Liverpool
Sports.content:
Sky News understands a consortium including the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is closing in on a deal to buy a roughly one-third stake in Liverpool.

Sky News has learnt that Fenway Sports Group (FSG), the Anfield club's controlling shareholder since 2010, is preparing to make an announcement about a transaction as soon as this week.

The deal will see Mr Bezos participate in an investor group alongside Eduardo Saverin, one of the co-founders of the social network Facebook.

The syndicate is led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and until recently a shareholder in Championship club Queens Park Rangers.

One source indicated that an announcement was expected in the coming days, although they cautioned that it could slip into next week.

If completed, the deal would install a trio of the world's wealthiest individuals as co-owners of the Reds, one of the most successful teams in the history of English football.

Mr Bezos alone has a fortune estimated by Forbes at over £207bn ($280bn), while Mr Saverin is said to be worth over £23.7bn ($32bn).

Their investment in Liverpool will reportedly value the club at £4.4bn ($6bn), making it one of the sport's richest-ever deals.

Sky Sports News has contacted Liverpool and FSG for comment.

Image: Amazon founder Bezos has an estimated fortune of over £207bn

While Mr Bezos has not previously been linked to deals in football, his prospective involvement in the Liverpool FC consortium underlines the extent to which sport is now viewed by wealthy investors as an asset class in its own right.

Mr Saverin, who is 44 years old, was part of a consortium which assembled an unsuccessful takeover bid for Chelsea FC during the 2022 auction triggered by Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

One insider said the deal was now expected to be slightly larger than previously thought, potentially involving a stake of over 30 per cent.

Nevertheless, if its valuation hits £4.4bn ($6bn), the deal will reinforce the huge financial success that FSG has enjoyed during its 16 years as the club's owner.

The Boston Red Sox owner acquired Liverpool for just £300m with the club in a troubled state financially.

The arrival of such a powerful consortium will fuel expectations that its members will ultimately seek outright control of the Reds.

A spokesperson for FSG said last month: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

FSG declined to comment further on the potential timing of a deal.

A spokesman for the consortium led by Mr Bhatia also declined to comment.

The last time a stake in Liverpool changed hands was in 2023, when Dynasty Equity bought a small interest valuing it at more than £3.3bn ($4.5bn).

Image: FSG have been in complete control of Liverpool since 2010

Sky Sports takes a look at some of the key questions surrounding the sale of a minority stake in Liverpool...

Who are Bhatia and Bezos?

Bhatia is a 46-year-old British Indian entrepreneur who has an investment banking background.

He currently manages a multi-asset investment firm called AyBe Capital, which invests in a range of diversified sectors including technology, media, property and real estate, consumer retail, and health.

Bhatia is married to Vanisha Mittal Bhatia, who is the daughter of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

Bezos is one of the most famous businessmen in the world and the owner of e-commerce giant Amazon, which he founded in 1994 out of his Seattle garage.

His other investments include aerospace company Blue Origin and venture capital firm Nash Holdings, which is the ownership vehicle for The Washington Post.

Sports.title: Super League's Final Charge: Play-off spots taking shape with five rounds left
Sports.content:
There are just five rounds of Super League action remaining and, with it, a whole lot of drama as Super League's Final Charge ramps up.

Seven teams remain in contention for a play-off spot and most of those are still eyeing a top-two finish.

In Super League, the two teams who finish in first and second are guaranteed a home semi-final across Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26.

In the week prior to that, the Play-Off Eliminators occur in which the third-place team takes on the team in sixth and fourth plays fifth for the chance to make it into the semis.

Then the winners of the semi-finals head to the Grand Final at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3.

There are going to be so many twists and turns along the way and you can catch them all live on Sky Sports.

With that in mind, let's take a look at what each team has remaining and what is on the line for them...

1) Leeds Rhinos (36 points)

Leeds Rhinos have been sitting pretty at the summit of Super League for a while now and they will want to hold onto that for their five remaining fixtures.

They stayed top in spectacular fashion with a win over Wakefield Trinity in their latest game, showing they mean business.

They last won the League Leaders' Shield way back in 2015 and last won a trophy in 2020 when they took Challenge Cup glory, so finishing top would see a welcome return of some silverware for the Rhinos.

In their last five matches, they face Leigh Leopards (H), York Knights (A), St Helens (A), Wigan Warriors (A) and Hull FC (H).

That means they have three teams in their run-in who are hunting play-off places. If they can remain unbeaten, League Leaders' Shield glory will be theirs and they will be one match from walking out at the 'Theatre of Dreams' once again.

2) Wigan Warriors (34 points)

The team who have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt. Matt Peet, head coach of Wigan, has made no secret of how hard he is pushing for a top-two finish because he knows how crucial that home semi-final is.

Not only that, the Warriors will be hungry to avenge their Grand Final defeat to Hull KR in 2025.

They have the Challenge Cup in their trophy cabinet and will have all eyes on adding a second piece of silverware.

Ahead of the play-offs, they still have to play Bradford Bulls (A), Wakefield Trinity (H), Hull KR (H), Leeds Rhinos (A) and Catalans Dragons (H).

Wigan are likely to have their sights firmly set on ensuring they beat Wakefield and Leeds to pile on the pressure.

3) Wakefield Trinity (32 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caius Faatili produced an incredible run as he set up Caleb Hamlin-Uele's try for Wakefield against Leeds

What a season it has been for Wakefield Trinity. They are on the hunt for their highest Super League finish, but will now want to bounce back following their heart-breaking two-point defeat to top-of-the-table Leeds.

Wakefield returned to Super League last year following their relegation in 2024 and have lit up the competition, their star-studded side becoming a formidable one.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Sinfield scored for Wakefield against his father's former side Leeds as rugby league legend Kevin watched on proudly

They have games against St Helens (H), Wigan Warriors (A), York Knights (H), Warrington Wolves (H) and Leigh Leopards (A) left. That is four teams out of the seven still in the fight.

They will look at York as an absolute must-win and crucial two points. The Wigan and Warrington games will also be key as they are two other teams right in the chase for a top-two spot.

4) Warrington Wolves (30 points, one game in hand)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Bradford Bulls and Warrington Wolves as Matty Ashton scored twice in a dominant 42-4 victory for the visitors

Warrington Wolves, along with Hull KR, have six matches remaining thanks to their rescheduled round-two match.

This was moved due to the Robins playing in Las Vegas.

With that, it is a more jam-packed Final Charge for them but also one gives Sam Burgess' side a good opportunity to prosper.

In their remaining fixtures, they face York Knights (H), Hull KR (A), Huddersfield Giants (H), Hull FC (A), Wakefield Trinity (A) and Toulouse Olympique (H).

If the Wolves are going to be contenders, they will have to pick up points against the four lowly sides they face.

5) Hull KR (28 points, one game in hand)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Castleford Tigers against Hull KR from the Super League

The other side with six games remaining, Hull KR, are right in the mix and will want it to stay that way and climb as high up the table as possible.

The Robins were the team who did it all in 2025, ending the wait for a new team to win the competition, and now they will want to send coach Willie Peters out on a high by going back to back.

Their remaining six matches are against Catalans Dragons (H), Warrington Wolves (H), Toulouse Olympique (H), Wigan Warriors (A), Huddersfield Giants (H) and St Helens (A).

Four out of the six are at Craven Park, which will only boost their chances. Wins against Catalans, Toulouse and Huddersfield will also be a non-negotiable.

6) Leigh Leopards (28 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Leigh Leopards against York Knights from the Super League

The team that has become renowned for coming good when they need to, Leigh Leopards want to shore up their spot in the play-offs once again.

After a disastrous start to the season, Adrian Lam's side have found their groove, made waves and look in real good nick at present.

However, they have a tough end to the season in which they will know every win will matter.

The Leopards face Leeds Rhinos (A), Bradford Bulls (H), Huddersfield Giants (A), St Helens (H) and Wakefield Trinity (H).

No one can deny that is a difficult Final Charge, but if Leigh want to make it to the Grand Final for the first time, they need to show their steel now.

7) St Helens (24 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of St Helens against Hull FC in the Betfred Super League

St Helens have five matches to try and ensure they do not make some unwanted history.

Saints have never missed out on the play-offs. Most recently they lost 20-12 to Hull KR in the semi-finals in 2025 as the Robins went on to complete the treble.

After their most recent loss to Hull FC, it is fair to say St Helens look down and out.

However, they will now refocus and aim for five wins out of five to be in with a shout. If they win all five, they move to 34 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens chairman Eamonn McManus announced his side will take on Hull FC in a Super League clash in Dublin on April 25

Not only that, they face some of the other play-off chasing teams so some matches basically become worth four points.

They will take on Wakefield Trinity (A), Castleford Tigers (H), Leeds Rhinos (H), Leigh Leopards (A) and Hull KR (H).

Four out of their five remaining matches are against teams in the top six - talk about having to take your moment.

Will they do the unthinkable? If they do somehow find some form, that final-round contest against Hull KR could be extra tasty...

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Badri chases four-timer at Windsor
Sports.content:
Windsor takes centre stage on Monday with a six-race Flat meeting live on Sky Sports Racing.

7.15 Windsor - Badri seeks four-timer in Sprint Series Final

Badri seeks a four-timer in the feature race at Windsor, the Fitzdares Sprint Series Final Handicap over six furlongs.

This horse has been a credit to connections, winning 15 times in 75 starts with his last three runs resulting in success, all at Pontefract. That has taken him from 89-rated up to 99 which is his best mark since March 2024.

Another Abbot returns to Windsor looking to follow up his course-and-distance success two weeks ago after previously running a creditable race in behind Amazing Journey, who went on to to win the International Handicap on King George Day at Ascot. That form reads very well and he could be hard to beat.

Sudden Flight is a model of consistency, finishing second in his last three starts which included in behind Another Abbot two weeks ago. He does find winning hard to come by, though, having not won since July last year, but is now better off at the weights with William Haggas' charge and looks sure to run his race.

6.15 Windsor - Harry Knows and Keep Kicking On feature

Previous-winners Harry Knows and Keep Kicking On lock horns in the Fitzdares Nursery Handicap.

Sports.title: Brennan secures FedEx Cup Playoffs spot with Wyndham Championship win
Sports.content:
Michael Brennan secured his place in the FedExCup Playoffs as he won the Wyndham Championship by three strokes from Beau Hossler.

Brennan had a run of five straight birdies between the fourth and eighth holes, and recovered from a bogey on the 11th by picking up further shots on the 13th and 18th holes, saving par on the 17th with an excellent second shot after running into the rough with his tee-shot.

Hossler, who shared the overnight lead with Brennan, had kept himself in touch with a birdie on the third and an eagle at the par-five fifth, but then bogeyed the ninth and 12th holes as Brennan surged forward.

"I did great for nine holes," Brennan said. "I felt really good on the front nine. Just playing my game, I was really staying within myself, hitting good shots.

Image: Brennan shot a final-round 64 at Sedgefield Country Club

"Felt like I was really in control. Got a little nervous around 10 and 11. I made a really nice par putt on 12 and that kind of steadied me a little bit going through and I'm just glad to make a few putts coming in.

"It's everything. I mean, I don't want to be done playing golf. I feel like I've played the best golf I have all year the last couple weeks.

"Unfortunately, a couple tough Sundays, but outside of that, I've been playing really solidly. This is my sixth week in a row and so seven's a lot, but I think I'm going to be perfectly happy running on fumes next week."

England's Harry Hall finished with a round of 65 to take a share of fifth place, one shot clear of compatriot Matt Wallace who had a share of seventh after he also closed with a 65.

Sports.title: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC push for Infantino to quit and discuss rival competitions
Sports.content:
Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf will push for Gianni Infantino to resign after writing an open letter calling for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”.

In a dramatic escalation of the war that has threatened to tear football apart since details emerged of the Fifa president’s failed Football Forward Enterprise scheme, the three governing bodies accused Infantino of “trust broken through deception” and condemned his failure to acknowledge that the proposal should not have been unilaterally launched.

The three confederations are understood to have started preliminary discussions about the organisation of new competitions amid Uefa’s repeated threats to boycott Fifa events. As things stand, next month’s under-20 women’s World Cup could take place without the presence of European teams and alternative options are being sought.

The letter is signed by the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, his AFC counterpart, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, and the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani. Efforts to unite around a suitable candidate to replace Infantino have stepped up since his privately-backed plan was revealed and Montagliani is believed to be among the leading contenders.

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” part of the letter reads. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it. When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

It strongly criticises Fifa’s response to the crisis, which saw a meeting between a small number of senior staff in Rabat followed by an apology from Infantino that appeared not to show remorse for the scheme itself.

View image in fullscreen The Canadian Victor Montagliani consoles Lionel Messi after the World Cup final. He is believed to be interested in running for the Fifa presidency. Photograph: Will Oliver/EPA

“It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment,” the letter says. “It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong. There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the Fifa World Cup was a profound failure of judgment – not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions Fifa exists to serve.”

The three presidents also call for an independent review, conducted by a body outside of football, into the scandal. Fifa had previously committed to presenting a full report to the Fifa Council at its next scheduled meeting. The letter also directly addresses concerns that countries may lose out on financial aid under a different leadership, saying it is “[not] about any member association losing the support it has earned, despite the fearmongering directed at our leadership to suggest otherwise.”

The letter concludes: “There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness … Football’s strength has always been its unity. We call for that unity to be honoured now, with leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Any candidates to run for the Fifa election must announce their bid by 18 November. The confederations are understood to consider all options on the table in their push for Infantino to be replaced, provided they fit within Fifa’s statutes and governance framework.

While the letter outlines the stances of the three confederations, and particularly their leaderships, the story is more complicated within individual member associations. Few outside Europe have been willing to come out publicly against Infantino and only a small minority have been tempted to recall the letters of support they had sent backing his re-election next March. Additionally the influential African and South American confederations, Caf and Conmebol, have both come out backing Infantino in recent days.

A number of larger member associations are understood to have written to Infantino asking for a meeting in which he would be required to explain his actions around the FFE scheme, with no response received so far. Nor has Infantino been in touch personally with federations to address his leading role in the ongoing turmoil.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 2: Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 7th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 4th

Prospects

The image of John McGinn hoisting aloft the Europa League trophy in Istanbul as the confetti cannons fired is crystallised in the minds of Aston Villa supporters, but less than three months on, plenty has changed since one of the club’s greatest days. Three major players from the starting lineup – Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, two of whom scored – have exited, and another may follow if Arsenal make a serious play for the dependable Ezri Konsa.

A key trio of coaches have also left – the set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, assistant manager Pako Ayestarán and the influential individual coach, Antonio Rodríguez Saravia – but most importantly the common denominator and driver of Villa’s incredible rebirth remains in post. It is a good job Unai Emery enjoys a challenge. It has been a typically busy summer, with pre-season trips to Portugal, Indonesia and Hong Kong, plus the Super Cup against Paris St-Germain in Salzburg on Wednesday and a friendly trip to Mönchengladbach to follow, but there is work to do if Emery is to repeat the feat of fourth place and break new ground, again, by securing Champions League qualification for successive campaigns.

After a terrible start, Villa edged over the line last season, but the landscape is unlikely to be so forgiving this time. Nobody played more minutes for Villa than Rogers and it was no surprise Villa’s alarming drop in form around spring coincided with Tielemans being injured. Villa need their replacements to work. João Gomes, a £38m buy from Wolves, looks a smart fit; the tigerish Brazil midfielder made the third-highest number of tackles in the division last season (107) and was fourth on the list for ball recoveries (194). Johan Manzambi is one of the game’s most exciting young talents, while Emery believes he can rehabilitate Alejandro Garnacho, who has joined on a season-long loan from Chelsea.

Only Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester City have amassed more Premier League points in the three-and-a-half years since Emery arrived, and while it would be foolish to write him off, every season his task seems to get that bit harder. He can still call on a core cast of reliable performers in Konsa, McGinn, Matty Cash, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins, while Boubacar Kamara’s return from injury this month is a timely boost. But it is hard not to wonder whether Villa have peaked.

Off-field picture

The response of a senior executive was telling when asked if qualifying for the Champions League makes life easier when it comes to meeting the financial rules. “Not easier but less difficult,” came the reply. Villa have since signed a lucrative shirt sponsorship deal with Visit Rwanda, worth about £20m per season, though Amnesty International warns Rwanda “is using sportswashing to deflect attention from its terrible human rights record”. Meanwhile, Villa Park’s makeover continues with the North Stand closed for the season, the stadium’s capacity falling to 37,000 during its redevelopment. The new-look stand will have a steel roof, modern facade and accommodate more than 50,000 supporters, and will be ready for 2027-28 and Euro 2028.

Owner-fan relationship

Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens will always be adored for putting Villa firmly back on the map, elevating them to become major Premier League players and, ultimately, as the people who gave Emery the keys to transform the club. Both joined the on-field celebrations in Istanbul in May, Sawiris with a claret-and-blue scarf around his neck. Michael Angelakis, chair of investment company Atairos and chief executive of Comcast, acquired a minority stake in 2023. The story goes that Sawiris, Egypt’s richest man, handed Emery a blank sheet of paper and asked him to design his vision when meeting the Basque for the first time in Madrid, at the home of the agent Jorge Mendes.

The manager

“He lives like a monk in a tracksuit,” was how Villa’s director of football operations and Emery’s right-hand man, Damian Vidagany, described the 54-year-old manager’s work ethic in the book Waking The Giant. During the season it is not unusual for Emery, who has an apartment in Birmingham city centre, to spend 12 hours a day at Villa’s Bodymoor Heath base, sometimes analysing footage on his laptop while on the exercise bike or treadmill, long after his players have gone. Emery’s squad have grown accustomed to long meetings, sometimes twice a day – one was held less than 12 hours after cementing their place in the Champions League after beating Liverpool in May, in preparation for Emery to clinch a record fifth Europa League title of his coaching career.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi looks pleased to be wearing the claret and blue. Photograph: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty Images

There were a few nerves at Villa as Manzambi illuminated Switzerland’s World Cup, concerns his price could balloon or that bigger fish may blow them out of the water. But Villa had done their homework and got a longstanding target over the line for a club-record £51m amid interest from rivals. Manzambi was on Villa’s radar long before he impressed against them for Freiburg in the Europa League final. Murat Yakin, the Switzerland head coach, described Manzambi as “a street footballer”, saying the 20-year-old’s humility and quality means he is capable of playing across the pitch. He played regularly as a No 8 in the Bundesliga and Emery is an admirer of his versatility.

Stat attack

Aston Villa scored 15 goals from outside the box last season. Seven teams had recorded more in one of the previous 17 Premier League campaigns, but no side in that period bettered their 8.4% shot conversion rate. As only 3.6% of attempts from this range are converted on average, Villa’s 2025-26 tally feels impossible to repeat.

Set for a breakthrough

It will be interesting to see if the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, son of former Plymouth and Shrewsbury forward Guy, can build on his encouraging pre-season form. Emery and his coaches are big fans of Madjo, a physical striker born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, so no wonder this month Villa welcomed the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) clearing Madjo to feature after Fifa rules prohibited him from playing after joining from Metz in a £10m deal in January. “English player allowed to play in England #freemadjo,” McGinn posted on social media. It has been a whirlwind 12 months for Madjo: he made his Ligue 1 debut last August aged 16, before scoring on debut for England Under-17s a few weeks later. Four goals in pre-season has led to a sense that his first competitive minutes for Villa are close.

World Cup impact

Amadou Onana, whose Villa career has been stop-start owing to injury, ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in Belgium’s last-16 win over the USA. Manzambi enjoyed a fine World Cup, even if his tournament also ended with a knee injury, ruling him out of Switzerland’s last 16 and quarter-final matches and delaying his Villa debut. Martínez made it to another final with Argentina. Konsa started every game for England before the semi-final against Argentina: his 72nd-minute introduction from the bench for Anthony Gordon widely pinpointed as a negative change that invited pressure.

Sports.title: Manchester City closing in on £85m Bouaddi to soften blow of Rodri’s expected exit
Sports.content:
Manchester City are closing in on signing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, with the midfielder’s expected arrival clearing the path for Rodri to join Barcelona.

The 18-year-old has agreed personal terms with City but the club are still finalising the deal with his French club Lille, who value Bouaddi at around €100m (£85m).

City’s new manager, Enzo Maresca, is believed to want to integrate the Moroccan into his first-team squad immediately for the new season. City meet Arsenal in the Community Shield this Sunday before opening their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth on 23 August.

Barcelona are confident of landing Rodri from City but will have to return with an improved offer following an initial €45m bid which was rejected last week. The sale of Ferran Torres, who is of interest to Paris Saint-Germain, would finance Rodri’s purchase. City are all but resigned to the sale of the 30-year-old, who has a year left on his contract.

If the Bouaddi deal can be completed he would join Elliot Anderson, who arrived earlier in the summer from Nottingham Forest for £116m, in Maresca’s new-look midfield, which has also lost the experience of Bernardo Silva this summer.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are interested in Leicester’s coveted teenager Louis Page.
