Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 1: Arsenal
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 1st (NB: this is not necessarily Ed Aarons’ prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st

Prospects

Even losing on penalties in the Champions League final could not take any of the gloss off last season as Arsenal ended their 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions. The celebrations have continued all summer after some wild scenes on the streets of north London on their return from Budapest, although concerns over the fitness of some key players after their exploits at the World Cup are mounting.

Arsenal have acted quickly to reinforce their midfield by signing Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle given Declan Rice’s workload must be managed very carefully after playing through neural pain in his hamstring and lower back since December. The arrival of Greece forward Christos Tzolis to replace Leandro Trossard also looks like a smart piece of business on the left-hand side of the attack. But with Vinícius Junior staying at Real Madrid, despite Arsenal’s best efforts, supporters will be hoping there is still a chance that the sporting director, Andrea Berta, could conjure up a heavyweight attacking signing before the window closes given Bukayo Saka’s fitness problems in recent seasons.

The back injury that will sideline William Saliba for an unknown period could prove even more central to Arsenal’s hopes of retaining their title. A defence that conceded 27 goals last year in the Premier League may struggle without the immense talents of the France defender, even if they can bring in Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa as hoped. Whether Arsenal can maintain their dominance from set pieces over the past two campaigns will also be crucial, with more scrutiny expected from video assistant referees after the fallout from their controversial victory at West Ham in May.

Not since 1935, when Arsenal became the second team to win three successive league titles, have they retained their crown. Having strengthened the deepest squad in the division still further, they will take some stopping again.

Off-field picture

Money definitely isn’t an issue for Stan Kroenke. Arsenal’s co-owner became America’s largest private landowner this year and has spent more than £1.5bn on new players since becoming the majority shareholder in 2011 through his holding company, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE). Next on the agenda is an upgrade to the Emirates Stadium that could increase the capacity of their home to more than 70,000. Talks have begun with the stadium’s original architects, Populous, over a project that could cost up to £500m. The much-criticised shirtsleeve deal with Visit Rwanda ended last season and has been replaced by the HR company Deel, itself controversial in some sections of the Arsenal fanbase, while Emirates have renewed their longstanding partnership until 2033.

Owner-fan relationship

Kroenke and his son Josh – who are co-chairs – clearly revelled in carrying out the Premier League trophy at Selhurst Park before it was presented to the captain, Martin Ødegaard, after Arsenal’s final game of the season in May. Having once been criticised for running the club “like an investment vehicle”, now they are praised for the enormous effect they have made. Kroenke Jr’s promise there would be “no standing still once this season ends” was an ominous sign to their rivals given KSE have a reputation as serial winners in a number of sports in America.

The manager

Mikel Arteta’s expected bumper new contract extension – that will make him one of the best-paid managers in the world – has yet to be confirmed, but there is no doubting his commitment to the cause. The Spaniard could not bear to watch as Manchester City’s challenge collapsed against Bournemouth last season and was in his back garden “building a fire” when Arsenal were confirmed as champions. With Pep Guardiola gone, Arteta has the opportunity to build a new winning dynasty of his own.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen The Gunners fans will be hoping to see Bruno Guimarães’ goal celebration on numerous occasions this season. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

The arrival of Guimarães was another big statement of intent from Arsenal. The former Newcastle captain wants to win more trophies after capturing hearts and minds on Tyneside and he will provide several options in the already well-stacked engine room. As well as relieving the load on Rice, the versatile 28-year-old Brazil midfielder is capable of fulfilling a number of roles, from deep-lying playmaker to box-to box destroyer. While it remains to be seen how Arteta chooses to use Guimarães when he also has Martín Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ødegaard and Mikel Merino at his disposal, his talents will only add to the quality in Arsenal’s squad.

Stat attack

Referees have been told to pay much more attention to grappling during set-pieces this season so it will be interesting to see if this has any effect on Arsenal. Only three teams in the Premier League had a better non-penalty expected goal difference than the Gunners had from set plays alone.

Set for a breakthrough

Max Dowman was a record-breaking revelation as he dipped his toes into senior football for the first time last season and the signs are that the 16-year-old could be handed more opportunities after impressing again during pre-season. A brilliant goal and an assist against Girona capped a man-of-the-match display from the right flank. With Saka and Noni Madueke to be eased back in after returning from World Cup duty, Dowman is ready to add to his solitary Premier League start, against Crystal Palace on the final day of last season, and should appear more regularly in cup competitions.

World Cup impact

Rice and Saka arrived in the United States feeling the effects of a marathon season and it was to their immense credit that they played through the pain barrier and made it to England’s eighth match of the tournament. Only Thomas Tuchel knows why he left Saka on the bench in the semi-final against Argentina and his hat-trick in the third-place playoff a few days later showed how potent he can be even with an achilles problem. Both require an extended break before returning to the rigours of club football and Arsenal will give them as long as possible. But such is their importance that it will be sooner rather than later.

Sports.title: Arsenal step up push for defensive cover with Timber and Saliba sidelined
Sports.content:
Arsenal are stepping up their efforts to sign defensive cover for William Saliba after Mikel Arteta revealed Jurriën Timber is well away from returning to competitive action. Saliba will be sidelined for an extended period after breaking down during the World Cup with a back injury.

After Arsenal lost a second successive friendly when Borussia Dortmund won 3-2 on Sunday to lift the Emirates Cup in a performance that featured several defensive mistakes, Arteta would not be drawn on when the France defender is expected to return, but said it would take “some time to heal”.

There are also concerns over Timber, who pulled out of the Netherlands squad on the eve of the World Cup after failing to recover from a persistent groin injury that led him to miss most of the run-in last season.

“Jurriën is progressing really well,” Arteta said. “He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now, but it’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.

“William Saliba is in rest mode at the moment for two weeks. He had to do almost nothing, an aggravated injury, so it’s going to take some time to heal.”

Pressed on how Arsenal will cope without Saliba, he said: “We have experienced that in the past, unfortunately. When he’s been available, he’s hit home and the stats are incredible. We know we lost a massive player, the same with Jurriën.”

Arsenal have had a bid for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa rejected and are expected to return with a new offer for the England defender, who is also capable of playing at right-back. Villa value him at £60m, but with less than two years left on his contract Arsenal are unwilling to pay that much for the 28-year-old. The Premier League champions have also shown an interest in signing Cristian Romero from Tottenham, but any move for the Argentina defender is extremely unlikely given Spurs’ reluctance to sell to their north London rivals.

Arteta, who started with Cristhian Mosquera in central defence alongside Gabriel Magalhães against Dortmund, said Arsenal’s existing players must get up to speed before Sunday’s Community Shield against Manchester City, but did not rule out bringing in another defender.

“It has to be the right player in the market to make us much better,” he said. “We conceded some poor goals today, in the way we competed especially. But that’s a collective responsibility. So we need to improve with the players we have.”

Sports.title: Van Dijk looks forward to more quality arriving at Liverpool before new season
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk is ready to welcome Ronald Araújo as his new centre-back partner at Liverpool with the deal to sign the Barcelona defender almost complete.

Van Dijk played almost an hour, his first pre-season appearance, as Liverpool were beaten 3-2 by Monaco at Anfield, having led 2-0. The Dutchman fouled Aleksandr Golovin to concede a penalty just before the break, which Golovin scored.

Jérémy Jacquet remained absent, with Liverpool’s new £50m arrival being treated with kid gloves after an injury-hit spell at the end of last season with Rennes. Araújo has been signed to bolster Andoni Iraola’s defensive options, with Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni also sidelined.

“Any player that arrives at the club we will be welcoming,” Van Dijk said of Araújo. “I have no idea if it has been announced or not. I have not seen him so let’s see.”

Van Dijk was upbeat about Jacquet and the prospect of more transfer activity between now and the transfer deadline on 1 September. Liverpool are keen on adding to their forward line with Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola of interest.

“Let’s see what the next couple of weeks are going to bring. Any quality we can add to the team will definitely be welcome so let’s see.

“I’ve not seen any of him. I’ve spoken to him,” Van Dijk said of Jacquet. “I’ve seen him walking around and we have conversations. I can’t wait to see him back on the pitch and I hope that happens very soon. I’m not a doctor, so I don’t know exactly the situation, but I have a feeling this week he could be back on the pitch, hopefully as soon as possible.”

While Van Dijk accepted Liverpool are in a transition period after the sacking of Arne Slot, he revealed he has been in regular contact with Iraola and offered his full support to the new head coach.

Van Dijk said: “We had a great conversation in the first week when it got announced and the main thing for him to know is I am here for him regardless, anything he needs, wants to know, wants me to do for the team or whatever. Hopefully we will be successful this season.

“Nothing to take away from Arne and his staff, we had an amazing time together, but obviously last year [was] a disappointment. This year we have a new manager who has new ways of preparation, so we have to adapt to the new staff, different training methods. I liked working under Arne and I am sure I will like working under the new manager.”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Endrick set for Villa loan? De Jong offered in Rodri deal?
Sports.content:
A sense of excitement is what Aston Villa need at the moment after selling off key players. What better way to create it than signing a prodigious talent from Real Madrid? The Villans have inquired about the Brazilian Endrick, who impressed on loan at Lyon last season, and may make a similar temporary move to the Premier League.

Manchester City are not particularly keen to sell Rodri but, with a year left on his contract money may well talk, especially if the midfielder wants to leave. Barcelona’s first bid was rejected but they are readying another. One idea is to offer Frenkie de Jong as part of the deal, so at least Enzo Maresca would have a shiny new midfielder to play with.

One player who could be leaving Camp Nou is the World Cup-winning goalscorer Ferran Torres, who has reportedly told Paris Saint-Germain he wants to pop across to the French capital. Not that a deal between the clubs has been agreed.

Another potential swap deal is on the cards between Everton and Crystal Palace. Calls have been made to discuss Dwight McNeil moving to Selhurst Park and Brennan Johnson swapping places with him at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The two wingers have struggled for game time perhaps a swap would reignite their careers. McNeil almost ended up at Selhurst Park in January before a late breakdown in talks left the player and his family furious.

Promoted Ipswich have been active in the market and could add the Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Exequiel Palacios. A bid has been faxed over, leaving the Tractor Boys to play the waiting game, but they may face competition for his signature.

After what must have been a lot of wrangling, Chelsea have agreed to loan Filip Jörgensen to sister club Strasbourg. The Blues are well-stocked with players and need to bin a few who can’t be sent to Strasbourg, so they may allow Jamie Gittens to head on loan to Roma.

The departure of Bruno Guimarães will prompt a rethink at Newcastle, who rather desperately need a new central midfielder. Sandro Tonali was sold a while back, giving the club some cash to play with, but they still seem to be thinking about signing João Palhinha who is not wanted at Bayern Munich The former Tottenham man Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is another option. Palhinha is also of interest to Aston Villa, who have made contact with the Bundesliga champions.

Manchester United are planning for the future with a move for the Leicester teenager Louis Page. The 18-year-old came through the academy ranks with the Foxes, but is naturally more than happy to take the leap from League One.

Sports.title: José Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013
Sports.content:
José Mourinho has revealed he signed a contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager in 2013 only to tearfully renege on the deal and return to Chelsea.

The football world was rocked when the Scottish great announced he was retiring having overseen a 13th Premier League title triumph during a spell of unrivalled dominance at Old Trafford.

United have failed to return to the top of the English game since Ferguson stepped down, with his successor, David Moyes, sacked after only 10 months in charge.

Mourinho was later brought in, spending two and a half years in charge from 2016, but revealed in a new Netflix documentary about his life that he had agreed to come earlier.

“I go to Chelsea in 2013 but in that period there is something nobody knows,” the Portuguese said in the documentary, which is entitled Mourinho. “I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth, and I think the objective of this work that we are doing is to tell the truth. When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.”

Mourinho continued: “I was, of course, very flattered, because Manchester United has an incredible appeal. When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

double quotation mark He phoned me and he was crying. He says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea.’ Sir Alex Ferguson

“But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football and, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved.”

Ferguson was one of the footballing figures interviewed for the new documentary and admits he was under the illusion Mourinho was accepting the offer, only for the situation to change in a matter of hours.

“Early evening he phoned me and he was crying,” the United great said. “And he says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word.’ The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

Mourinho had a strong bond with Chelsea after leading them to two Premier League titles, an FA Cup and two League Cups during his first spell.

View image in fullscreen Alex Ferguson’s long spell as Manchester United manager ended in May 2013. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

The Portuguese parked differences with the Chelsea owner, Roman Abramovich, to return to Stamford Bridge after leaving Real Madrid, winning another league crown and League Cup before being sacked in December 2015.

“For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic, but I don’t regret because it was a decision that I made with my heart,” Mourinho, now back in charge of Real Madrid, said.

“And I think it is nature that says something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it’s nature. I did it for love.

“I went back with the feeling of, yes, I go home, but with big responsibility because what I did before is history, and you don’t want to destroy your legacy.”

Sports.title: Where to watch UEFA Super Cup: Unai Emery forced to make line-up decision early as Aston Villa begin ‘new era’
Sports.content:
Where to watch UEFA Super Cup: Unai Emery forced to make line-up decision early as Aston Villa begin ‘new era’

The first European trophy of the 2026/27 campaign will be claimed this week as Aston Villa take on Paris Saint-Germain.

PSG won the UEFA Super Cup last year, having lifted their first-ever Champions League title a few months earlier.



3 PSG won the Super Cup last year by beating Spurs on penalties Credit: Getty

And the French giants are back in the big game again, beating Arsenal on penalties to go back-to-back in UEFA's elite competition.

They took on Premier League opposition in Tottenham last time they were here - now they take on another English side.

Aston Villa come up against the Ligue 1 champions after beating Freiburg to win the Europa League last season.



Unai Emery proved his expertise in the competition yet again, as Villa got their hands on their first European trophy since 1982.

But as he aims to claim another title on the continent, he is going to be without his new £51million signing Johan Manzambi.



Manzambi, who starred at the World Cup with Switzerland this summer, joined the club following a transfer hijack.

The 20-year-old opted to sign for Villa over Newcastle, but arrived in the West Midlands carrying a knee injury - and due to that, he has been left out of the squad for the Super Cup completely, so won't be part of the line-up.



It has been reported that there is no definitive return date for Manzambi, but he's expected to be out for weeks, not months.

Villa will hope they can succeed without their new man, as Emery admitted that he feels as if a 'new era' has begun at the club.

"I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies," he said. "We’re trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it: winning trophies."

3 Villa's new midfielder Manzambi is not fit enough to feature in the Super Cup Credit: Getty



Where to watch UEFA Super Cup

The 2026 UEFA Super Cup will take place on Wednesday, August 12.

It will be played at the Red Bull Arena in Salzburg, Austria, with kick-off set for 8pm in the UK, which is 9pm local time.

Fans can watch the action between PSG and Aston Villa live on TV via TNT Sports and stream online via HBO Max.

The French giants are already the reigning champions, having beaten Tottenham on spot-kicks in the Super Cup last year.

This time around, they take on Aston Villa, who won their first European title since 1982 in the Europa League.

Unai Emery has added some new faces since tasting glory against Freiburg in May, including Alejandro Garnacho.



Garnacho has started in his two Villa appearances so far in pre-season, but has he impressed enough to start in the Super Cup?

Emi Buendia, Evan Guessand and Alysson will all challenge for the left-wing spot, along with the ex-Manchester United star.

PSG vs Aston Villa: What has been said?

Speaking ahead of the Super Cup, Villa boss Emery said: "I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies.

"[The Super Cup is] very important," he said. "We’re trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it: winning trophies.

"To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain – the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with."

On Luis Enrique and PSG, Emery added: "His teams always play well.

"The relationship I have with him, built through competing against each other, in the same way that I feel proud of the work I do and how we evolve, I also feel like it’s a great challenge to face the best coaches in the world.



"For me, competing against [Pep] Guardiola is magnificent, competing against Luis Enrique is magnificent. Why? Because they demand a lot of me, they motivate me a lot.

"Based on the full respect I have for managers, that respect is even greater when competing against them, which means that I want to fight to beat them, as I look at them as the best."

Sports.title: Wrexham agree £8m deal to sign new No. 1 goalkeeper from Premier League club
Sports.content:
Wrexham agree £8m deal to sign new No. 1 goalkeeper from Premier League club

Wrexham have agreed an £8million deal with Sunderland for goalkeeper Anthony Patterson, talkSPORT understands.

The 26-year-old was ousted as the Black Cats' starting gloveman last term following the arrival of Robin Roefs.



2 Patterson has three-and-a-half seasons of Championship experience under his belt Credit: Getty

Patterson was subsequently sent out on loan to Millwall for the second half of the 2025/26 Championship campaign, where he made 14 appearances across all competitions.

And he's now set to call the second tier home once more, albeit with Wrexham.

Patterson will now have to battle Danny Ward and Arthur Okonkwo for the starting role between the sticks at the Racecourse Ground.



Which other players have joined Wrexham this summer?

He represents the Welsh side's third piece of business this summer following the arrivals of Danny Imray and Ben Whiteman.

Imray moved to Wrexham from Crystal Palace in a deal worth approximately £5m while Whiteman arrived from Preston North End for £3m, although he was accused of 'crossing the line' by Paul Heckingbottom to make the deal happen.



Wrexham go into the 2026/27 campaign hoping to improve on their seventh-place finish from last term, where they finished just two points outside of the play-offs.

However, under new EFL rules, teams that finish seventh and eighth in the Championship this term will qualify for the play-offs.



The expanded format was first announced in March, with the third and fourth-placed teams advancing straight to the semi-finals while teams that finish between fifth and eighth will compete in one-off eliminator matches.

Phil Parkinson's side have already commenced the 2026/27 season, slipping to a 1-0 loss away to Middlesbrough in their Carabao Cup first round tie last Friday.

Will Lankshear's 61st-minute strike was all that separated the two sides at the Riverside.

2 Wrexham are building for yet another promotion push Credit: Getty



Phil Parkinson's reaction to Wrexham's Carabao Cup loss to Middlesbrough

Despite the defeat, Parkinson viewed the contest as a valuable opportunity to get some much-needed competitive minutes into his players.

"The lads will come on enormously for tonight's game physically," Parkinson said following the match.

"It was always going to be a test for us, and we've had to manage some of the players' minutes - that was pre-decided - but we'll get them back and have a good week now.

"We got the two new lads (Imray and Whiteman) some minutes, which is important."



Wrexham will face League One side Wigan Athletic in a behind-closed-doors friendly on Monday before their Championship campaign gets underway on August 17 against fellow Welsh side Cardiff City.

Sports.title: Troy Parrott told to reject Premier League for Championship – but he casts doubt on transfer
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott told to reject Premier League for Championship – but he casts doubt on transfer

Troy Parrott has seemingly poured cold water on a potential move to West Ham, claiming the 'football world is a lot bigger than England.'

talkSPORT understands the Hammers are making a strong push to sign Parrott, who has netted an impressive 51 goals in the last two seasons for Dutch side AZ Alkmaar.

3 Parrott finished joint-third in the Eredivisie Golden Boot standings with 16 goals Credit: Getty

However, West Ham don't necessarily have a clear run at the Republic of Ireland international.

It is also understood Fulham, Ajax, PSV Eindhoven, Real Betis and Como have all expressed an interest in Parrott, who was previously on Tottenham's books for seven years.

Even though the Hammers may be leading the race, Parrott is not as hot on a return to England as he once used to be.

What did Troy Parrott say about rumours linking him back to England?

In an interview with Dutch publication De Telegraaf, the 24-year-old admitted his move to AZ has opened his eyes to football beyond English shores.

"Before I went to the Netherlands, I was completely focused on England," Parrott said.

"I dreamed of the Premier League.

"But once in the Netherlands, I discovered that the football world is a lot bigger than England."

PSV, Como and Betis' interest may be particularly intriguing for Parrott given the trio can all offer Champions League football this season.

Betis return to Europe's premier club competition for the first time in over two decades while Como, led by Cesc Fabregas, will make their Champions League debut.

As for Fulham, Parrott would join at the dawn of a new era given Alvaro Arbeloa is the new man in charge.

3 Parrott made headlines this year after inspiring Ireland at the World Cup play-offs Credit: Sportsfile

Parrott would also have competition for a starting role given the Cottagers acquired striker Gonzalo Garcia, who earned his first cap with Spain in June, from Real Madrid earlier this summer.

A move to West Ham would have Parrott tasked with helping the club secure an instant return to the Premier League following their relegation.

Andy Townsend's verdict on Troy Parrott being linked to West Ham

Although the Hammers are in the second tier of English football, Andy Townsend is adamant a player of Parrott's ilk would tear it up.

"Good finisher, Troy Parrott," Townsend said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"He definitely has that knack of being in and around where that ball is going to drop. He sees it, he recognises it and when he gets there, he can finish, he really can. He's done very well in Holland."

Townsend added: "Honestly, I think someone like Troy can work at a club like West Ham.

3 Nuno Espirito Santo is looking to win promotion from the Championship for the second time in his career with West Ham Credit: Getty

"(Taty) Castellanos is full of running, Troy is not that sort of player, he doesn't want to charge around all over the place.

"But when it comes in the box and there's others in there with him, he seems to get a yard of space and he can finish."

Sports.title: John Terry admits Jose Mourinho spied on another team while at Chelsea in shock revelation
Sports.content:
John Terry admits Jose Mourinho spied on another team while at Chelsea in shock revelation

John Terry has revealed that Jose Mourinho obtained footage of a Bolton Wanderers training session to aid Chelsea's Premier League title chances.

The Portuguese manager ended Chelsea's 50-year league-title drought during his first stint at Stamford Bridge after guiding the west London outfit to the trophy in 2005.

3 Mourinho heavily relied on Terry during Chelsea's golden era Credit: AFP

Terry became the Blues' permanent captain under Mourinho, going on to lead the team to five English top-flight titles during his 13-year reign as skipper.

He had two spells at Stamford Bridge, with the first ending in 2007 before re-joining in 2013. Mourinho even reneged on an agreement to join Man United to head back to west London.

The legendary captain spoke in Netflix's new documentary on Mourinho's golden era at Stamford Bridge, and claimed how his former manager used unusual methods at Cobham.

Years prior to Southampton's infamous 'Spygate' scandal, details have now emerged on how video analysis played a part under Mourinho's regime.

The tactic was spearheaded by a young Andre Villas-Boas, who would later go on to manage both the Blues and Tottenham.

Villa-Boas said: "That was something of a quantum leap in the field of match analysis.

"Not many people were doing it at the same level we were doing it at the time.

"That was in the era of the old DVD players, which would sometimes malfunction, and Jose would smash the projector or the DVD player out of sheer passion!"

Did spying on teams help?

Terry detailed one specific incident prior to a meeting against Sam Allardyce's Bolton Wanderers.

The former defender shared: "We were watching a video, and suddenly Sam Allardyce appeared in Bolton's training, saying: hit Gallas, he's not good in the air.

3 Mourinho is regarded as Chelsea's greatest ever manager Credit: Getty

"He was spitting and talking in that way through the microphone. It was like, my goodness, who gets footage from someone's training ground? I still don't know where Mourinho got this footage!"

Allardyce managed Bolton for eight seasons, securing their promotion back to the Premier League after a three-year absence.

The former England boss even achieved European football with the northern club, as Bolton went on to finish sixth place in 2005.

However, despite that successful era for the Wanderers, they were still unable to beat Mourinho's Chelsea - a run that included a 5-1 thrashing by the Blues in their second Premier League-winning season.

Mourinho's managerial tactics

Terry confirmed he would have been prepared to be carried out in a 'coffin' for his former manager.

The duo spent five-and-a-half seasons together across two spells, winning three titles, three League Cups and one FA Cup.

The former England defender recalled how his boss would ignore him during training whenever he was injured, which led to the former Chelsea skipper to taking painkilling injections to continue playing.

3 Mourinho and Terry won eight trophies together over two spells at Stamford Bridge

Terry admitted: "For him [Mourinho], I would give everything. I would leave that pitch in a coffin for him."

Behind Mourinho's stern media image, Terry insisted there was a softer side and would often ask the players to bring their children to the training ground on Sundays.

Terry formed the backbone of Mourinho's army and described playing under him as 'going into battle.'

He concluded: "There was a picture of the Premier League hanging in the dressing room.

"From those first team meetings, to the very first game against Man United, the words and the terminology he would use in those meetings…like: ‘We are going to f*** them. We are going to win the league. We are going to take the trophy off them this year’. And we did."

Sports.title: What time is 2026 UEFA Super Cup? World Cup banned referee to oversee PSG vs Aston Villa
Sports.content:
What time is 2026 UEFA Super Cup? World Cup banned referee to oversee PSG vs Aston Villa

One of the opening games of the 2026/27 campaign is a clash between the two leading European champions this week.

Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain take on Europa League victors Aston Villa in the UEFA Super Cup on Wednesday night.

3 PSG won their second consecutive Champions League, returning to the Super Cup Credit: Getty

PSG defeated Arsenal in the final of UEFA's elite competition, claiming the title for the second straight year by sinking the Gunners.

The French giants beat the Premier League champions on penalties following a 1-1 draw, as Gabriel sent his decisive spot-kick over.

They are also the reigning Super Cup winners after beating Tottenham in the game last term, so they are aiming to go back-to-back in this clash.

As for Aston Villa, they won the Europa League with a comfortable 3-0 win over German side Freiburg in Istanbul.

This will be Villa's first Super Cup appearance since 1983, having historically won their first European title in 44 years.

Somali referee Omar Artan was appointed as the lead official for the match after he was denied entry to the United States to officiate at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

When is the 2026 UEFA Super Cup?

The 2026 UEFA Super Cup will be played this Wednesday - August 12.

Kick-off is set for 8pm UK time, which is 9pm local time.

It will be held at the Red Bull Arena in Salzburg, Austria.

This is the first time a UEFA final has been played at this stadium, which is the home of Austrian giants Red Bull Salzburg.

3 Aston Villa are going to take on PSG after winning the Europa League last season Credit: Getty

The venue staged multiple games at EURO 2008 and will become the 14th ground to host the match since the competition switched from being hosted every year in Monaco 13 years ago.

Adrian Durham will be your host, while commentary comes from Joe Shennan and former Aston Villa captain Andy Townsend.

Sports.title: Ex-PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan dead at 45 as loved ones mourn tragic loss: 'Rest easy, Matty'
Sports.content:
Ex-PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan dead at 45 as loved ones mourn tragic loss: 'Rest easy, Matty'

Golf is mourning the loss of former PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan following his shock death at the age of just 45.

The Canadian, who was described as 'a respected golfer, devoted son, hilarious brother, and friend,' turned professional in 2003 after playing college golf at Oklahoma State and Georgia.

He later secured his place among golf's elite and went on to compete in 32 PGA Tour events, securing three top-10 finishes as a rookie.

But according to an obituary, he passed away on Wednesday surrounded by his family at a hospital in Ontario, Canada. No cause of death was listed.

'Whether on the course or in everyday life, he had a remarkable ability to bring people together, offering encouragement, laughter, and genuine friendship to everyone he met,' it read, per the Kingston Whig-Standard.

'His welcoming personality and unwavering kindness made him a beloved figure within Kingston's golfing community and beyond.'

Golf is mourning the loss of former PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan following his shock death

He passed away on Wednesday surrounded by his family at a hospital in Ontario, Canada

McQuillan's father, Mark, began teaching him how to swing a club at the age of 10 before he went on to reach the Canadian Tour and then the PGA Tour.

'Matt developed lifelong friendships while mentoring anyone who loved the game of golf,' his obituary continued.

'He will be deeply missed by many and his spirit, love and compassion will be remembered every day. Rest easy, Matty. We love you.'

Golf Canada added in a tribute that it 'joins the Canadian golf community in mourning the passing of Matt McQuillan... one of Canada's most promising young golfers in the late 1990s.'

According to the PGA Tour, the 45-year-old returned to his hometown of Kingston, Ontario, to teach golf, 'helping introduce and develop the next generation of Canadian golfers.'

McQuillan's best PGA Tour result came at the 2011 John Deere Classic when he shot a final-round 64 to finish in a tie for third behind winner Steve Stricker.

Sports.title: UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC presidents accuse Gianni Infantino of 'deception' in open letter demanding FIFA president is held accountable for failed plot to sell the World Cup
Sports.content:
'Dear Football Family,

'Football is the world’s greatest shared passion. It belongs to no individual and no institution.

'It belongs to the players, the fans, the clubs, the Member Associations and every institution entrusted with safeguarding its future.

'It is in that spirit, as confederations representing its members, that we speak collectively today.

'The growth over the past decade has been real. But that progress was never the work of one individual. It was the product of FIFA, the Confederations, the Member Associations, and the thousands of people who dedicate their lives to the game.

'The expanded tournaments, the awarding of the 2030 and 2034 FIFA World Cups, the distribution of resources to associations. These were shared achievements, agreed together, delivered together.

'This is not about money. The Confederations have already called for the responsible distribution of FIFA's vast existing reserves to further strengthen investment in the development of Member Associations.

'Nor is it about any Member Association losing the support it has earned, despite the fearmongering directed at our membership to suggest otherwise. Nor is it about revisiting the expansion of competitions, World Cup allocations, or any other decisions reached collectively. Those decisions were made together, and they must stand.

'This is about something more fundamental: the integrity of the game, and the integrity of those elected to lead it.

'Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.

'When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.

'FIFA's recent letter to its Vice-Presidents and 211 Member Associations acknowledges that mistakes were made in the process. It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment. A proposal advanced on a compressed timeline, without meaningful consultation, and pushed toward a deadline before Member Associations could properly review its terms is not the product of an oversight — it is the product of a design intended to limit scrutiny.

'It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong. There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgment — not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve.

'FIFA has also committed to presenting a full report on these events to the FIFA Council, once again failing to recognize that proper governance in the face of such a profound lack of judgment would require that such a review be conducted by a fully independent third party, not by FIFA itself, its staff, or by any stakeholder within football. The FIFA administration should play no role in conducting the review.

'As per previous correspondence, all relevant documents and records must be preserved in accordance with UEFA’s communication on preservation of documents.

'FIFA's own letter also confirms that only one elected official was present at the leadership meeting in Morocco. No FIFA Council members or Member Associations were invited to participate. Only the management committee, composed of FIFA-employed senior staff, was present.

'This recent meeting, where a select number of members of the FIFA Management Committee—not the full Committee—were summoned abroad, rather than leadership going to Zurich to address the heart of FIFA, its staff, only reinforces these concerns and represents a continuation of the very pattern of conduct that brought us to this moment. It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him.

'There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness.

'These are not the qualities football deserves in its leadership. That is why we have taken this stance: not lightly and not alone, but together, and out of duty to the game we serve.

'Football’s strength has always been its unity. We call for that unity to be honoured now, for leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.'

Sports.title: T10 proposal is a cry for help from counties who know they're heading for a 'cliff edge' - here's what it reveals about the future for the haves and have nots of the county game, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
The suggestion by the new chairman of Sussex that a T10 competition may be one way of easing the financial concerns of the non-Hundred counties isn't just a sign of the times. It's a cry for help.

The ECB have insisted all along that the funds raised at last year's auction, when the Hundred was valued at £975million, would bankroll domestic red-ball cricket for a generation – an apparently powerful retort to the traditionalists who fear the tournament will devour England's 18-team domestic setup.

But the ECB's narrative does not tell the whole story. Far from it. In April, Daily Mail Sport revealed details of a secret meeting at Northamptonshire's Wantage Road involving nine of the 11 non-Hundred-hosting counties.

The mood was gloomy, with the clubs – almost all of them loss-making – worried about the growing divide between them and the seven host counties, a divide they worry will only grow once the Hundred's private investors demand a greater slice of a new TV deal for 2029, and the best players migrate inevitably to the richest clubs.

And while the non-host counties can in theory access around £25million each following the Hundred windfall, that money has to be spent on projects approved by the ECB, such as paying off structured debt or improving infrastructure.

One source who attended the meeting, held without the knowledge of the ECB, said: 'The feeling was that all the clubs are heading to a cliff edge at various speeds. They will all fall over one after the other if something is not addressed in the short term.'

Sussex are proposing a T10 competition to supposedly help non-Hundred hosting counties

And that is where Ed Warner, the new Sussex chair, comes in. Sussex were one of two non-host counties (along with Durham) to miss the secret meeting, and for good reason: they have spent much of the year trying to unravel the financial mess that led to them being placed in special measures, and docked points in all three county competitions.

After telling The Guardian that the Hundred had 'not rescued us in any way, shape or form', Warner captured the mood that day at Wantage Road by considering ways a non-host county might stage more cricket, and make more money, during the Hundred's nearly month-long duration – a period, at the height of summer and during the school holidays, when clubs are staging only four home Metro Bank 50-over matches.

Warner wondered: 'Why couldn't you have a T10 triangular competition with Kent and Essex, for example? Make it very kid-friendly, make it a day at the seaside, then go and play at Canterbury, then go and play in Chelmsford.'

His suggestion, though not itself discussed at the meeting, deserves full marks for lateral thinking. But it should concern cricket lovers on a few counts.

The first is that it would further complicate an already insane schedule, in which the response to the introduction of a fourth format – the Hundred – has been to stage it at the same time as the 50-over competition, diminishing a format in which England are now international also-rans. Our calendar is already full to bursting, without a fifth format trying to elbow its way in.

The second is that T10 feels like part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom. Yes, Abu Dhabi has been hosting its own T10 tournament since 2017, but it has made headlines mainly for reasons of corruption, both proven and alleged. If the Hundred feels like a hurry, T10 is a sprint. What next: F5, or the toss of a coin?

The third concern, and the most significant, is that Warner felt the need to air the suggestion in the first place.

Forget for a moment the financial incompetence at Hove that last week led business management consultancy firm Campbell Tickell to suggest an overhaul of the Sussex board 'as soon as is practically possible'.

The format would complicate an already insane schedule and be part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom

What matters is that the smaller counties are having to countenance alternative means of paying the bills at a time when the ECB tell us the game is richer than ever.

As one chief executive put it at the Northampton meeting, the promise of Hundred money has generated more uncertainty, not less, because of the unknown impact on the next broadcast rights deal.

The ECB will blanch at the idea of counties coming up with their own fifth-format schemes, since it would entail an admission of failure by the board. But Sussex's T10 musings are the symptom of a wider malaise – no matter the repeated insistence that the Hundred will save English cricket.

Unless the ECB get to grips with the smaller clubs' concerns, there will be more desperate ideas where that one came from.

Sports.title: Tracking private jets, Andrea Berta holding his nerve and a last-ditch plea from Matthias Jaissle: This is how Bruno Guimaraes became an Arsenal player - and why Mikel Arteta was so desperate to get him
Sports.content:
The back-and-forth over whether Arsenal and Newcastle are actually in talks, the plane trackings and the staunch denials in the North East are finally at an end.

Bruno Guimaraes is an Arsenal player, theirs for £75million, and a transfer saga which has dragged on for weeks, much to the entertainment of rival fans, is over. Mikel Arteta has his man, a player he’s long admired and been desperate to sign.

This transfer has been an exhausting process, and far from straightforward. But Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has come out of it looking incredibly shrewd, having pulled off a relative ‘bargain’ in the current climate.

Guimaraes' long journey to Arsenal started back in June. As Daily Mail Sport reported on June 24, the Brazilian had instructed agents to find him a new club and Newcastle were braced for an offer from the Gunners. Their interest had been registered.

Newcastle’s response was bullish. He wasn’t going anywhere, according to sources at the club. Given his status as captain and the player’s quality, Guimaraes’ value was enormous – particularly in light of the departures of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. They did not need to sell.

Money talks, however. Newcastle had briefed that they wanted closer to £100million, but internally there was acceptance that an offer of around £75million would see progress.

Bruno Guimaraes has joined Arsenal in a protracted £75million move from Newcastle

The transfer saga is finally over, with Guimaraes' long journey to Arsenal starting back in June

A force of nature.



Guimaraes is a Gunner ✍️ pic.twitter.com/E7k4mIHICg — Arsenal (@Arsenal) August 8, 2026

At Arsenal, they were willing to dig their heels in over the price, in the knowledge that Guimaraes really wanted the move. He had agreed personal terms with the Gunners last month and informed Newcastle of his desire to leave if a suitable offer came in.

There were also optics at play. Newcastle didn’t want to be seen as letting their talisman and a fan favourite leave without putting up a fight. Their fans would rightly have felt aggrieved.

So the negotiations dragged on, largely involving agent Kia Joorabchian. Newcastle would claim there had been no formal contact from Arsenal and felt bewildered by the process, relayed in reports of no direct contact between the clubs.

This conflict in media coverage added to the increasing frenzy attached to a potential move.

Weeks went by, before a real acceleration came last week. As Daily Mail Sport reported on Friday, July 31, a deal had been agreed in principle with a date reserved for the medical. Though a few sticking points remained.

Newly-appointed Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle also decided he wanted a final chance to try to convince the Brazilian to stay put.

Guimaraes travelled to Newcastle’s La Manga training base in Spain on Monday, before waiting for permission to leave and have his medical at Arsenal after telling Jaissle of his desire to move.

The initial reports that he failed to arrive on Sunday resulted in social media sleuths tracking flights to see if Guimaraes was in the air. It had all got a bit mad.

Even the Arsenal players were braced for the move. When Riccardo Calafiori was asked about Guimaraes’ impending transfer on Wednesday night after Arsenal’s 3-1 defeat by Real Betis in Dublin, he turned to the press officer and asked: ‘Is it official yet, no?’

Berta is a tough negotiator. He loathes to overpay, which in this market is extremely hard not to do.

Arsenal had wanted to pay a smaller fee for the Brazil midfielder, who turns 29 in November, while Newcastle demanded a minimum of £80million.

That Arsenal decided to play the long game and stick to their guns frustrated some of their supporters. But the club were never in doubt of the end result.

Newly-appointed manager Matthias Jaissle made a last ditch plea to persuade him to stay

Arsenal chief Andrea Berta held his nerve on the transfer fee throughout negotiations

It’s a smart deal in a market which has, as one agent claimed, ‘gone out of control’. As Daily Mail Sport reported last week, even kids as young as 16 are being paid £20,000 a week, as in the case of Man City’s Mishel Nduka.

In the senior ranks, Chelsea bought Morgan Rogers for £117million, while Spurs splashed out £100million on Tonali.

The strategy of Arsenal and Berta has paid off - after they walked away from Rogers because their valuation of the player had been far exceeded.

The deal for Guimaraes represents value for money - and it is one Berta deserves credit for.

An Arsenal midfield, which was already dominant, now looks even more menacing. Alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard, Guimaraes completes a formidable trio.

Rice provides the ability to cover acres of space, while also being a threat going forward and strong defensively. Odegaard is in charge of creating chances in the final third.

Guimaraes, meanwhile, is an all-round No 8 who can affect games at both ends of the pitch, and brings an aggressive edge. His attempts at more ambitious passes will add some unpredictability the Gunners lack at times.

And so, after weeks of twists, denials and negotiations behind the scenes, the saga is finally over. Guimaraes is an Arsenal player – and Newcastle’s fight to keep their captain has achieved nothing more than a sizeable cheque.

Sports.title: Former Premier League bad boy Nile Ranger claims he got into a fight with Andros Townsend on England duty after the ex-Crystal Palace star 'spat in his pasta'
Sports.content:
Nile Ranger has claimed he and Andros Townsend were involved in a heated altercation while representing England as youngsters on international duty.

Despite never representing the Three Lions at senior level, Ranger scored six goals in 11 appearances for England's U19s after bursting on to the scene as a teenager.

The former Newcastle prodigy, 35, revealed on a podcast this week that he once clashed with fellow ex-England youth star Townsend while the pair were sharing a room in Ukraine on international duty.

'He wasn't playing and getting in the team at the time, but he's a man where he's stretching at night time and keeping himself ready,' Ranger told Undr the Cosh.

'I've played but I didn't play the best. And I'm like to Andros, "Look, just go to sleep man, just relax. You're stretching and doing all of this but your chance will come". I'm actually genuinely telling him that, I'm being real.

'He's like, "You what? Did you see how you played today? You had a stinker, I don't want to play like that. I've got to make sure I'm stretched out and ready".

Ex-Newcastle star Nile Ranger (left) has claimed he and Andros Townsend (right) were involved in a heated altercation while representing England as youngsters on international duty

The forward was once regarded as one of Newcastle's brightest prospects as a teenager

'I don't know why he was coming at me. Take your anger out on someone else bro because I'm not the one. I'll just knock you out and then it's just long (not worth it).

'Anyway, we go down for food the next day and, you remember those old-school blue Lucozade bottles with the yellow top, he's drinking from it and he's spitting in my pasta. I'm looking around at players and being like - are you witnessing this as well? This is crazy antics right now.'

Continuing the anecdote, Ranger claims he and Townsend went upstairs and started brawling, surrounded by team-mates including former England international Kyle Walker.

'I can see Andros there, I'm on to Andros, and I've just crashed him,' Ranger added, making a punching gesture. 'His head hits the bin and man are trying to stop me, Kyle Walker trying to stop me, but the rage inside is just going mad, going berserk.

'We got split up, he's gone to his room. I don't know if the coaches found out about it but I've gone back later and he's like, "Look, let me stop you, I'm sorry. I think just being out here is getting to me and what not".

'I know how it feels. It's like when you get an injury or something and you're not playing. Or you feel like you can play and aren't getting the chance. It was just anger built up, that sort of thing.'

After off-field issues derailed his career, he ended up playing for a string of non league clubs

🚨 NEW SERIES OUT TOMORROW 🚨



Nile Ranger looks back on clashing with Andros Townsend while on England U19s duty 🥊 pic.twitter.com/LcqRCA5Q2n — UndrTheCosh (@UndrTheCosh) August 9, 2026

Once regarded as one of Newcastle's brightest young prospects, Ranger's off-field behaviour repeatedly overshadowed and ultimately derailed his career.

As a teenager, he spent time in a young offenders’ institution following an armed robbery, and his early professional years were subsequently punctuated by disciplinary problems and run-ins with the law.

After Newcastle opted not to renew his contract in 2013 after a string of off-pitch controversies, Ranger moved to Swindon Town before spells at Blackpool and Southend United.

He took a two-year break from football in 2018 following further run-ins with the law. Since returning in 2020, he has bounced between several non-league clubs, starting with Spalding United before brief spells at Southend, Boreham Wood, Kettering Town, Wellingborough Town and Chatham Town.

Once again a free agent this summer, the striker left Chatham Town at the end of last season after scoring six goals in 14 appearances for the club.

Ranger has also spoken openly in the past about his struggles with gambling addiction. In a 2023 interview, he claimed that, had he behaved better off the pitch and maintained a healthier lifestyle, he could have been as prolific as Manchester City's goal machine Erling Haaland.

Sports.title: Beware Premier League rivals: Enzo Maresca's Man City are made for Erling Haaland and could help him produce his best season yet, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Back home 5,000 miles away, there ought to have been a certain Norwegian licking his lips at what Manchester City served up before they headed home from Asia. Presuming he has a subscription for the club’s in-house TV channel, that is.

This performance was made for Erling Haaland. The attacking style Enzo Maresca hopes to implement is made for Haaland. Atletico Madrid struggled for answers in how to counter City’s wingers – boldly direct all game – as they fizzed balls across the six-yard box.

That is Haaland’s zone and even before Omar Marmoush netted effectively the same goal twice in two minutes just before the hour – Antoine Semenyo hitting an area, the Egyptian tapping in – there came very real evidence that Haaland is going to be labelled a tap-in merchant. And City will not mind that one bit: that is where their goals are coming from this season.

It looks a game plan reliant on a man with a killer’s instinct, knowing exactly where to plonk himself. Haaland is the best in world football at that and City’s idea is clearly to lean into his strengths even further than they had done already.

Maresca had twice shown frustration before Marmoush’s double when Savinho had seemingly laid certain goals on a plate for a striker, only for nobody to arrive. The Italian bowed his head once and then outstretched the arms as Marmoush and others failed to fly in.

‘We cannot create the amount of situations and not finish the action,’ Maresca said. ‘There we need to be clinical. We need to improve. We are getting better there. With Erling we can be even more dangerous.’

Omar Marmoush produced two close range finishes from crosses aimed towards the six-yard box

Enzo Maresca's gameplan looks to have been devised with Erling Haaland in mind

Rayan Ait-Nouri scored Manchester City's third goal in their 3-1 victory over Atletico Madrid

Words were had at half time and it was noticeable that not only Marmoush but Phil Foden would later be readier to meet Semenyo’s crosses, crashing into the box in the way that had been replicated over and over in training the evening before. The victory was topped off by Rayan Ait-Nouri’s late third.

‘The players want to play,’ Maresca said as he left the door open for Marmoush’s potential exit, with Tottenham monitoring his situation.

‘They want to play. When they don’t play, they’re not happy. Omar’s desire is probably to play more minutes. It doesn't mean that he isn't going to play more minutes here but it's also his decision.’

Spurs target Savinho shows what he can offer City

Spurs still hold a keen interest in landing the £70million-rated Savinho, who had intimated a willingness to seek a new challenge earlier in the summer.

But the Brazilian has shown Maresca what he can offer out on the right wing with this style of play. There were the dangerous cutbacks, the sort reminiscent of a bygone era in the early years of Pep Guardiola, that suggested more of an end product than had been evident in his first two seasons.

That was the positive side of a lively Savinho, who relentlessly beat his full back around the outside. And yet, there were reminders of his profligacy that has seen him score just seven times in 84 games across all competitions.

When pouncing on a mistake, the 22-year-old should have driven towards goal and forced Jan Oblak to commit, instead deciding to check back and attempt a curling effort into the far corner from outside the box. It whipped wide.

And one of Maresca’s other disappointments came as Semenyo hit a dangerous area, only for City’s other winger to still be on his heels. There is work to do and decisions to be made before the end of the transfer window.

Savinho produced dangerous cutbacks and reliably beat his full back, but still showed reminders of his profligacy

City will need Anderson to quickly get up to speed

Despite dominating, City had fallen behind before Marmoush’s brace. A scrappy opener by Jorge Dominguez, a 16-year-old defender who towers over most. The teenager stabbed past Gianluigi Donnarumma from the second phase of a corner. City should have cleared their lines but it wasn’t the end of the world.

What will have concerned Maresca more were the spaces between the lines that Rodrigo Mendoza, a 21-year-old signed from Elche in February, was afforded. Mendoza proved a problem for Mateo Kovacic, ghosting off the back of the central midfielder and creating two decent chances. City will need to be more robust in that area of the pitch when they meet Arsenal in Sunday’s Community Shield.

Elliot Anderson is not linking up with the team until Wednesday and so it is likely that Kovacic will feature alongside Tijjani Reijnders in Cardiff. The pair have been strong on the ball in South Korea while having obvious things to work through defensively from a positioning sense.

As Barcelona expect to wrap up a deal to land metronome Rodri, City will need Anderson to quickly get himself up to speed.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat
