Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector, despite Polish government measures to cushion the rise in consumer prices. Orlen has also this year seen its highest ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets. The results come amid a political dispute over a government plan to impose a windfall tax on excess profits from fuel sales, aimed at recouping billions spent on consumer subsidies. Orlen would be the biggest target of the tax, but the plan has been obstructed by opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki. W pierwszym półroczu Orlen zarobił na czysto 15,8 miliarda złotych. Trzy razy więcej niż przed rokiem.https://t.co/qJS81csI0H — TVN24 BiS (@TVN24BiS) August 6, 2026 On Thursday, Orlen reported consolidated net profit of 15.9 billion zloty (€3.7 billion) for the first six months of the year, almost tripling from the 5.7 billion zloty recorded in the same period of 2025. Revenue rose to 152.2 billion zloty from 134.4 billion zloty. CEO Ireneusz Fąfara acknowledged that the figures came amid exceptional market conditions. Energy prices jumped globally in March, after the US and Israel began to attack Iran and Tehran responded by blocking the Strait of Hormuz, a key export route. Fąfara noted that, despite this, Poland had maintained some of Europe’s lowest fuel prices. He said that Orlen had prioritised fuel availability and competitive domestic prices while taking advantage of stronger margins abroad, where it brought in an “absolutely record level of revenue from foreign markets”. In the first half of 2026, foreign markets accounted for 35.7% of Orlen’s revenue, up from 33.8% a year earlier. The bulk came from Germany, the Czech Republic, Lithuania and Austria, where Orlen operates petrol stations, as well as from trading activities in markets such as the Netherlands and Switzerland. Pierwsze półrocze 2026 roku ORLEN zamyka rekordowym zyskiem z rynków zagranicznych. Wynik netto całej Grupy w II kwartale wyniósł 7,7 mld zł. Wypracowane wyniki finansowe pozwoliły na wypłatę rekordowej dywidendy dla akcjonariuszy oraz dalsze finansowanie największego programu… pic.twitter.com/ohcxksuv4G — ORLEN (@GrupaORLEN) August 6, 2026 Orlen has expanded rapidly in recent years, as it has swallowed up other state-owned energy firms and sought to diversify away from its traditional focus on oil towards gas, renewables and hydrogen. In March this year, Orlen’s market valuation rose to its highest ever level of €35.2 billion, up from €7 billion in early 2022. As a result, it overtook the market capitalisation of Russian energy giant Gazprom. Mateusz Czyżkowski, an analyst at brokerage XTB, attributed Orlen’s record profits this year to “skilful balancing between geopolitical conditions and local pressures”, including government-imposed fuel price caps that squeezed margins. “The global commodities market in the second quarter of 2026 was strongly buoyed by tensions between Iran and Israel and ongoing disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz…This significant geopolitical premium boosted profits in [Orlen’s] Upstream & Supply segment,” he wrote in a note. The announcement of record profits comes as Orlen finds itself at the centre of a political dispute over the government’s proposed windfall tax, which would introduce a 60% levy on excess profits from liquid fuel sales. The measure was expected to raise around 4 billion zloty, which would have offset most of the roughly 4.7 billion zloty the government spent on keeping fuel prices lower for consumers amid the crisis in the Middle East by, among other things, cutting VAT and introducing a maximum daily price. However, although the tax was approved by the government’s majority in parliament in July, President Nawrocki refused to sign it into law, instead referring it to the constitutional court for review – a process that has no time limit and can take years. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 According to government calculations, Orlen would account for around 60% of the tax base if the measures eventually come into force. However, at his press conference on Thursday, Fąfara emphasised that the company supports the windfall tax. “We have viewed this solution positively from the very beginning. I believe it is in the interest of the company, our customers, and the country,” he said. However, Fąfara rejected suggestions that Orlen could unilaterally reduce pump prices by sacrificing margins. “We cannot lower prices in defiance of the market and global prices…If we lowered prices below parity, there would be a shortage of fuel,” he warned, adding that artificially low prices would encourage speculative exports and fuel tourism. Prices at petrol stations jumped today in Poland after the government ended the last of the support measures introduced to cushion consumers from the energy crisis caused by the war in Iran. Some places saw prices rise by as much as 14%https://t.co/mUfWUyDMle — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 1, 2026 Prime Minister Donald Tusk used Orlen’s record profit announcement to reiterate criticism of the Nawrocki for obstructing the windfall tax. “Taxing such extraordinary profits made by oil companies, not just Orlen, was intended to bring down prices at petrol stations. That is precisely what Karol Nawrocki blocked. Remember this when you’re tanking up,” Tusk wrote on social media. Nawrocki’s office has, however, rejected the idea that an increased tax on fuel companies would somehow reduce fuel prices, arguing that, if anything, it would have the opposite effect if companies pass some of the costs onto consumers. Zysk Orlenu w pierwszym półroczu był wyższy od zeszłorocznego o 10 miliardów! Opodatkowanie takich nadzwyczajnych zysków koncernów paliwowych, nie tylko Orlenu, miały służyć obniżeniu cen na stacjach. To właśnie zablokował @NawrockiKn Pamiętajcie przy tankowaniu. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 6, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: New Polish opposition group proposes paying parents “salary” to encourage more births
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. New Polish opposition group Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), which recently broke away from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party, has proposed the idea of paying a “parental salary” for the first three years of a child’s life. The idea is part of a package of proposals to tackle Poland’s dire demographic situation released on Friday by Development Plus in its first major policy announcement since leader Mateusz Morawiecki announced that the group would soon become a political party. 3600 zł miesięcznie na dziecko do 3. roku życia – jedna z wielu propozycji @RozwojPlus dla demografii! Pensja Rodzicielska wynosząca równowartość płacy minimalnej, czyli obecnie około 3600 zł netto miesięcznie przez pierwsze 3 lata życia dziecka. To ponad czterokrotnie więcej… pic.twitter.com/253pwcskNK — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) August 7, 2026 The proposed parental salary would amount to 3,600 zloty (€837) per month, the equivalent of the minimum wage after taxes. It is 4.5 times more than the current child benefit payment of 800 zloty per month that all Polish parents of children under 18 receive. Development Plus says that the parental salary could be combined with income from other work that parents undertake and that it would include contributions towards their pensions. It would end once a child turns three, after which parents would have access to normal child benefit payments. The group says that, for now, the idea is just a proposal, based on expert analysis of how to tackle Poland’s demographic crisis, and that it now wants to “refine it through dialogue with Poles” rather than “imposing top-down provisions”. Poland has long been grappling with a shrinking, ageing population. Last year, the number of births fell to a new post-war low of 238,000, while deaths totalled 406,000. That marked the 13th consecutive year in which more people died than were born in Poland. The country’s fertility rate – meaning the average number of children that are born to a woman over her lifetime – fell to a new record low of 1.068 in 2025. That is one of the lowest figures anywhere in the world and well below the so-called “replacement rate” – the figure needed to ensure that the population does not decline – which is generally defined as 2.1. Poland’s fertility rate, already one of the lowest in the world, fell to a new record low of 1.07 in 2025, deepening concerns over the country's shrinking and ageing population https://t.co/OMGC1MpA5l — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 28, 2026 Successive Polish governments have introduced various measures intended to boost the birth rate, though so far without clear success. The former PiS government, with Morawiecki as finance minister and later prime minister, introduced and expanded the current child benefit programme. While there was a brief bump in births after it was launched in 2016, numbers subsequently continued their downward trend. After PiS lost power in 2023, the current government, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, continued the child benefit programme and also introduced new payments to support parents who return to work and restored funding for IVF treatment, which was previously cut by PiS. When announcing the proposed parental salary on Friday, Development Plus also outlined seven other proposed new policies to ease Poland’s demographic problems. One would allow workers to have a portion of their contributions go towards their parents’ pensions. Another pledged to provide better maternity care, including access to anaesthesia, a private hospital room and dedicated midwife, prenatal testing, and infertility treatment. Other policies promised more flexible working arrangements and mortgage repayments to prevent people from having to choose between a family or a career, as well as school hours and after-school care that “adapt to the lives of families, not the other way around”. Development Plus also proposed “granting parents the right to represent the voices of their minor children”. However, they provided no details of what this would mean in practice. Dzieci to nasza przyszłość! To fundament bezpieczeństwa Polski i polska racja stanu. Jak sprawić, by Polaków rodziło się coraz więcej? Oto strategia demograficzna dla Polski Stowarzyszenia @RozwojPlus🇵🇱➕. pic.twitter.com/1hiQPNuL47 — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) August 7, 2026 Development Plus was founded as an association by Morawiecki in April this year. That immediately prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. Matters came to a head last month, when PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński demanded that all the party’s lawmakers sign a pledge of loyalty and commit to leave any political associations they are part of. Morawiecki and his allies refused to do so, prompting Kaczyński to declare that meant they had effectively resigned from the party. Last week, Development Plus announced it had formed its own separate parliamentary caucus with 40 MPs in the Sejm, the most powerful lower house of parliament. The move immediately made it the third-largest group in the parliament, while also meaning PiS was no longer the biggest. On Monday this week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”, following PiS’s shift in a more hardline direction over recent months. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish opposition calls for deportation of Ukrainian conscription-age men not working legally
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has called for Ukrainian men of conscription age who are not legally working to be deported to Ukraine. The policy, which continues a recent hardening of PiS’s position towards Ukraine and Ukrainians as it competes with the far right for support, was condemned by government figures, who called it “absurd” and “disgusting”. 🇵🇱 Bezpieczeństwo obywateli powinno być priorytetem każdego rządu. Potrzebne są zdecydowane działania wobec osób przebywających w Polsce niezgodnie z prawem. 👉 Udostępnij! 🔥 Ku nowemu rządowi! pic.twitter.com/m8MctmmPXd — Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (@pisorgpl) August 6, 2026 On Thursday, PiS, which has recently been hit by falling support in the polls and the defection of a large breakaway group of more moderate MPs, held a policy convention at which it presented ideas it wants to implement if it returns to power after next year’s parliamentary elections. “One of [our] government’s first, most significant decisions will be to deport men, Ukrainians of military age, who are not legally working in Poland,” announced Tobiasz Bocheński, a deputy leader of the party. “They will have the opportunity to fight for their homeland, so that the horrors of this war can quickly end,” he continued. “Because for Central and Eastern Europe to be secure and free, Ukraine must win.” Bocheński denied that the policy was inhumane, noting that, in 2022, when PiS was in government, “Poles, like no other nation in Europe, opened their hearts, their homes and their wallets to women, children, the elderly and disabled people fleeing Putin’s bombs”. Poland was the primary destination for refugees fleeing Ukraine in 2022. Almost one million of them remain in the country, alongside hundreds of thousands of other Ukrainian immigrants, many of whom arrived before 2022. They are by far Poland’s largest foreign national group. In their announcement of the proposed policy, PiS gave no details of how it would work in practice, nor on what legal basis Ukrainians who are legally resident in Poland and have not violated any laws would be deported. News website Interia, which had reported on PiS’s plans shortly before they were officially announced, notes that data from Poland’s labour ministry show that only around 11,000 Ukrainians are registered as unemployed in Poland. The figures are not broken down by gender, but most are believed to be women. However, PiS’s policy would also apply to Ukrainians in the so-called grey economy, where people work informally without registering or paying taxes, reports Interia. Military-age Ukrainian men in other European countries should not receive social benefits, says Poland's foreign minister, @sikorskiradek. "There should be no financial incentives for avoiding the draft" https://t.co/5TcTqyDa6X — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2024 PiS’s plan was immediately criticised by government figures, with interior ministry spokeswoman Karolina Gałecka calling it “an absurd idea” and “pure demagoguery”. She noted that over 95% of Ukrainian men of conscription age in Poland are working legally and paying taxes. “Without these people, many key sectors of the Polish economy would simply grind to a halt,” wrote Gałecka. “Stop the incitement.” Deputy interior minister Maciej Duszczyk, meanwhile, told broadcaster TVN that, among the Ukrainian men not working, many are wounded soldiers in Poland for treatment and rehabilitation or fathers caring for disabled children. Deportations are a “purely political, disgusting idea”, he added. Interior minister Marcin Kierwiński wrote that, “when [PiS] was in power, they couldn’t even deport those who were breaking the law, and now they’re supposedly going to deport everyone without rhyme or reason”. Since taking power, the current government has increased deportations of foreigners who are in Poland illegally or broke the law while in the country. Last year, it carried out over 9,000 deportations, up from 7,200 in 2023, the last year that PiS was in power Absurdalny pomysł @pisorgpl ws. deportacji Ukraińców to czysta demagogia! Ponad 95% mężczyzn w wieku poborowym legalnie pracuje w 🇵🇱 i płaci podatki (dane ZUS).@OficjalnyJK zapowiada deportacje. A jak miałoby to wyglądać w praktyce? Patrole sprawdzające dokumenty na ulicach?… — Karolina Gałecka (@K_Galecka) August 6, 2026 During the conference on Thursday, PiS emphasised its tough approach to migration more broadly, saying that it would “create a new, restrictive system for foreigners” that would track each immigrant in the country. “Every foreigner will have their own individual account,” and if they commit any offences or fail to abide by any administrative obligations, “the information will be immediately entered into the system, and the deportation process will begin”, said Bocheński. “The only good migration is the return of Poles from abroad,” declared the party on social media. 🛡️ Bezpieczne granice to bezpieczna Polska. Skuteczna ochrona granic i walka z nielegalną imigracją to obowiązek każdego odpowiedzialnego państwa. 👉 Udostępnij! 🔥 Ku nowemu rządowi! pic.twitter.com/rRPZpmXi5U — Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (@pisorgpl) August 6, 2026 In fact, it was during PiS’s time in power from 2015 to 2023 that Poland saw the largest wave of immigration in its history, and one of the largest anywhere in Europe. In every year between 2017 and 2022, Poland was the EU member state that issued the highest number of first residence permits to immigrants from outside the bloc. There are now over two million foreigners registered as living in Poland, making up just 5% of the population. Around three quarters are Ukrainians (1.55 million), with the next largest groups being Belarusians (139,300), Indians (26,100), Georgians (22,200), Russians (19,500), Vietnamese (15,100) and Turks (14,500). The number of foreigners with residence permits in Poland has reached two million, making up just over 5% of the country’s population, new government data show. The largest national group by far are Ukrainians, followed by Belarusians and Indians https://t.co/SI09WtR7hR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 26, 2026 While in government, PiS welcomed Ukrainian migrants and refugees and was a strong supporter of Ukraine in its defence against Russian aggression. However, since going into opposition, it has taken an increasingly tough line. That has reflected a broader shift in Polish society, with a variety of polls showing rising negative sentiment towards Ukraine and Ukrainians. Recent months have also seen a rise in reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland, including a number of high-profile incidents. Meanwhile, two far-right parties that have long taken an anti-Ukrainian stance, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), have soared in the polls, placing pressure on PiS to toughen its own position. One Confederation MEP, Stanisław Tyszka, mocked PiS’s latest policy announcement. “PiS wants to heroically deport hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians whom they themselves let into Poland,” he wrote. “Comedy.” The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland is up 30% so far this year, police data show. The figures come following recent high-profile cases of verbal and physical attacks against Ukrainians, who are Poland's largest immigrant group https://t.co/pcTsJddDz7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 17, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland invokes emergency grid capacity powers for second time in three days amid heatwave
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s power grid operator, PSE, has, for the second time in three days and third time this summer, invoked emergency measures to ensure supply amid an ongoing heatwave. Before this summer, it had only done so twice in the eight years since such powers were introduced. However, following a meeting with PSE and other state energy officials, Prime Minister Donald Tusk has assured Poles that, despite “a very difficult period”, the “situation is under control” and power supplies are secure, thanks in part to the growth of renewables in recent years. ❗️PSE ponownie ogłaszają okresy przywołania na rynku mocy❗️ To już 3. raz w tym roku, kiedy operator sięga po to narzędzie. W historii zdarzyło się to tylko 5 razy, wliczywszy 3 przypadki tegoroczne, co pokazuje wyjątkowość roku 2026 dla energetyki. pic.twitter.com/DbCPnpyae4 — Jakub Wiech (@jakubwiech) August 6, 2026 PSE has called on contracted electricity generators to increase output and large consumers to cut use to help balance the grid on Thursday between 5:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m., as temperatures have this week approached 40°C (104°F) in many parts of the country. The same measures were introduced on Tuesday, as the heatwave pushed up electricity consumption, partly due to increased use of air conditioning and refrigeration. Participants in Poland’s capacity market are paid for maintaining standby capacity and fulfilling their obligations when called upon by the operator. According to PSE, the mechanism is “a remedial measure” used when the generation capacity available to the operator falls significantly below the required safety level. Previously, the measures were invoked in June this year, amid another heatwave that saw Poland hit its highest-ever recorded temperature of 40.5°C. But before that, they had only been used twice since being introduced in 2018. Temperatures in Poland have reached the highest level on record, with a figure of 40.3°C (104.5°F) recorded this afternoon, as the heatwave that has hit Europe this week moves eastwards https://t.co/eRhRxiuCGq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 28, 2026 Poland’s weather institute IMGW issued heat warnings on Thursday for 13 of the country’s 16 provinces, with daytime temperatures forecast to reach between 33C and 38C. High temperatures and prolonged drought conditions have also pushed water levels in many rivers to extremely low levels, with the Vistula, Poland’s longest river, only 5 centimetres above the historic low of 4 centimetres it fell to in Warsaw last year. Some other parts of the river have hit all-time record lows, reports Polsat News. One result has been a disruption of cooling supplies to Poland’s power sector. State energy firm Enea this week announced reduced operations at two of its coal-fired plants that are cooled by water from the Vistula. Around 1.1 gigawatts (GW) of capacity (just over 1% of Poland’s total) has gone offline. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk convened a meeting of a government crisis team, including PSE’s deputy president, to discuss the current heatwave and its potential impact on the power sector. However, afterwards he assured that “the situation is under control” and that the fact that Poland now has “a lot of energy from solar panels and wind turbines makes our system relatively secure”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Poland’s renewable sector has expanded rapidly over the last decade. Last year, it provided just over 29% of the country’s power, with onshore wind supplying 14% of the energy mix and solar 12%. Renewables generated 29.4% of Poland's electricity in 2025, almost exactly the same figure as in 2024, ending a period of strong growth since 2021. Coal (52.2%) remained the dominant source, though its share declined. For more, read our full report: https://t.co/XjD9hfhabo pic.twitter.com/WklP7dYL78 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 2, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish top court confirms withholding funds from opposition PiS party over campaign finance irregularities
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s top administrative court has upheld a decision by the finance ministry to withhold state subsidies from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party due to campaign finance irregularities. The decision was welcomed by the government, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying that there will be “no money for grifters”. PiS, however, argues that the money is being withheld for political reasons and accuses the authorities of “Russian standards”. Naczelny Sąd Administracyjny oddalił w środę kasacje ws. dotacji i subwencji dla PiS. – Miażdżący dla PiS wyrok podtrzymany! – stwierdził szef MF Andrzej Domański https://t.co/bcL18WbiYf — OKO.press (@oko_press) August 6, 2026 The dispute dates back to August 2024, when the National Electoral Commission (PKW) rejected PiS’s financial report for the previous year’s parliamentary election campaign after identifying around 3.6 million zloty (€838,000) in unauthorised expenditure. As a result, the PKW ordered that PiS should lose 10.8 million zloty from the state subsidies that political parties in Poland receive based on their level of electoral support. The party would normally have received 25.9 million zloty based on its 2023 election result. The decision triggered months of legal wrangling, with PiS arguing that the funding should be restored after the Supreme Court upheld its complaint against the PKW’s decision. However, finance minister Andrzej Domański refused to release the money, saying there were unresolved legal doubts over the ruling. The finance minister has refused to comply with the electoral commission's decision to pay out subsidies to the opposition PiS party He says there are "legal doubts" over the issue. But PiS says he is obliged to pay and will be held criminally responsible https://t.co/ZwIZRqn5tp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 9, 2025 Those doubts stem from a broader dispute over the controversial and contested judicial reforms implemented by PiS when it ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023. The chamber of the Supreme Court that ruled in PiS’s favour was created as part of those reforms. It has previously been found to not be a legitimate body by both the European Court of Justice and European Court of Human Rights because it contains improperly appointed judges. After the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling, the PKW initially said it would not recognise the decision until the chamber’s legal status was clarified. Two weeks later, however, it reversed that decision and approved PiS’s financial report. Domański still declined to restore the subsidy, arguing that the PKW’s resolution was internally contradictory. While it approved the payments, it also stated that the chamber’s ruling should come from a body recognised as a court and that it was not determining whether the chamber met that standard. PiS challenged Domański’s decision. However, its case was initially rejected by a lower court in June last year, and that decision has now been upheld by the Supreme Administrative Court (NSA), which is the final court of appeal for administrative issues. The NSA found the minister had acted lawfully in withholding the funding. It also said the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling had no legal effect because it had been issued by a body that was not a properly constituted court, reports news website OKO.press. The ruling was welcomed by Domański, who called it a “crushing blow to PiS” and said that “yet another PiS lie has been exposed”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk, meanwhile, wrote on social media: “Just as we said, there is and will be no money for grifters.” Tak jak mówiliśmy, dla przekręciarzy pieniędzy nie ma i nie będzie. https://t.co/4Kqexj6NoC — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 5, 2026 The PKW’s decision to cut PiS’s funds was made after it found that government resources – including from the justice ministry, Government Legislation Centre (RCL) and Research and Academic Computer Network (NASK) – had been used to support the party’s election campaign. However, PiS has always argued that the decision was a political one, implemented at the behest of the new Tusk government in order to undermine the main opposition party. Radosław Fogiel, a senior PiS lawmaker and former party spokesman, said that the new NSA ruling “does not change the essence of the matter: it unlawfully deprives the main opposition party of the subsidy to which it is entitled. Russian standards.” Chłopie, powstrzymaj emocje! Ekscytacja jak u nastolatka przed pierwszą randką. A czego dotyczy ów "miażdżący wyrok"? Skargi na bezczynność Ministra Finansów. To, że przybyli mu w sukurs kwestionują decyzję Sądu Najwyższego, nie zmienia istoty rzeczy: nielegalnie pozbawia główną… https://t.co/NONA2tOoxf — Radosław Fogiel (@radekfogiel) August 5, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Shella Radio Visualizes Struggling Culture Scene At National Gallery
World.content:
A radio tower installation at Prague’s National Gallery is showcasing local efforts to preserve alternative culture as the Czech government seeks to cut funding to the arts and other public sectors.

Created by members of Prague-based Shella Radio, the tower is adorned with fabrics and relics of previous parties hosted in Ankali & Planeta Za, a nightclub that has faced closure due to financial problems.

“We believe in the idea of this radio as an amplification of voices that are often neglected in other spaces,” Shania Rodriguez, a Prague-based DJ and Shella radio host, said in an interview. “Here, they can be vocal about the issues and problems within our system and also share ideas of change.”



Many artists and curators say the environment for cultural organizations has grown more challenging due to financial cuts by the new right wing government led by Andrej Babiš.

The planned budget for this year shrank by 3.9 billion crowns – an almost 20 percent decrease from the previous year, according to the Czech Ministry of Culture. The cuts sparked widespread backlash across the country in April, and many took to the streets.

Shella, an Egyptian Arabic slang word meaning “a group of friends who do things together,” hosts political talk shows, electronic music club nights, and summer markets featuring local artists.

“The idea behind our installation was to be able to transmit parts of our identity that have been fundamental in Shella Radio’s trajectory,” Rodriguez said. “This DIY approach gives us the freedom to customize and handcraft our installation and studio space using materials from our temporary home: Ankali.”

The installation is part of the Necessary Wishes exhibition at the National Gallery which brings together more than 50 collectives and artists.

The event is free of charge and ends on September 13.

By: Lili Anna Lempek, Adam Pohořilský, Milena Gevorgyan, Isabella Fattore

World.title: Where to See the Partial Solar Eclipse in Prague and Across Czechia
World.content:
Skywatchers in the Czech Republic will have two reasons to look up on the night of August 12.

A partial solar eclipse will be visible in the evening, followed by favorable conditions for watching the annual Perseid meteor shower.

The eclipse will be visible across Czechia shortly before sunset, with the Sun low over the western and northwestern horizon. In Prague, the partial eclipse is expected to begin at about 7:19 p.m., reach its maximum at 8:12 p.m. and end around 8:27 p.m.



At the height of the eclipse, the Moon will cover about 86 percent of the Sun’s disk in Prague, making the event particularly noticeable if skies are clear.

The eclipse will look different depending on where observers are located. The farther east they are, the later the eclipse will begin and the less of it will be visible. In eastern Czechia and much of Slovakia, the maximum phase will take place after sunset, when the Sun is already below the horizon.

The event will be a partial eclipse in Central Europe, while a total solar eclipse will be visible in parts of Greenland, Iceland and Spain. Astronomers and eclipse enthusiasts are expected to travel to those areas to experience totality.

A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, blocking part or all of the Sun from view. In Czechia, the eclipse will be especially low on the horizon, so observers will need an unobstructed view toward the west and northwest.

Several Czech observatories are preparing public observing events. A list of locations and other information about the eclipse is available through the Czech astronomical website astro.cz.

Perseid meteor shower will follow

The same night will also offer good conditions for watching the Perseids, one of the most prominent annual meteor showers.

The shower will reach its peak during the early hours of August 13, when the Moon will be only a few hours past its new-moon phase. With virtually no moonlight in the sky, faint meteors should be easier to spot.

The Perseids are active from July 17 through August 24, but the best opportunity this year will come during the night of August 12-13.

Under dark skies and favorable weather, observers away from cities could see between 50 and 80 meteors per hour.

Light pollution will be the main obstacle for anyone hoping to see large numbers of meteors. The best locations are well away from major cities, ideally several dozen kilometers from strong sources of artificial light.

World.title: Non-Alcoholic Beer Sales Rise by More Than 25% in Czechia
World.content:
Beer remains a staple of the Czech shopping basket, but new sales data from online supermarket Rohlík shows that drinking habits are gradually changing.

Traditional lagers still dominate, while non-alcoholic beer is recording the fastest growth among the main beer categories.

The category has grown by more than a quarter over the past year, with Birell among the brands driving the increase. Birell sales alone are up by almost 20%.



Together with flavoured beers and radlers, non-alcoholic beer now accounts for close to one-third of all beer sales on Rohlík.

Beer from small and regional breweries is also gaining ground, with sales increasing by more than 11%.

The biggest decline is being recorded among craft beers grouped by style, including IPA and APA. This is currently the only major beer segment experiencing a year-on-year drop.

Czech brands continue to dominate the market. More than nine out of every 10 beers sold through Rohlík are from domestic brands.

Imported beers, however, are growing at a faster rate. Their sales have increased by 18% year-on-year.

Beer sales peak at the weekend

Friday is the busiest day for beer sales, with roughly twice as much beer sold as on Monday. Friday and Saturday together account for almost two-fifths of the category’s weekly sales.

Orders containing beer also tend to include significantly more items than orders without beer, suggesting that customers often buy it as part of a larger meal or weekend shop rather than as a standalone purchase.

Seasonal patterns have also shifted. Beer sales during this year’s summer months have reached levels comparable with the December Christmas peak.

World.title: Explore Holašovice: A UNESCO-Listed Gem with Its Own Stonehenge
World.content:
For over 20 years, the South Bohemian village of Holašovice has held a place on the UNESCO World Heritage list.

Located approximately 16 kilometers west of České Budějovice, this village is famed for its picturesque houses, built in the distinctive Peasant Baroque style.



The first recorded mention of Holašovice dates back to the late 13th century. The village has a rich and storied history, marked by events such as the Hussite wars and a devastating plague in the 16th century that significantly reduced the local population.

The iconic houses that now define Holašovice were constructed in the latter half of the 19th century, reflecting the Baroque, Rococo, and Classical influences prevalent in South Bohemian architecture of that era.

The village’s ethnic composition underwent significant changes during and after World War II. Following the establishment of the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia, the Czech residents were forced to leave Holašovice, and the village was annexed to the Third Reich.

After the war, the German population was expelled, once again altering the village’s demographics.

Lada’s Pond and the Czech Stonehenge

Despite its turbulent past, Holašovice has retained a unique atmosphere that continues to attract visitors.

In addition to its charming houses, tourists can explore the local chapel and the picturesque Lada’s Pond, which, along with a statue of a water sprite, seems to be straight out of a painting by Josef Lada.

Just outside the village lies a unique stone circle, often referred to as the “Czech Stonehenge.” This site was designed to channel negative energy away from the human body, offering visitors a chance to experience its reputed healing properties.

World.title: Prague 7 Plans Floating Swimming Pool on the Vltava in Holešovice
World.content:
A floating swimming pool could be built along the Vltava River in Prague’s Holešovice district, near U Vody Park.

Prague 7 City Hall is considering using a section of the waterfront near the Port 7 development for the project.

The municipality hopes the pool could be ready within three years, although the cost has not yet been determined.

The project is still in its early stages. The district is currently looking into whether it could obtain older or unused pontoons and adapt them to create the swimming facility.



One of the main questions is where the pool water would come from. Prague 7 is considering both the Vltava and the municipal water supply.

The aim would be to use this data to determine when swimming in the river is considered safe. Čižinský has suggested introducing a simple traffic-light system similar to those used in cities such as Copenhagen and Amsterdam, allowing swimmers to see whether conditions are suitable.

According to Čižinský, the Vltava generally has good enough water quality for swimming, although conditions can deteriorate after heavy rainfall.

Recent measurements support this concern. Prague hygiene officials have been monitoring the water at Branická beach since the beginning of this year. The water has generally received a rating of two on the five-level scale used by hygienists.

The Holešovice proposal is not the first plan to introduce a floating swimming facility on the Vltava.

A similar idea was included in an earlier proposal to transform Prague’s riverfront. The project near Vyšehrad envisaged a large floating structure measuring 69 by 7.5 meters, with a swimming pool and a smaller paddling pool. A second connected vessel would have provided facilities for visitors.

The proposal was later put aside. In 2025, Prague property councilor Adam Zábranský of the Pirates said the investment was not among the city’s priorities.

World.title: Construction Disrupts Prague Tourists and Businesses During Peak Summer Season
World.content:
Construction projects across Prague’s historic center are proving a pain for tourists and locals alike who say the clumps of dirt, building supplies and equipment block popular sites and make it difficult to move around one of Europe’s most visited cities.



Heading down Národní to the Charles Bridge or going for a beer near the Vltava river now looks more like a vast construction site where tourists need to look out for more than the cobble-stone streets and baroque spires.

“It’s their first time here too, [they’ve] never seen it and now it’s torn up,” said Sherryl, a tourist visiting from the United States with her friends.

A major source of the disruption are upgrades to the public transport system. The central tram route delivering travelers to the heart of the city near the Národní Divadlo stop has been shuttered for weeks.

The disruption has taken a heavy toll on surrounding businesses like Aggeo, an Italian grocery store along the corridor. Its manager, Irena Kumpová, noted a sharp drop in foot traffic from travelers and regular local customers, who stroll by the National Theater on their way to gaze at the artist David Černý’s famous Kafka head.

“I’d rather stay closed… it’s a catastrophe,” remarked Kumpová.

With tourism growing every year in Prague, the widespread construction is making its mark this summer. So far this year, 1.7 million people have visited Prague, marking the strongest start in 15 years, according to Prague City Tourism and the Czech Statistical Office.

Tram services are suspended through the city center, clogging the streets and forcing many to find another way to work or home. For businesses that rely on heavy foot traffic during the busiest months of the year, that means less earnings.

“I have a table outside, but mainly just to signal to people that we’re open, but no one sits there right now,” said Kumpová.

The reconstruction is part of Prague’s broader effort to modernize its transport network, including long-term investments such as the future tram connection to Wenceslas Square and the expansion of Metro Line D as the city seeks to expand public transport.

Not everybody minds the disruption. The loud machines, dusty air, and obstructed sidewalks offer a certain charm for some who view the construction as part of the sightseeing experience.

“Despite the construction, it’s still beautiful,” said Raluca Costachescu, a traveler from Romania.

Written by: Mae Bryant, Bilyana Spasova, Milica Petrušová, Zuzana Kormančíková, Zhanna Bekiryan

World.title: Live Nation and PPF to Run Three Major Prague Venues
World.content:
Live Nation and PPF Group are forming a joint venture that will operate three of Prague’s major event venues — O2 Arena, O2 Universum and Forum Karlín.

The companies plan to invest in the venues and upgrade their facilities, with Live Nation set to hold a 51 percent stake in the new company.

The agreement will bring together one of the world’s largest live entertainment companies and PPF, the investment group that owns O2 Arena and O2 Universum through its subsidiary Bestsport.



PPF has also operated Forum Karlín, which has been owned by Patria Investment Company since last year.

The companies announced the planned partnership in a joint statement. Financial details of the transaction and the amount of the planned investment have not been disclosed. The deal remains subject to the required regulatory approvals.

Under the agreement, the new operator will be responsible for the day-to-day running of all three venues, including event planning and programming. The venues themselves will remain under their existing ownership structures, and their names will not change.

The partners said they intend to invest substantially in the facilities over the coming years. The aim is to improve conditions for audiences and performers while expanding the number of events held in Prague and strengthening the city’s position on the international concert and entertainment circuit.

PPF said the cooperation with Live Nation is also part of its strategy of developing the long-term value of its assets alongside major international companies.

Live Nation Entertainment operates across several areas of the live entertainment industry, including concert promotion, ticketing and sponsorship. Its businesses include Live Nation Concerts, Ticketmaster and Live Nation Sponsorship.

PPF Group is an international investment company with holdings across Europe, North America and Asia. Its portfolio includes telecommunications, media, financial services, real estate, e-commerce, industry and biotechnology.

World.title: Prague to Restore Tram Service Between Holešovice and City Center
World.content:
Residents of Prague 7 will regain a tram connection between Holešovice and the city center from September, with tram line 5 set to operate through the district and continue toward Wenceslas Square.

The change follows months of pressure from Prague 7 officials and local residents, who have called for better tram connections since the cancellation of line 14.

The district had previously requested either the return of line 14 or the introduction of an equivalent service and organized a petition supporting the demand.



The new arrangement will initially be temporary. According to the Prague Integrated Transport (PID) system, two trams will operate on the route at least through December 2026.

Line 5 to replace temporary route

The new service is linked to planned transport changes in Žižkov. Because of a traffic closure there, tram line 34 will be replaced by line 5 in Holešovice.

At Holešovice train station, line 5 will connect with line 6, effectively creating a continuous service between the two routes. Trams will run from the station through the Holešovice area, past the market and across Vltavská Street before continuing toward Wenceslas Square and other parts of central Prague.

For passengers in Holešovice, the move restores a connection that was lost when line 14 was discontinued.

Service could change again next year

The situation between January and June 2027 has not yet been fully settled. According to PID, the final arrangement will depend in part on discussions between the incoming leaderships of Prague 3 and Prague 7.

Maintaining the additional tram service in Holešovice during that period could require limited reductions elsewhere in Prague 3. Another option would be to temporarily return to the existing arrangement using combined tram lines 6 and 34.

PID has warned that permanently combining lines 5 and 6 could also create delays at both ends of the route. Such a change could affect passengers travelling through Prague 2 and Prague 5, even though it would provide the direct connection sought by Prague 7.

World.title: Why Hungary’s cheapest shop may have closed – and shoppers are already furious
World.content:
Hungary’s cheapest shop has refused to explain why it has been closed for several days, citing “technical reasons” – an explanation that few people believe. Most suspiciously, all of the company’s European shops have reportedly shut, with “technical issues” cited in each case. Some commentators already believe the Budapest outlet will not be closed for merely a few days – which might be understandable in the event of a technical problem – but for much longer. Its staff have reportedly already been dismissed.

Hungary’s cheapest shop – with compromises

Until 1 August, Basket Plusz, the Mere group’s only Hungarian shop, regularly posted videos advertising a range of cheap products. The Russian-backed group’s Budapest outlet, located in the city’s 18th district, opened at the beginning of December last year, just in time for Christmas, and marketed itself as Hungary’s cheapest shop – a claim that, judging by customers’ experiences, appeared to be justified.

That came with serious compromises. The store relied on B- and C-tier brands, contracts that favoured suppliers – who were paid only for goods that had actually been sold – and a stark, warehouse-like appearance. The premises, crammed with pallets and resembling a Metro-style warehouse more than a conventional supermarket, offered a poor shopping experience but undoubtedly helped to keep prices down.

Some customers, however, complained that the products they bought were not as good as comparable items sold by other retailers.

Another explanation for the closures

The sole Hungarian outlet closed last week, citing technical problems. Its Facebook page has not been updated since, and reports suggest that the small number of employees working in the quasi-warehouse-style shop have already been sacked.

The technical explanation appears particularly suspicious when viewed alongside similar reports from Slovakia and the Czech Republic.

The Russian MERE discount chain. Photo: mere.ws

Világgazdaság reported that Mere’s Slovak shops – where the chain also arrived last December – as well as its Baltic and Czech outlets, had also ceased trading. Technical reasons were cited in those cases, too. The real explanation, however, may be the EU’s sanctions package adopted at the end of July, which placed Sergei Schneider, one of the owners of the group behind the Mere, Svetofor and MyPrice chains, on a sanctions list.

The Czech Republic even froze the family’s shares after the sanctions came into force. As a result, they cannot sell their holdings or receive dividends.

Is the group withdrawing or merely going dormant?

In Lithuania, the authorities are investigating whether the newly opened Ola shops are linked to the Russian group and whether they represent an attempt to evade sanctions. Previously, 30 shops closed in the country and 250 people were sacked.

According to Világgazdaság, the central question is whether the closures signal the group’s withdrawal from Central Europe or are merely temporary measures.

The Russian MERE discount chain. Photo: mere.ws

Hungarian customers have expressed their anger over the closure in Mere-related Facebook groups, while hoping that the shop will reopen soon. Although some accept that the closure may be the result of sanctions, many believe that neither the EU nor the government led by Péter Magyar should drive out what they regard as a promising initiative.

If you missed: Is shopping abroad really cheaper? Why are Romanians and Bulgarians outspending Hungarians? New study provides answers

Why was the owner of a food company sanctioned?

The sanctions against Sergei Schneider came into force on July 23 and include an asset freeze, a ban on financing and the suspension of the company’s operations.

The stated reason is that the Russian businessman’s corporate empire plays a significant role in sustaining Russia’s domestic economy and therefore contributes indirectly to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

World.title: Real Hungarian summer starts this week after record heatwave – latest weather forecast
World.content:
Sunny, hot weather is expected throughout next week, with a brief spell of cooler conditions in the middle of the week. Showers and thunderstorms may occur in isolated spots at the beginning and end of the week, according to a forecast by HungaroMet Zrt sent to the Hungarian news agency MTI on Sunday.

Real Hungarian summer weather – forecast

Monday will be largely clear and dry, although cloud cover may increase from the west during the afternoon. There is a small chance of an isolated shower or thunderstorm moving in from the direction of the Alps. Southerly winds will occasionally freshen across the north-western Transdanubian region and the Northern Hungarian Mountains, while remaining mostly moderate elsewhere. Temperatures will rise to between 31 and 37C.

Tuesday will be mostly sunny, with some high and cumulus cloud. Showers and thunderstorms are likely only in a few places, chiefly in the west, south-west and north-east of the country. North-westerly winds will freshen across an increasing number of areas and may become strong in places. Morning temperatures will generally range from 16 to 22C, although it will be warmer near the water, in elevated areas, city centres and the Kisalföld region. Afternoon highs will reach 32 to 38C, with the hottest conditions expected in the Great Plain.

It will be hot this week, but not as scorchingly hot as last week. Source: Anadolu

Wednesday will bring predominantly clear or sunny skies and dry conditions. Northerly and north-easterly winds will freshen in several areas and may become strong at times, particularly east of the River Tisza. Morning temperatures will generally be between 17 and 24C, while afternoon highs are expected to range from 27 to 34C, with the lowest readings in the north-east.

Warming starts in the second half of the week

Thursday will be clear or sunny and dry. North-easterly winds will freshen mainly in the eastern half of the country. Temperatures will range from 9 to 19C in the early hours and from 28 to 33C in the afternoon.

Friday will remain clear or sunny, with no rain expected. North-easterly winds may freshen in places across the eastern and north-eastern parts of the country. Overnight lows will range from 8 to 19C, while daytime temperatures will reach 30 to 35C.

Rare solar eclipse to grace Hungarian skies this week – here is where you can see the most!

Saturday will continue to be largely clear, sunny and dry. Winds will be light or moderate and variable in direction. Temperatures will fall to between 8 and 20C overnight before rising to 31 to 36C during the day.

Sunday is expected to be mostly clear or lightly clouded and sunny. There is a slight chance of showers and thunderstorms in the north-west. Southerly winds will freshen, with temperatures rising from 10 to 22C at dawn to between 32 and 38C in the afternoon.

World.title: Georgian tourist attempted to rape Hungarian teenager – but Chinese neighbours stepped in just in time
World.content:
A 24-year-old Georgian tourist allegedly attempted to rape an 18-year-old Hungarian girl in Hajdúszoboszló, before Chinese women living nearby intervened. The man is said to have dragged his victim towards a patch of bushes, where she began shouting for help in English. Several Chinese women living in the area heard her cries.

Georgian man was visiting Hungary as a tourist

The 24-year-old Georgian national had travelled to Hungary as a tourist. However, he may not be returning home any time soon after being suspected of committing a serious criminal offence.

He met the young Hungarian woman in a park surrounded by blocks of flats in Hajdúszoboszló. They initially drank together, but the man allegedly wanted more.

He began touching and kissing the woman against her will. When she pulled away and resisted, he grabbed her by the wrist and dragged her towards a darker, overgrown area, allegedly intending to rape her. The woman then began shouting for help in English.

Chinese women rescued Hungarian teenager

Several Chinese women living on a floor of a neighbouring block of flats heard the cries. They also called out in English, asking whether the woman was in trouble and needed help. Moments later, she replied in the affirmative. By the time local residents became aware of what was happening, they saw only a man running out of the bushes and attempting to flee. Authorities identified and arrested him using footage from public CCTV cameras.

He has been remanded in custody pending trial because of concerns that he might flee or go into hiding, as well as the possibility that he could attempt to influence or intimidate the victim and witnesses. If convicted, he could face up to eight years in prison. He refused to speak to RTL Híradó, which reported on the disturbing incident. When asked directly in English whether he was willing to answer a few questions, he replied with a firm “no”.

Have you read this one? Paramedics attacked in Transylvania after being mistaken for organ traffickers and child kidnappers

Where will he serve his sentence?

If he is convicted and receives the minimum custodial sentence of two years for attempted rape, he could serve his sentence either in Hungary or in Georgia.

If he remains in Hungary, he will not receive special treatment. He would be held in a prison alongside Hungarian and foreign inmates, most likely at one of the capital’s Venyige Street or Nagy Ignác Street facilities.

The yard of a Hungarian prison. Photo: PrtScr/YT

However, the convicted man, the Hungarian state or the Georgian state could apply for him to be extradited to Georgia to serve his sentence there. The necessary international agreements are in place, but the authorities of both countries would have to approve the transfer.

World.title: PM Magyar made important announcement about turbine nr 3 at Paks NPP, Parliament to elect new President
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar said turbine number 3 of the second unit of the Paks nuclear power plant will start generating electricity from Monday evening.

In a post on social media Monday Magyar said that this morning the water level of the Danube was 19cm above the low point reached a week ago, and the process of restarting a turbine at the NPP has begun.

PM Magyar to speak ahead of agenda, parliament debate continues

Parliament’s two-day extraordinary session will start with PM Magyar’s speech ahead of the agenda on Monday. Two Fidesz lawmakers are scheduled to take oath of office, and parliament is scheduled to debate committee reports and amendment proposals to legislation on health care, the strike rights of teachers and eliminating the state of emergency, among other matters.

The house resumes work after last week’s cancellation due to extreme heat and energy-saving measures. The session is set to start at 13:00, according to the official website.

Following Magyar’s address and remarks by parliamentary group leaders, two new MPs, Olivér Hortay and André Palóc, will take their oaths. János Bóka, leader of the Fidesz parliamentary group, announced earlier this month that Hortay and Palóc would replace Péter Szijjártó and Gyula Budai, who resigned their seats, and join the Fidesz parliamentary group.

Parliament debates on different issues continue

Parliament then will debate an amendment proposal to health-care data management laws to allow pregnancy care providers to access syphilis infection data even if the screening did not take place within their care, aiming to accelerate syphilis detection and prenatal treatment.

Lawmakers will also table an amendment to education laws removing restrictions on the right to strike for those employed in public education and abolishing the rule that professional matters must be coordinated solely with the National Teachers’ Chamber.

A change to the law on transitional rules related to the end of the state of emergency and epidemic preparedness will be next on the agenda, eliminating the ministerial discretionary power to designate sites for battery recycling plants.

Further, lawmakers will discuss an amendment to the 2026 central budget law incorporating changes related to commitments under the Recovery and Resilience Plan and the obligation to pay into the Regional Development Fund.

New president to be elected on Tuesday

If parliament approves the proposal, the compatibility conditions for officials of the Hungarian Chamber of Agriculture, Food Industry, and Rural Development will tighten. In future, the organisation’s officials cannot be parliamentary or European parliamentary candidates, county assembly chairmen or members, mayors, government political executives, or government officials acting as supporters under the state budget law in the agricultural subsidy system. Additionally, the chamber’s officials will be barred from holding positions in political parties.

If ou missed: Viktor Orbán filmed in Serbia with MOL executive and controversial Hatvanpuszta estate architect

As parliament is scheduled to vote on the new president on Tuesday, parliamentary groups have until 10:00 on Monday to submit their nominations. The house committee will review the nominations at a meeting starting at 12:30.

Andrea Bujdosó, Dr András Baka and Péter Magyar. Baka is the Tisza Party’s nomination for presidency. Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

At its Saturday parliamentary group meeting, the ruling Tisza party decided to nominate Andras Baka, the former president of the Supreme Court, for the presidency. Mi Hazank announced at the end of July that it would propose Mate Toth, an energy lawyer, for the position, although its six-member parliamentary group cannot officially submit a nomination.

World.title: Central bank: Meeting euro adoption criteria would benefit Hungary’s entire economy
World.content:
The annual inflation rate could realistically remain below 2 percent, in line with the target set by the Hungarian National Bank (MNB) in June, the central bank’s deputy governor said in the latest episode of the MNB Podcast.

According to a statement sent by the MNB to the Hungarian News Agency (MTI) on Sunday, Péter Benő Banai stressed that, alongside achieving and maintaining price stability, the central bank’s primary objective is to act as a constructive partner in meeting the conditions for Hungary to join the eurozone.

Hungary’s inflation target may be due for a review

Banai recalled that Hungary’s current 3 percent inflation target is higher than the inflation targets of several other European countries and also exceeds the 2.7 percent inflation reference value included in the European Central Bank’s latest convergence report.

In light of the government’s intention to adopt the euro, he said it could therefore be appropriate to review Hungary’s inflation target. The deputy governor stressed that achieving and maintaining price stability is also of primary importance for sustainable economic growth.

Discussing euro adoption, Banai said that meeting the necessary economic conditions – including sound public finances, a declining debt-to-GDP ratio, low inflation, low yields on long-term government bonds and exchange-rate stability – would be beneficial for the Hungarian economy as a whole.

Euro adoption brings both benefits and risks

Banai added that adopting the euro has both advantages and potential disadvantages. Membership of the eurozone, he said, would not in itself lead to faster economic convergence. In the longer term, the pace of Hungary’s economic catch-up would instead depend on the quality of economic policy, he said.

If you missed it: Hungary’s euro introduction could create a major bond investment opportunity, analyst says

MNB: Bank fraud down by 41% in some categories

Speaking about efforts to combat cyber fraud, Banai highlighted the results of the central bank’s “five strikes” programme, launched last summer. Thanks in part to the initiative, the number of fraudulent transactions involving bank transfers fell by 41 percent in some categories, while in many cases the programme also succeeded in reversing previously rising trends in fraud.

Qvik offers cheaper alternative to card payments

Regarding the Qvik instant payment system, Banai said the development was not only a convenient alternative to bank cards, but also offered a cheaper payment solution for the national economy. The full episode is available on the MNB’s YouTube channel, according to the statement.

World.title: Rare solar eclipse to grace Hungarian skies this week – here is where you can see the most!
World.content:
A rare celestial event is set to light up the skies over Europe next Wednesday, with a solar eclipse visible from Hungary. While a total eclipse will be visible from parts of Spain and Iceland, observers in Hungary will be treated to a spectacular partial eclipse – and those in the western part of the country will have the best view.

Because the eclipse will occur shortly before sunset, location will play a particularly important role in determining how much of the Sun can be seen being covered by the Moon.

Sopron will have the best view

The westernmost parts of Hungary will be in the most favourable position for watching the eclipse. Sopron and its surroundings are expected to offer the best view, with almost 86% of the Sun covered by the Moon before the Sun disappears below the horizon.

The timing of the event means that the further west observers are, the greater the extent of the eclipse they will be able to see.

For comparison, observers in Spain, the Balearic Islands and Iceland will be able to experience a total solar eclipse, while Hungary will remain outside the path of totality. Even so, the partial eclipse promises to be a remarkable sight for anyone interested in astronomy, Időkép writes.

Solar eclipse: Degree of eclipse before sunset. Photo: Időkép

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

How to watch the eclipse safely

Choosing the right location will be essential. Since the Sun will already be very low in the sky, buildings, trees and hills could easily block the view. An open location with a clear, unobstructed western horizon will therefore offer the best chance of seeing the event.

It is also important to protect your eyes.

Never look directly at the Sun without proper certified solar viewing glasses or an appropriate solar filter. The fact that the Sun will be close to setting does not make direct viewing safe.

Clear skies could offer perfect conditions

The weather forecast currently suggests favourable conditions for observing the eclipse, with largely clear and cloudless skies expected across much of Hungary on Wednesday. That could provide excellent viewing conditions for the rare celestial spectacle – even as the country continues to experience hot summer weather.

For those hoping to catch the eclipse, heading to an elevated or otherwise unobstructed location in and around Sopron could offer the most spectacular view Hungary has to offer.

World.title: Sziget 2026: Festival reveals price of budget meals as huge food line-up awaits
World.content:
Sziget Festival is not just about world-famous music acts. This year, the Budapest festival is once again putting a strong emphasis on food, with everything from street food and international favourites to Michelin-starred cuisine on offer. And for festival-goers watching their spending, the popular fixed-price “budget food” option is returning – capped at HUF 3,500 (approx. EUR 10) per meal.

Every year, tens of thousands of people descend on Budapest’s Hajógyári Island for Sziget Festival, with organisers expecting close to 100,000 visitors this year. While the line-up includes major international and Hungarian acts, food has increasingly become an important part of the festival experience.

Budget meals will cost HUF 3,500

Sziget introduced its fixed-price, budget-friendly food initiative a few years ago, giving visitors an affordable alternative to some of the festival’s more expensive dishes.

This year, budget meals will be capped at HUF 3,500, and visitors will be able to buy a one-pot meal for that price, Sziget founder Károly Gerendai told Mindmegette.

The initiative works similarly to fixed-price food options at some of Budapest’s major Christmas markets: participating vendors offer a designated dish at the same maximum price, helping festival-goers keep their food costs under control.

There will be numerous food areas around the festival site, featuring both food trucks and permanent-style food outlets. Visitors can expect classic festival favourites such as hot dogs, burgers and lángos, but also more sophisticated options.

One of the major new additions is Food Paradise, inspired by the concept of Time Out Market. Visitors can eat while DJs provide live entertainment, turning the area into more than just a place to grab a quick bite.

The VIP section will go even further, bringing together some of the best-known names in Budapest’s restaurant scene, including restaurants from the Costes group and 101, as well as dishes associated with venues such as MÁK and Kádár Étkezde.

Photo: Kádár étkezde

Familiar favourites are returning

The 2026 line-up also includes a number of restaurants and food brands that have become familiar faces at festivals and in Budapest’s street-food scene.

Among them is Los Monos, known for its Mexican-inspired food and tacos, while Krumpello will once again demonstrate what can be done with the humble baked potato, serving generously loaded jacket potatoes.

Meraki will bring Greek-inspired dishes and Mediterranean flavours, while Crunchy will cater to fans of crispy, juicy chicken dishes. These are just some of the options available, with the festival promising a broad range of cuisines and styles.

Food Paradise will offer more than a quick festival meal

Food Paradise is expected to be one of the key new food destinations at this year’s Sziget. Rather than simply functioning as a conventional food court, the area is designed as a social and gastronomic hub where visitors can sit down, meet friends and take a proper break between concerts.

The day starts early, too. Between 9 AM and noon, a brunch party will feature breakfast dishes, coffee and DJ sets for early risers. From the afternoon onwards, the focus will shift towards the wider food offering and evening festival atmosphere.

Among the names expected at Food Paradise are 101 Bistro, specialising in modern Asian street food; Tuning Burger; Buja Disznó(k), famous for its schnitzel; Digó, serving Neapolitan-style pizza; Nemo Fish & Chips & Seafood; and á Table, offering pastries and French-inspired dishes.

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

Michelin-starred cuisine is also coming to Sziget

One of the festival’s most notable gastronomic additions this year will be found in the VIP area. Costes, one of Hungary’s best-known fine-dining names and associated with Michelin-starred cuisine, will be among the restaurants serving festival-goers.

The VIP food line-up will also include Buja Disznó(k), Digó and 101 Bistro, while TOKIO will bring a more refined take on modern Asian cuisine. It is an unusual combination: one moment you can be watching a major international act, and the next you can be eating food associated with some of Budapest’s leading restaurants.

Sustainability is also on the menu

Sziget is also placing greater emphasis on sustainability across its food operations. The festival will continue its composting programme, which was recognised with an international innovation award in 2019. This year, the system will be extended across all of the festival’s food courts.

Organic waste, as well as the biodegradable plates and cutlery used at the festival, will be collected separately and composted.

The organisers are also requiring participating food vendors to make at least three sustainability commitments. These can include offering vegetarian or vegan main courses, avoiding red meat, using organic ingredients, sourcing products from Hungarian producers or using sustainably sourced palm oil.

A new Green Hospitality Programme will also launch this year, with higher sustainability standards for participating vendors. The first businesses to receive the new certification include Hot by Sophie’s Delight, Vegan Island by Napfényes, Crunchy, Zing Burger & CO, Pasta Vibes and Mambo Pasta Bistro.

A farmers’ market is coming too

For those looking for something fresher after several days of burgers, pizza and lángos, Sziget will also feature its first Farmers’ Market. Local producers will offer fresh vegetables, fruit and other products, giving festival-goers another option beyond traditional festival food.

An Aldi store will also return to the festival, with a full shop built on site. One unusual feature is that visitors will be able to buy fresh meat for grilling and have it prepared for them at the festival. There will also be options for people with dietary restrictions, including gluten-free and/or lactose-free dishes, as well as vegan food.

Sziget food is no longer just about burgers and lángos

Festival food has changed considerably in recent years. What was once largely a choice between a burger, pizza or lángos has evolved into a much broader gastronomic experience.

At Sziget this year, visitors can start the day with brunch and coffee, grab Asian street food in the afternoon, enjoy a Neapolitan pizza before a headline show, or even opt for fine-dining-inspired dishes in the VIP area.

And for those who simply want to eat well without spending a fortune, the HUF 3,500 budget-food option offers a much-needed cheaper alternative. The full list of participating food vendors and further details are available on the official Sziget website.

World.title: Drugging fears emerge after multiple women fall ill during DJ show in Hungary
World.content:
Concerns have emerged over alleged drink spiking at the site of Budapest’s Sziget Festival after several festivalgoers reported that women suddenly became seriously unwell during Hungarian DJ and presenter Balázs Sebestyén’s Saturday night show.

One young man said his sister collapsed and became unresponsive after having a drink at one of the festival’s food and drink outlets. According to reports shared on social media, as many as 18 young women were treated at one medical point with similar symptoms.

The reports have not been independently confirmed as cases of drink spiking, and Hungarian police have reportedly not received an official complaint about such incidents at the festival.

Young woman reportedly collapsed after a drink

Norbert Galambos, who attended the event with his sister and a group of friends, described what happened in a widely shared Facebook post.

According to his account, his sister suddenly collapsed after drinking at a festival bar and stopped responding. When the family sought medical assistance, he said paramedics initially asked how much alcohol she had consumed and whether she had taken drugs.

Galambos stressed that his sister does not use recreational drugs and that she had simply gone to the festival with friends. He also criticised the way he says the pair were treated by medical staff, arguing that his sister was treated as though she had voluntarily taken drugs.

The Hungarian National Ambulance Service shared his post and said it takes the claims seriously and will investigate the circumstances. The service also emphasised that professional medical care should be accompanied by appropriate and empathetic communication with both patients and their concerned relatives.

Reports of more women becoming unwell

According to accounts shared by festivalgoers, the incident may not have been isolated. Witnesses claimed that a number of women experienced similar symptoms and sought medical assistance during the event. One account circulating online claimed that 18 young women were treated at a single medical point.

However, this figure has not been independently verified, and it remains unclear how many people may actually have been affected or what caused their symptoms. Another festivalgoer, a 39-year-old woman named Enikő, also described becoming suddenly ill during the DJ show.

She said she had asked someone to bring drinks from a VIP area because of the long queues at the festival bars. She claimed that shortly afterwards she became severely unwell and lost control of her movements. According to her account, her husband and another couple who happened to be nearby helped her until medical assistance arrived. She later said she was convinced that her symptoms were not simply the result of drinking alcohol.

What is GHB?

Some of the social media reports have suggested that GHB, sometimes known as “Gina”, may have been involved. However, there is currently no confirmed evidence establishing that GHB was responsible for the reported incidents.

GHB is a synthetic psychoactive substance that is colourless and odourless in liquid form. It can cause drowsiness, confusion and impaired consciousness, while larger amounts can result in unconsciousness and potentially life-threatening breathing problems.

Combining GHB with alcohol can be particularly dangerous because both substances can depress the central nervous system. The drug has also been associated with sexual assaults and robberies because a person under its influence may become extremely vulnerable and unable to protect themselves.

Importantly, the symptoms described by festivalgoers alone cannot establish what substance, if any, was involved. Medical assessment and toxicological testing would be needed to determine the cause.

GHB can disappear from the body quickly

According to Blikk, one difficulty in investigating suspected GHB exposure is the substance’s relatively short detection window.

GHB can generally only be detected in blood for a few hours after consumption and in urine for several more hours. This means that if someone suspects they have been drugged, seeking medical attention as soon as possible can be important. A hair test may potentially detect GHB exposure much later, but such testing is more specialised and costly.

No official police complaint reported so far

Despite the growing number of social media posts, there has so far been no confirmed report of an official police complaint concerning drink spiking at Sziget, according to the reports available. The claims therefore remain allegations at this stage.

The Hungarian National Ambulance Service is investigating the circumstances surrounding the treatment of the reported patients, while the exact number of people affected and the cause of their symptoms remain unclear.

Festivalgoers are nevertheless being urged to take sensible precautions, including keeping an eye on their drinks, staying with friends and seeking medical help immediately if they or someone in their group suddenly becomes confused, severely drowsy, unconscious or otherwise seriously unwell.

If you missed it: Transylvanian villagers attack ambulance after seeing TikTok rumours about kidnapping children

Sziget not aware of drugging incidents

Sziget also responded to the above reports. In their response to Daily News Hungary, they stated that medical services were provided during the event in cooperation with the National Ambulance Service. Of the more than 60,000 visitors, fewer than 100 required medical attention; of these, 20 cases were alcohol-related, and there were no drug-related incidents.

“We, too, were deeply outraged by the reports that appeared on social media, and we encourage anyone affected by such an incident to contact the police. For our part, we will do everything we can to assist the investigative authorities in their work,” they wrote.

They also noted that their catering units have been working with the same tried-and-true, reliable subcontractors for years, who serve the public safely and to a high standard.
