The Congress and the INDIA bloc have repeatedly demanded a statement from Amit Shah in Parliament and have staged protests both inside and outside the House over the issue.

On Monday, another Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi also demanded statement from Amit Shah in Parliament.

Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, however, has maintained that the Opposition cannot dictate which minister should come to Parliament and make a statement, saying the decision rests with the government.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 16 LIVE: Consumers do not need to pay any UPI charges, no MDR for small merchants: Finance Minister Sitharaman
World.content:
The Lok Sabha on Monday (August 10, 2026) passed The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026’, without discussion, amidst a heavy sloganeering by the Opposition MPs. Meanwhile, the Rajya Sabha passed The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026’, through a voice vote.

Both Houses saw couple of disruptions on Monday (August 10, 2026), Lok Sabha was adjourned minutes after the proceedings began at 11 a.m., amid protests from the Opposition demanding discussions on various issues. Rajya Sabha was also adjourned a few minutes later. Both Houses reconvened at 12 p.m.

Lok Sabha introduced four Bills amid protests- The Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026, the Minerals and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 and The National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Rajya Sabha briefly took up some business, but was adjourned minutes later.

Floor leaders of the Opposition parties held a meeting in the chamber of the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, to chalk out the strategy for the Floor of the House on Monday (August 10, 2026).

The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 is also expected to be taken up in the discussion of the Opposition leaders. The Lok Sabha is scheduled to take up the introduction of several key bills on Monday, including the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, and the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

World.title: Police recruit trainee accused of duping cadets in uniform fraud in Kerala’s Thiruvananthapuram
World.content:
The Peroorkada police here have registered a case against a police recruit trainee for allegedly defrauding his fellow cadets of over ₹7 lakh under the pretext of collecting funds for uniforms.

The accused, Sambhu R. Krishnan, attached to the Kerala Armed Police (KAP) Battalion-3, is accused of siphoning off the funds amounting to ₹7,18,320 to gamble on online betting games.

According to the official complaint lodged by Mujeeb Rahman, Officer Commanding of B Company at the Special Armed Police (SAP) Battalion in Peroorkada, the fraud took place between July 3 and July 13. During the period, the accused served as a member of a uniform committee formed to organise uniform materials and tailoring services for recruit trainees in KAP Battalions-3 and 5 that are stationed at the SAP facility.

Mr. Krishnan allegedly convinced trainees in the battalions to transfer uniform funds directly to his mobile number under the false assurance that he would deposit the payments with the SAP canteen for cloth materials and a society for stitching the uniforms.

Instead of settling the official bills for the uniform materials and tailoring, the accused allegedly diverted the entire collected sum into online betting games, the complaint alleges.

Internal inquiry

The issue came to light after an internal inquiry, leading the Officer Commanding to file a complaint at the Peroorkada police station on Sunday (August 9, 2026).

The police have booked Mr. Krishnan under Section 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, which deals with cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.

World.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russian city of Nizhnekamsk kills 13, authorities say
World.content:
A Ukrainian drone attack on Monday (August 10, 2026) on the Russian city of Nizhnekamsk killed 13 people, including a child, and wounded 48 others, authorities in the Tatarstan region said.

Also Read: Bad for both: On the Russia-Ukraine conflict

Officials didn't say what the drones targeted, but the city is an important oil refining hub, home to two refineries and a petrochemical plant. Ukraine has targeted Russian oil facilities with long-range drones almost daily in recent months. The barrage has caused fuel shortages in Russia, eaten into Russian refining capacity, and unsettled the Russian public.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says it is a campaign to force Russian President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table and stop his more than 4-year-old invasion.

Nizhnekamsk came under a “massive” drone attack targeting industrial and civilian facilities on Monday (August 10) morning, according to the press service of Tatarstan's head, Rustam Minnikhanov. No further details were immediately available.

Also Read: A brief history of the Russia-Ukraine war | Explained

Ukrainian officials made no immediate comment.

Nizhnekamsk is roughly 1,200 kilometers (750 miles) east of the Ukrainian border and has a population of about 240,000.

Ukraine's domestically developed long-range drones have flown increasing distances deep inside Russia, with some now reaching Siberia, around 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) from the border.

“We do deliver entirely justified responses, and every Russian strike will be met with our response. Russia's war will be felt more and more at their own home – in Russia,” Mr. Zelenskyy said late Sunday (August 9) on social media.

“The only reason this is continuing is Russia's unwillingness to end this war.” Russia has also regularly battered Ukraine from the air using missiles, powerful glide bombs and drones, hitting civilian areas and causing thousands of civilian casualties, according to the United Nations.

The World Health Organisation's European office said Monday (August 10) that one of its warehouses in the central Dnipro region of Ukraine had been struck twice in less than 24 hours.

The attacks destroyed emergency supplies worth an estimated $500,000 that were intended for front-line health facilities, it said in a statement.

No casualties were reported.

World.title: Collectorate staff’s death and doctor’s illness take a political turn in Kerala after Pinarayi Vijayan’s social media post
World.content:
The death of a senior clerk at the Kasaragod Collectorate and the illness of a senior paediatrician at Kannur Government Medical College have assumed a political dimension following Kerala Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan’s Facebook post linking the two incidents to alleged harassment of government employees.

While Mr. Vijayan criticised what he described as politically motivated transfers and intimidation of officials, the police investigation into the death of the Kasaragod employee, Ashalatha, has so far found no specific incident, person, or act of harassment cited in the woman’s dying declaration.

District Police Chief P. Nidhinraj said her dying declaration was recorded while she was in critical condition. She reportedly spoke about mental difficulties at home and at her workplace but did not name any person or identify any particular incident as the reason for taking the extreme step.

An FIR has been registered and statements are being collected from her co-workers and relatives. The police said she had recently been transferred within the Collectorate from a relatively hectic assignment to a comparatively lighter workload. Both her previous and new postings were within the same establishment.

The case has nevertheless become a political flashpoint after Mr. Vijayan alleged in his Facebook post that “wrong decisions” by the government and organisations supporting it were “creating a frightening situation in which even government employees were losing their lives.”

Mr. Vijayan linked Ashalatha’s death to mental stress allegedly caused by the compulsory section transfers. He also referred the alleged intimidation faced by the senior paediatrician.

The doctor, a senior professor who has been in government service since 1996, reportedly developed severe chest pain after members of a Congress-affiliated employees association confronted her over the transfer and joining of a Grade 4 employee, according to the family members.

The association members confronted her at her outpatient workstation while she was attending patients and pressured her to sign a transfer-related document, though she reportedly had no administrative authority over the transfer, the family members alleged.

The Head of Department had already informed the employees that the transfer could not be implemented immediately as university examinations were underway and it could be considered after the examinations concluded five days later.

She subsequently developed severe chest pain. An ECG showed changes and an echocardiogram indicated acute stress-induced cardiomyopathy, they said.

She was admitted to the ICU on Saturday and remained under cardiac care. Though her condition improved, doctors indicated that recovery could take two or four weeks. The family is, however, yet to decide on a formal complaint.

Vijayan slams Satheesan

In his post, Mr. Vijayan accused government-backed organisations of threatening employees who refused allegedly unlawful transfer orders and “those raising their voices for service rights.” He alleged that “politically motivated mass transfers” had paralysed the civil service and criticised Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan.

He also defended the previous LDF government’s record on employee benefits, citing the 12th Pay Revision Commission, and accused the UDF of delaying pay revision, dearness allowance arrears, earned leave surrender benefits, and assured pension.

He also alleged that 2,800 digital survey workers were removed without eligible salary arrears, and referred to earlier mass dismissals involving Kudumbashree, KSRTC and PSC-appointed teachers.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget 2026: TVK-led government’s first financial blueprint
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, on Wednesday (August 5, 2026), presented the Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay-led government’s maiden Budget in the State Assembly. While some of the schemes based on the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK) poll promises found a place in the Budget, several prominent assurances, such as the ₹2,500 monthly assistance for eligible women heads of families, six free LPG cylinders a year for every family, and free travel for women on all government bus services, did not figure in it.

Some of the major announcements included the provision of an eight-gram (one-sovereign) gold coin and a silk saree as ‘Annan Seer’ to eligible brides; upgradation of basic infrastructure in urban and rural Adi Dravidar habitations; a law college in Madurai; and specialised homes for senior citizens and transgender people.

During his two-and-a-half hour presentation, Mr. Wilson said the State’s outstanding debt is estimated at ₹10.98 lakh crore in the Revised Budget Estimates (RBE) for 2026-27. The outstanding debt-to-GSDP ratio is estimated at 27.01%, and the government plans to borrow ₹1,73,445 crore and repay ₹51,971 crore during the current financial year, he said.

World.title: At least seven dead, including two children, as car swept away in Madhya Pradesh flash flood
World.content:
Seven people, including two children and a woman, died on Monday (August 10, 2026) in Madhya Pradesh’s Rajgarh district when a van was washed away amid flood-like situation by heavy rains, police said.

According to the police, the incident took place in the early hours on Monday (August 10, 2026) when the van was trying to cross a small bridge that had water flowing over, near a bypass in Padana village under Sarangpur tehsil.

#WATCH | Rajgarh, Madhya Pradesh: Eight people, including children, died and two were rescued after an Omni van carrying 11 passengers was swept away by strong currents in the swollen Jhiri stream near Padana in Rajgarh district.



Local administration and rescue teams launched… pic.twitter.com/MJuRr0FlI0 — ANI (@ANI) August 10, 2026

There were 11 passengers, including women and children, in the car, and two people have been rescued alive while rescue efforts are on for two missing persons, Sarangpur Sub-Divisional Officer, Police (SDOP) Arvind Singh told The Hindu.

The victims are residents of Dewas district.

A purported video from the scene shows two locals rescuing one of the passengers using a rope amid neck-deep water levels.

Mr. Singh said that about 45 villages across the tehsil are facing flood like situation and urban areas are dealing with severe water-logging, prompting rescue efforts across in areas that witnessed sudden rise in water levels.

“The area has received cloudburst-like rain since around midnight [Sunday] and the situation turned bad very quickly in several villages. The administration and the police have been running rescue efforts since early morning to bring people to safety,” he said.

“In the morning, we received information from Padana about the van. The rescue teams reached the spot soon and seven bodies have been recovered so far. The search operation is going on to find the two missing persons,” Mr. Singh said.

“Locals are saying that the driver showed negligence and moved ahead to cross the bridge even after people warned him about high-flowing water,” the officer added.

World.title: Sahasra Ghatabhishekam performed at Srisailam temple
World.content:
As part of the ongoing ritual propitiating gods for timely and adequate rains, Sahasra Ghatabhishekam of Lord Mallikarjuna Swamy was performed at the Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple, Srisailam on Monday (August 10, 2026).

Monday was the fourth day of the ongoing five-day Varuna Yagam Sahitha Sahasra Ghatabhishekam being organised by the Devasthanam at the temple. The fourth day Ghatabhishekam commenced with special rituals in which Endowments department Additional Commissioner S S Chandrashekhara Azad, Trust Board Chairman Pothugunta Ramesh Naidu, Executive Officer M Srinivasa Rao and others participated.

As part of the proceedings, various rituals were performed by the temple priests. Abhishekam was performed using the sacred waters of the Krishna River and the holy waters of the Mallikagunda located within the temple premises. Some 36 ritviks from various regions are participating in this program, alongside the temple priests and Vedic scholars.

The priests performed rituals for the sacred Krishna River at Pathalaganga and brought the holy river water back in ceremonial vessels (Kalashams). The priests carried the water vessels on their heads amid traditional music and the chanting of Vedic mantras, they proceeded to the Nandi temple. They performed Abhishekam and other rituals for Lord Nandishwara, followed by the village deity Goddess Ankalamma and the guardian deity Lord Veerabhadraswamy.

Later, the priests carried the water vessels to the main temple and after performing rituals at the Akka Mahadevi Alankara Mandapam within the temple complex, the Sahasra Ghatabhishekam (ritual bathing with a thousand pots of water) of Lord Mallikarjuna, amid ritual chanting of Rudra mantras, was performed.

Upon the completion of the Ghatabhishekam, the Mahanivedana, Neerajana and Mantrapushpa ceremonies are scheduled to conducted. For the occasion, a temporary wall, three feet in height, was erected across the entrance to the Lord’s sanctum sanctorum to ensure that the deity remains immersed in the Ghatabhishekam waters throughout the day.

U.P. CM Yogi showers flowers on Kanwariyas, describes Kanwar Yatra as unparalleled example of devotion, unity

Kanwar Yatra is an annual pilgrimage where devotees of Lord Shiva collect holy water from the Ganges River from places like Haridawar, Gangotri, Gaumukh, or Sultanganj and take it to their local temples, often walking barefoot for long distances.
